------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv26
Cast Protect and Shell on yourself before going further. Take care to renew
your protective buffs when they wear off. Checking status affinities and
considering our options, you can put a number of stuff on it - Blind, Sleep,
and Berserk.
Sleep will again be your strongest ally in the battle, and make sure you wear
Sash and Tourmaline Ring acc to counter Slow and Poison statuses from Mousse.
If you kept Flame Staffs from Dustia chaining before, now's the time to equip
them.
When Mousse drops from ceiling, spread your chrs out, max out chrs' MAG and
begin casting Sleep until it connects and make sure to put on correct acc in
case Mousse casts Slowga or Toxify. Or to simplify the matter, equip Niho and
toss Alarm Clock on the mark for insta-sleep. Works 100% of the time, no hassle
required. Now that Mousse is asleep, switch to casting Fire on the blob - since
it's sleeping and weak to fire, damage done will be tripled (if Flame Staff is
equipped, even 4,5x as much damage).
Sleep will wear off soon, so make sure you're prepared for applying it again.
Do not allow Mousse to gain sanity after critical stage, as it will spam
Waterga until your chrs are gone. Reduce Mousse's HP all the way to zero and
you win.
An alternate way to winning this fight is putting Mousse on Berserk, in which
case it won't be using any skills except rephys. Sure it can attack way faster
and stronger, but it doesn't ignore EVA and putting Blind on it is another
superior tactic.

reward for completing the hunt you get 2800 gil, Yoichi Bow.

------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv27
This will be one tough nut to crack. Looking at status affinities it is only
susceptible to Slow and Blind, but you have a small chance that boss starts
with Reflect on, so that is out of window. You can keep coming back and check
on it if Reflect is on in subsequent battle. And boy do I hate this guy's PA.
First off, thanks to Null VIT it will always inflict status on you, unless you
are wearing accessory which makes you immune. And you can't hope to reflect
spells back as boss has Piercing Magic. You can null Silence and Blind, but for
Sleep you will have to rely on Alarm Clock for now. Even though boss has Null
VIT, you can cast Shell on yourself to have 50% less chance for boss to hit you
with status effects.
Coming into battle with Protect on will be first smart decision, as is
equipping Argyle Armlet to be immune to Blind - be sure to switch in Rose
Corsage for each time boss tries to Silence you. As battle starts, pay
attention to meter on right side of your screen - if you get pushed all the way
against the wall, you'll have an instant game over. Boss will wail on you with
status magic the most before it begins to ready Telega after losing only 20%
HP. At this time one of your chrs will be sent into X-Zone, and there is no way
of countering this status, except by traveling into another screen. If somebody
gets targeted for Telega, have that chr perform a Quickie. When chr is lost to
X-Zone, swap in another chr from reserve.
Boss will rarely use its regular attack, and Doom isn't of importance either,
because battle will end before Doom counter reaches zero. Since you have access
to Berserk, cast it on two of your attackers and let them get to work on
lowering Wall's HP to dangerous levels (make sure they can null Blind). Or
perform an oilslick by using Oil on boss and then blasting it with Fire. Its
attack increases when in critical, but as pointed out earlier, it much rather
uses status magic. Remember, if things go grim, you can flee the battle and
retry later when you regroup or have better equipment.
There is another way to quickly defeat it by employing same tactic that you
used against Garuda. Reflect all your chrs and then cast either Dark or Aero
(latter is little bit stronger) on yourself to have your magic reflected four
times! Repeat as needed until boss falls and becomes dust. Literally.
-------------------- CONGRATULATIONS! YOU ARE VICTORIOUS! ---------------------

- After the battle you will see 'Azure Jewel' in the wall behind the now
deceased boss. Nothing can be done about the jewel just yet, instead travel W.

------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv27
About two times easier than earlier Demon Wall. This one has less HP, longer
hallway for advancing, and doesn't begin with Reflect crap on. Also, you can
examine burning pillars on side of hallway and choose to fiddle with them. If
flame goes out, boss will be temporarily stopped, but if flame turns blue, boss
gains a bit of advance speed boost. All in all, I didn't touch them at all.
Also, unless you pack correct accessory, boss will always succeed to putting
you under bad status. Like before, you can escape from this Wall as well into
previous hall.
Begin by casting Protect and equipping Argyle Armlet to null Blind. Even though
boss has Null VIT, you can cast Shell on yourself to have 50% less chance for
boss to hit you with status effects. Take care to renew your protective buffs
when they wear off. Now the next option is to Reflect yourself - this will
bounce back everything except Telega, Doom and Annul, but if you do that, you
will need to cure with items.
If Reflect doesn't suit you, remain healthy with Cura and use Alarm Clock to
wake up sleepy chrs. Put boss under Slow and Blind to have it taste some of its
own medicine. Expect to have one chr baleeted into X-Zone, so you could be
better off chucking a Quickie with that chr. When chr is lost to X-Zone, swap
in another chr from reserve. Doom won't bother you, and in case of being
Annul-ed, simply use Charge to recover some MP. Once boss loses half HP, it
will fortify itself with Chain Magick, allowing it to cast magics instantly -
maybe Reflect on yourself sounds like a good idea now? Additional quick way to
dispose of boss is Oil-ing it and then... Fire it up! There is another way to
quickly defeat it by employing same tactic that you used against Garuda.
Reflect all your chrs and then cast either Dark or Aero (latter is little bit
stronger) on yourself to have your magic reflected four times! Repeat as needed
until boss falls and becomes dust. Literally.

- The sword I mentioned before is Demonsbane. I recommend going outside and
save your game at GCR, as getting the sword may take a few tries. Once ready,
take either of the paths you just created and travel W.

[The Tomb of Raithwall / Hall of the Sentinel]

- Travel W.

[The Tomb of Raithwall / Royal Passage]

- Path now leads N and S, and it matters not which you take. You will travel
down lots of stairs and eventually some Tallows will start dropping in on you.
Here look for the chest - it may contain Demonsbane (or Holy Mote, or some gil,
or chest may not even be there). If you see no chest, reload the game. I
suggest you go for two Demonsbane swords, which is what I got. Once you have
two swords, travel to [Hall of the Sentinel], that is the regular 'way' into
tomb.

[The Tomb of Raithwall / Royal Passage]

- Go downstairs and open the Urn for map of [The Tomb of Raithwall]. Blue 'Way
Stone' will return you to [Hall of the Destroyer]. From this platform descend N
stairs and press on towards N room. Once you reach two paths branching E, take
lower one. At the end enter N door to reach N room, which is first of your
objectives.

[The Tomb of Raithwall / Northfall Passage]

- Move thru rooms (while doing so, I suggest to Poach Lesser Chimeras until you
get Main Gauche - this exceptional dagger offers +34 Evade) until you find one
with 'Northfall Pedestal' containing red switch. Press the switch (will lower
the Mystic Altar by a half), kill enemies that appear and then examine red 'Way
Stone' behind you to be teleported back to the platform.

[The Tomb of Raithwall / Royal Passage]

- From this platform descend S stairs and press on towards S room. Once you
reach two paths branching E, take lower one. At the end enter S door to reach S
room, which is second of your objectives.

[The Tomb of Raithwall / Southfall Passage]

- Move thru rooms until you find one with 'Southfall Pedestal' containing green
switch. Press the switch (will totally lower the Mystic Altar), kill enemies
that appear and then examine green 'Way Stone' behind you to be teleported back
to the platform. Use the blue 'Way Stone' to transfer behind 1st Demon Wall,
and then the yellow 'Way Stone' to get to [Valley of the Dead]. Save your game
at GCR (you also need to buy few Handkerchiefs), then return to the
three-teleport-platform and use either red or green teleport (I used red) to
return to the place where you pushed the appropriate switch.

- If following red trail, you will see a hole in the wall in place where Mystic
Altar used to be (W from 'Way Stone'). Follow this new path and then take S
door.

[The Tomb of Raithwall / Cloister of Flame]

- Proceed to center of the room and... heeey, what's that?

------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv28
Okie dokie, your first esper fight! It is indeed trial by fire, and fire you
shall have - plenty of it, in fact. Esper commands fire element, and as such
you should avoid using it, but you are perfectly welcome to blast Belias with
Water spell. Checking status affinities we see that you can only put Slow and
Sap on it - better something than nothing; Belias also doesn't combo and is
quite slow in getting attacks off. Shell should be your primary means of
defense, followed by Protect and that is it. Take care to renew your protective
buffs when they wear off.
Belias will alternate between swiping at you and slinging Fire every now and
then until you reduce its HP far enough for it to use Saber. At this point its
physical damage output doubles, at the expense of Belias taking as much damage
as it dishes - effect will eventually wear off. Once esper loses half HP, it
will greet you with a healthy dose of Firaja, followed by Greater Barrier (I
hate this move) for the known combo of Protect, Shell and Damage Resist. If
anyone gets affected by Oil from Firaja, use Handkerchiefs immediately! Don't
let your chrs succumb to something as crappy as Fire spell.
Also from losing-half-HP point onward boss turns into formiddable opponent, as
its attacks become stronger. Whoever your tank is, having that chr equipped
with shield is useless, as Belias now ignores EVA and will always hit you, so
put a stronger weapon into chr's hands.
Once Belias' HP dwindles into critical range, it can now cast magic instantly,
and you don't really want to see another Firaja (unless you're with Shell all
the way to the highway). It is only a matter of few well placed attacks at this
point until Belias bites the bullet. Here, have some cheese with that.
-------------------- CONGRATULATIONS! YOU ARE VICTORIOUS! ---------------------

------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv28
The boss' sidekicks should kiss the floor immediately, which shall be partially
accomplished by Fran's Berserk rage - OMG, it's the bunny on the warpath!
Checking boss status affinities he can be put under number of crap - Slow,
Sleep, Sap and Berserk. You definitely don't want the latter on him, so refrain
from tacking it on - but you certainly want Slow and Sleep on. Be careful
though - as soon as magic casting is detected, boss will Reflect himself, so
you should chuck Sleep and Slow on at the same time and hope that magics hit
boss before he is done with Reflect. Or you can cast Reflect on yourself and
bounce spells to him in that way (heal with items in this case).
Cast Protect and Regen on yourself and take care to renew your protective buffs
when they wear off. His Shell and Haste will eventually wear off on their own,
and he has no means of regaining them, so you're cool in this field. Keep
poking his HP down until he loses half HP - at that time he will always hit you
and his damage output increases. When he loses 60% of HP, say hello to Enrage
and even madder comboing rate following afterwards. Keep your cool and remember
that you have Cura to keep you healthy and Raise to revive fallen comrades. In
about few more chucks of sword swinging traitor starts to push up the daisies.

Mosphoran Highwaste

Mighty mountain range standing between Dalmasca and Nabradia. Well-known for
its odd rock formations: overhangs forming roofs over the mountain paths, and
lone spires of rock jutting toward the sky.
```

```
In a col between the peaks is a flat area where spring water bubbles from the
ground, creating an ideal resting place for weary travelers. The shrines
standing in the clearing were built during the Galtean Alliance, the names of
the gods they enshrine long since lost to the ken of Man.

- Last area can only be accessed after your party reaches Phon Coast. More
details are further down in the walkthru.

- From [Southern Skirts] travel W to [Summit Path] (while you're in this area,
make sure to track down and kill some Wary Wolf rare foes in order to obtain
Power Armlet, an acc which nulls Stop), and then take SE exit to [Babbling\
Vale].

- Here you will find GCR for the area and a merchant, which you should
definitely check out, for he sells Golden Amulet (doubles LP earned), Thief's
Cuffs (improves stealing rate and allows to steal multiple items in one go),
Ruby Ring (adds Reflect when worn), Nishijin Belt (null Sleep), Gillie Boots
(null Oil), and Quasimodo Boots (null Sap). After shopping is done, go around
Highwaste and kill stuff for EXP, LP and loot. Always have Golden Amulet
equipped on your reserve chrs so they gain LP while your main chrs defeat foes.
I gathered enough LP so that my main party learned third and final Quickies.

- There's lots of shrines around this section - they will come into play much
later in the game, helping you claim an esper and to get access to other parts
of the area you cannot yet reach.

- When you think you had enough, use GCR to warp to Estersand.

===============================================================================
DALMASCA ESTERSAND area
===============================================================================

CACTUAR QUEST

- Go to village's river bank and talk to Tchigri. His dad is missing, so they
ask you to tag along for some protective mission - agree to help and you will
travel to [North Bank Village]. Here talk to Ruksel and you return to [South\
Bank Village]. Talk to Dantro's wife and she will mention about boiling the
flower you gave her before and dropping it behind her house. Go there and
examine 'Dran?' spot for a new cactus to pop out. Return to Tchigri and travel
to [North Bank Village] again. Get close to biggest cactus and voila. You will
get 1000 gil and Wyrmfire Shot. The ferry is running again, so you can now
freely cross between the two villages.

- In [North Bank Village] you will find a moogle from Cartographers', who sells
a map of [Mosphoran Highwaste] for 2400 gil.

- Depart for [Broken Sands] area of Estersand. When you get there, look around
for white-flowered trees around middle of the area - check the 'Mysterious
Glint' and you will obtain Valeblossom Dew. There are three total to be found,
and MAKE SURE YOU DO NOT SELL THEM. If you're goofy enough to sell them anyway,
return to [Broken Sands] and look for Valeblossom Dew again - you need to give
at least one to Dantro's wife in order to proceed to next step. Also look for
point of interest called 'Weathered Rock' - when it is struck, it will collapse
and create a small shortcut in the area.

DESERT PATIENT QUEST

- You will not be able to give her any items needed for this quest until
Cactuar quest is completed.

- Go to Dantro's wife in [South Bank Village] and give her Valeblossom Dew. If
you still have Great Serpentskin in your inventory, she will take that as well
(you must confirm to give her the Great Serpentskin); and like I said several
times before - you don't need to have Great Serpentskin). Then leave the
village and return immediately. Talk to Dantro's wife once more and she directs
you behind her hut.

- Again, you do not need Great Serpentskin at all! If you want, you can decide
to never do Nidhogg hunt, and you'll still nab Barheim Key.

- There is a moogle (*he* has been sick?) behind her hut - talk to him, and you
get Barheim Key KI. Additional reward of Balance Mote, OR Magick Gloves, OR
Golden Amulet will be yours as well, depending on how many items you have
brought to Dantro's wife for healing process. Barheim Key opens another route
to [Barheim Passage] from [Murmuring Defile].

- If you will poke into Barheim's hidden depths, know that you can obtain two
great weapons - Deathbringer (steal from rare enemy Ithuno which appears in
[Special Op Sector 5]), and Zeus Mace (drop from rare enemy Minibug which
appears in [East-West Bypass]).

- Use GCR to warp to Rabanastre.

------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv29
Orthros will be the first to feel the full power of Niho. Cast Protect, Shell
and Regen on yourself before going further. Take care to renew your protective
buffs when they wear off. Checking status affinities and considering our
options, you can put some stuff on it - Sleep, Disease and Blind.
When you enter battle, have the chr with Niho toss Alarm Clock on Orthros to
put it to sleep. Like with Mousse, don Flame Staffs and begin chucking Fire on
Orthros - fire weakness + Sleep + Flame Staff will give you 4,5x bigger damage.
When it comes to items, Orthros is the only consistent source of Slime Oil - if
you want to unlock all bazaar packages, you'll need to steal couple of Slime
Oils from it.
Orthros has a ton of status attacks, so keeping it asleep is your primary role.
You will no longer have to bonk yourself on the head if status attacks miss
since Niho will inflict statuses for you with 100% chance.
Should you consider fighting Orthros without Niho, have appropriate acc
equipped when it casts its status magic and make sure your chrs are spread out
so that only one is hit at a time. Applying Reflect is a wise idea as well, as
most of mark's spells will be bounced back to it.
-------------------- CONGRATULATIONS! YOU ARE VICTORIOUS! ---------------------

- After battle you receive Stolen Articles KI. Report Orthros hunt back to
Contrite Thief and you will receive: 3800 gil, Horakhty's Flame, Unpurified
Ether.

------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv30
Cast Protect, Shell and Regen on yourself before going further. Take care to
renew your protective buffs when they wear off. Checking status affinities and
considering our options, you can put a number of stuff on it - Disease,
Reverse, Slow, Immobilize, Silence, Oil and Sap.
Equip Flame Shields, Miters, best armor you have, and set your gambits to
remove Oil with Handkerchiefs. Then focus on three Bombs prowling around King
and remove them from battlefield.
Once they are gone, turn on King and have it taste some Miter justice - be
advised that King has Return Damage active. Use NihoRem to inflict above
mentioned statuses and you're set. If you don't have Niho yet, inflict at least
Silence, Sap and Immobilize.
Silence prevents King from using Fira and Cry for Help, and that means you'll
be free from reinforcements. Disease will disable boss' Renew and Chain Magick
skills - if boss can't heal, it'll fall quickly.
In case inflicting Disease isn't an option, stay on alert for boss' Renew which
it can use often (for sure when boss enters critical HP - but one time only).
Keep hacking away and you will win in no time. You may have to resort to
Quickies to help you nail the boss in case it keeps healing itself. If things
go grim, you can run away from this battle.
-------------------- CONGRATULATIONS! YOU ARE VICTORIOUS! ---------------------

- With King Bomb history, your way is wide open. Return to [Quietened Trace] to
save your game, then from [Grand Bower] go into [Corridor of Ages], and then
take SW exit into Nabudis.

Necrohol of Nabudis

Palace once home to the royal family Nabradia. Called the Verdpale Palace, it
once stood proudly in the middle of a lake.
Now it stands in ruin, destroyed in the attack on Nabudis two years ago. Though
the ghost of the building remains in the crumbling walls, it is wholly gutted
and lies half-submerged in murk.
Now Mist flows freely through its abandoned halls, and its glorious memory is
profaned by a menagerie of vile creatures.

ASHE'S POSTCARD COLLECTION No.23 =-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-

- Again, to gain access here - King Bomb in Salikawood must be defeated.

[Necrohol of Nabudis / Hall of Effulgent Light]

- The only reason we are here at this moment is to collect Zodiac Spear. Be
advised that this is very dangerous trek and you may get KOed often, but the
ultimate prize is well worth the effort. Baknamy is a very annoying enemy and
if at all possible, try to lure single enemy away from the packs. Or equip Niho
and toss Phoenix Down or Remedy on every enemy you find - that way you'll
render them quite harmless. Anyway, from the entrance go W a bit, and then go a
bit N, then W again to reach a small room with pillar in middle. From the room
go W again to another pillar-in-middle room. Now go S and locate the stairs to
[Cloister of Distant Song].

- There is a secret Baknamy Merchant hidden in Necrohol. You can find it in
[Necrohol of Nabudis / Hall of Effulgent Light]. Make your way to NW corner and
examine the lonely room up there. You will notice a passage leading into
another room (which is not shown on the map) with Pandora. Kill it if you want
(may drop Aegis Shield) and then examine corners of this hidden room until
"???" pops up. Press Action and merchant will appear. At this moment it was
only selling Ethers.

[Necrohol of Nabudis / Cloister of Distant Song]

- When you exit the stairway, go E past pillar-in-middle room, then N. You get
to deal with Elvorets now. At intersection turn E, and then N again. You should
see two Babils now, but we won't fight them. Turn gambits off, and run N past
the Babils, then turn E and run upstairs to next area.

[Necrohol of Nabudis / Cloister of the Highborn]

- Kill some Elvorets, then take E turn. Keep walking until you see two Babils
guarding a passage. Ignore them and go E, then turn N. You will see a small
room on the W and inside 16 treasures. If somehow you have come to possess
Diamond Armlet already, DO NOT HAVE IT EQUIPPED! Pop open all treasure and one
will contain Zodiac Spear, if you have followed my advice and didn't open the
treasures I told you to stay away from. If you have, tough luck, but not all is
lost, as the weapon can be gotten in another way. Now return the way you came.

[Necrohol of Nabudis / Cloister of Distant Song]

- Area should be fairly free of enemies, except maybe some Elvorets or Baknamys
spawning back. If you see Dark Elemental, do not cast any magic near it. If it
comes after you, whip on Reflect and run for the stairs.

[Necrohol of Nabudis / Hall of Effulgent Light]

- Enemies have spawned back, so you will have to kill them (try luring single
enemy away from the pack). When you have just but a final stretch to go, run
for the exit back to Salikawood.

------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv32
Before you come to battle, check to see that you have "Foe: undead" gambit, as
it will be of vital importance. Also needed will be some ranged weapons cos
Adra is a flying foe. Additional preps are done in form of casting Protect,
Shell, Bubble and Faith on your chrs. Having Power Armlet (drop from Wary Wolf)
will prevent Stop status from Thundaja.
Adra can be meddled with by putting Slow and Blind on it. In addition to head
honcho you will need to take care of Shambling Corpse foes that will keep
periodically appearing to offer support to Adra. Unfortunately Corpse is immune
to getting KOed with Phoenix Down, and we'll take care of it with combination
of Niho and Chronos Tear (you can buy them at [Mosphoran Highwaste / Babbling\
Vale]).
Before tacking on the hero-way of battle, let me tell you about cheese-way
first. As soon as Adra's intro is done, turn around and return the way you came
(in my case into [Hourglass Basin]) ignoring any Shambling Corpse foes that may
have spawned. When you've escaped from Adra's area, heal up your wounds, turn
around again and enter Adra's area once more. Esper boss music begins playing
immediately, but Adra is nowhere to be found - it is merrily waiting somewhere
in the area until you come close enough.
Slowly progress towards Adra's location, sistematically cleaning out undead
foes that will keep appearing. Expect to eradicate 15~16 enemies before coming
into Adra's reach. When it finally spots you, allow it to come to your location
and engage in battle. Now returning to hero-way of battle...
When battle begins, arrange two chrs' gambits to attack undead foes as they
appear and use third chr to attack Adra itself. You can take care of sidekicks
by casting Disable on them, or equipping Niho and tossing Chronos Tear to
inflict Stop. While Corpses can't do anything, smite them down and when they're
gone, have all chrs join forces against Adra. If you so desire, you can use
Niho in combination with Ethers to drain its MP but it'll eventually gain
enough MP back to shoot occassional Thundara your way. Adra also can't ignore
EVA, so a good shield will go a long way.
During first half of battle Adra will be taking as much damage as it dishes, in
addition to pelting you with Bleed and Thundara (keeping chrs apart is a good
idea to minimize the damage). Cura will prove more than enough to take care of
your healing needs. After losing 20% HP Adra begins using Flash Arc, a more
powerful version of thunder spell - it only hits one chr, though. Not much will
be changing until you enter second half of the battle.
First you'll be greeted with Thundaja which has a chance to inflict Stop (make
sure you're under Shell to halve that chance), and then Adra shields itself
with Perfect Defense (it'll wear off as soon as next Flash Arc is used). While
the boss is impervious to damage, heal yourself or recover MP or reapply buffs.
Once Perfect Defense is history, you'll be treated to Thundara spamathon mixed
with Flash Arc and Thundaja - keeping Shell on is of utmost importance.
Take care to have Adra under Slow, destroy Corpse foes as they pop up or just
have them under Stop check and heal often from constant thunder barrages. Soon
enough Adra kicks the bucket and you gain another ally.
-------------------- CONGRATULATIONS! YOU ARE VICTORIOUS! ---------------------

- Congrats, you now have the ability to summon Adrammelech. From [Arthroza\
Quicksands] go N to [The Balamka Fault]. Here pop open the Urn for map of
[Zertinan Caverns]. From [The Balamka Fault] go W to [Drybeam Cavern], then
into upper portion of [The Balamka Fault] again. Take lower of E exits to
[Sandfalls] and knock down 'Boulder'. Now follow the path and knock down
another 'Boulder', and one more 'Boulder' to clear the path. Now return to SCR
to save your game. If you were to take S-most exit from Zertinan, you will
reach Ozmone Plain, but that would mean skipping on some marks. So be a good
adventurer and return to Rabanastre.

- By the way, if you make way to [Zertinan Caverns / Sandfalls], you'll find
Grenade foes here. Keep up the stealing until you nab some Opal Rings, which
allow you to pierce thru target's Reflect (very useful strategy for some marks
and bosses).

- Once we take down remaining three marks, we shall go and claim another two
espers, so just hang on tight for now.

- Take S exit from Rabanastre to enter Giza Plains.

-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-= ASHE'S POSTCARD COLLECTION No.25
Giza Plains - the Rains

A vast savannah spreading to the south of the Royal City or Rabanastre, the
environs of which vary drastically between dry and rainy seasons.
Large dark crystals lie scattered here and there across the savannah. During
the Dry, they absorb the sun's radiance and glow with an auric brilliance. A
village of nomadic herders is located near the middle of the grasslands. During
the Rains, the villagers relocate to the mountains. While they reside in the
grasslands, the menfolk rarely return from their herding, leaving the women and
children to their own devices in the village.
These nomads know the art of capturing the energy of the dark crystals in
chunks of magicite, called sunstone, which they then bring to market to sell.
The animals by which the make their living are primarily of cockatrice stock.

------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv33
Cast Protect, Shell, Regen and Bubble on yourself before going further. Take
care to renew your protective buffs when they wear off. Checking status
affinities and considering our options, you can put a number of stuff on it -
Disease, Reverse, Slow, Immobilize, Silence and Blind.
Mark begins the battle with Shell and Bravery on, and its first move will be
Angelsong. Have Nishijin Belt on to prevent Sleep from rephy and that about
covers it. Toss NihoRem to inflict statuses mentioned above (except Reverse)
and the battle is all but won - it's asleep, in case it wakes up it can't heal
itself, slower attacking speed and rooted to the ground.
Croak is weak to fire, so have chrs don Flame Staffs and start poking the mark
with Fire spells until it falls defeated.
Croak provides a challenge otherwise - once it loses 60% HP, it'll use Growing
Threat (skill which doubles user's lv) and at critical HP it uses Aqua Bubbles
for serious damage. Avoid the danger of having all chrs hit by spreading them
out. If Niho isn't available, you'll want to keep casting Sleep, Slow and Blind
to cripple its fighting capabilities. Make sure you don't wander too far from
the mark or else it'll heal itself to full by using Renew skill.
-------------------- CONGRATULATIONS! YOU ARE VICTORIOUS! ---------------------

- After the battle you receive Ring of the Toad KI. Return to Sadeen and he
will award you with: 1200 gil, Serpent Rod, Teleport Stone. Sadeen will implore
you to take the ring you got to his beloved. This person is the village elder,
and you can give the ring to her during the Dry. There is still more - when the
ring is returned to the owner, and when it's next Rains season, you can go see
Sadeen again and talk to him for conclusion of his story.

- Also stop by [Crystal Glade] and speak with Nanau there about Gil Snapper
mark. You will receive Silent Urn KI, while location of Gil Snapper is in
[Tracks of the Beast].

- Cut down all six 'Withered Trees' and head to [Tracks of the Beast]. The
weather MUST BE heavy rain with lightning strikes - if it is, Bansat will show
up and inform you of Gil Snapper being in the area, but only one time. And if
it isn't, simply zone between two screens until desired weather comes. Engage
Gil Snapper!

------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv33
Before battle you may want to rid the area of turtles prowling around. Cast
Protect, Shell, Regen and Bubble on yourself before going further. Take care to
renew your protective buffs when they wear off. Checking status affinities and
considering our options, you can put a number of stuff on it - Disease, Slow,
Immobilize, Silence and Blind.
Battle begins and first business is to toss NihoRem - this will Silence the
mark, thus eliminating its magic skills, and Slow and Blind it as well
(otherwise apply statuses with magic spells), then spread your chrs around
Snapper and keep them close. Don't retreat too far or Snapper will Purify
itself of all bad statuses you put on it. Damage-wise Cura will keep you
healthy (note that you take damage for each strike you make at Snapper), and
have Argyle Armlet to null Blind from Flash skill. Everything you'll be getting
poked with is thus Flatten and rephy. Place your chrs just so far away that
Snapper won't use Purify and at same time isn't able to reach you with rephys
or Flatten.
Bansat will keep you up to date with Shell and Protect. Snapper is weak to
thunder element, so mix it in your attack repertoire every now and then. It
gains Damage Resist when it loses half HP.
Once Snapper enters critical range, it chills the battle with Blizzaga and then
spams Blizzara until its defeated... only since you keep it under Silence, no
such attacks occur - instead you're pelted with physicals.

Wide region of plains in Bancour, bordering Dalmasca. Mostly tall grasses,

decaying airshipwrecks punctuating the plains are monuments to the carnage once
wrought there.

-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-= ASHE'S POSTCARD COLLECTION No.27
Jahara

A garif village in Bancour. Here, a chieftain elder watches over the old ways,
and so administers the tribe. Though many other villages dot the area, there is
little direct communication between them.
The garif have worshipped magicite since ancient times, and tribal legends tend
much wisdom concerning the Stones. When the time is right, the elders teach
these lessons to the youth of the village, and, on rare occassions, to visitors
from other lands.
Abhorring machinery and iron, much of the garif material culture is based on
wood and stone and other unmanufacted things. Their houses made of grass and
strips of leather allow a breeze to pass through, and are uniquely suited to
the hot, arid climate.
On the hill overlooking the village is a meeting lodge, warmed always by a
bonfire. Near the lodge are the elders' huts, and below the hill is a clearing
ringed by a healer's hut, and the tents of craftsmen, as well as a place to
take care of a livestock, called "nanna" in the garif tongue.
Dalmasca has for many years honored the ways of the garif, and so kept up
peaceful trade and relations with this isolated people.

------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv33
Cast Protect, Shell, Regen, Bubble and Faith on yourself before going further.
Take care to renew your protective buffs when they wear off. Checking status
affinities and considering our options, you can put a number of stuff on it -
Stop, Confuse, Sleep, Disease, Slow, Disable, Immobilize, Silence, Blind, Oil
and Sap.
Geez, that's one easy mark to defeat after lots of high HP dudes. A single toss
of NihoRem will render Enke useless and at your mercy - bash at it in any way
you want since Enke will not be able to counter as it's been put to Stop.
Enke isn't much of a challenge either way - it heals itself twice during
battle, and uses Purify when it loses half HP (in case it suffers from status
change) followed with White Wind afterwards. White Wind is pass-able which
makes foe immune to any status change for two minutes - and it's not like it's
going to help it much anyway.
Berserk tank (Bacchus' Wine) with good equipment can single-handedly take down
Enke. It'll try to fortify itself with occassional Protect and Shell, but this
is only prolonging the inevitable - putting Enke 6 feet under.

Golmore Jungle

A sprawling jungle in the Jagd Difohr, it remains much as it always has been,
untouched by the hand of Man.
Though the viera make their villages within this jungle, the ways to their
enclaves are tangled and hidden.
Barriers throughout the jungle, too, prevent easy passage. These were erected
by the viera to prevent outsiders from intruding, the blessing of their people
needed before one may pass.

-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-= ASHE'S POSTCARD COLLECTION No.29
Eruyt Village

Hidden village of viera in Golmore Jungle. Viera enclaves are scattered
throughout the jungle, but all are warded against entry by those of other
tribes or lands. Viera are reclusive by nature, living separate from the world
outside, shunning even the society of their own kind, save when necessity
demands.
This isolation is in part made possible by the viera ability to hear the spirit
voice of the Wood, and thereby know all that comes to pass within Her borders.
Throughout the history of Ivalice, rarely have the viera ventured beyond the
borders of the Wood, and few outsiders know of their laws or customs.
Viera villages are formed of massive trees linked by suspended paths, with
dwellings and small shrines to the spirit of the Wood encircling the trunks.
During the day, many viera come to a clearing in the village, where a
glistering spring bubbles up from the earth, to meditate. Their leader resides
in the center of the village, and governs according to the Word of the Wood.
Those who perform the sacred ceremonial duties of salve-maker or wood-warder
stand at her side, defending the ways of the village and of the viera.
Compared to other races, the viera seem to move at a slower, more contemplative
pace, more at peace with the flow of time.
However, some younger viera have begun to question the wisdom of rejecting
change in the midst of a rapidly developing Ivalice.

------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv35
Next esper challenge awaits you! Zalera has a lot of moves, but only one of
them deals any damage - boss mainly relies on status meddling, Dead Bones
allies and instant KO.
First of all, come into the battle with level numbers that are divisible by 1,
2 or itself - as such equip Nishijin Belt and most status worries are off your
back (you'll only need to remove Stop with Remedy).
Let's take a look at what you can toss at boss status-wise - Slow and Blind are
your only status allies. Kill Dead Bones with Curagas or just usual physicals,
and you can also consider putting Disable on them.
Status buffs worth some consideration are Shell (most important one as it will
halve the chances for all status spells to succeed, including Kill and Death)
and Protect, other ones not much so since you're facing a time limit of 5
minutes and lots of potential KOes. In case you get put under Confuse, equip a
wimpy weapon until status is removed.
Zalera's first move is engaging defensive mode, where it gains a boost to DEF
and MDEF - as a result of this some Dead Bones will spawn as well. For as long
as Bones are around, Zalera won't attack you, so use this chance to defeat
Bones with ease. Be careful of Bones' Hawk Glare putting you on Disable while
you're disposing of them, and in case you cast any magic spell with Bones
around, they put up Reflectga. After you dispatch four Dead Bones, Zalera
switches to non-defensive mode and uses Enrage. Defensive mode can be
disengaged earlier if your attacks are strong enough to damage Zalera (the best
option is chucking Curaga, but boss' Reflect must wear off or be removed
first).
You'll now face an assortment of Kill, followed by few rounds of Stop, Sleepga
or Death. Afterwards boss switches to attack pattern of casting lv-specific
spells, ending the chain with Prime Lv. Death. If you've come in battle with
levels I suggested, you'll avoid all problems, otherwise equip necessary acc to
block the effects. If Zalera was affected with Slow or Blind, it'll continue
the chain with Purify.
Now comes the part where Zalera enters defensive mode again, calling out Dead
Bones for help... honestly, not much changes until boss hits critical HP
levels. At this point attack pattern is not followed anymore and you're blasted
with Prime Lv. Death (next one incoming after each next 14 commands). Zalera
can use most of its attacks now, though you have nothing to worry about since
you're protected. Kick its undead ass and claim next esper.
-------------------- CONGRATULATIONS! YOU ARE VICTORIOUS! ---------------------

- You can now summon Zalera! Take W exit to [Garamsythe Waterway].

------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv37
An exceptional esper challenge is at hand and you shall prove your worth by
stomping on Cuchu and getting it under your control. Status buffs that'll be
important to maintain are Shell and Bubble (Cuchu has lots of status spells at
disposal and Shell will be halving their chances to connect). Boss itself is
immune to all status changes so no help in that field for this battle. Fight
itself is led on water terrain with no significant advantages for either side.
When battle starts, magic field envelops the party and causes a severe HP
drain. There is no way to counter its effects, so you'll have to dedicate a chr
to constant healing. Quickly run into N dead end of battlefield, with Cuchu hot
on your trail - your goal is to trap yourself into the dead end, and have Cuchu
block the path. That way you can't get out, but Foobars also can't get in to
join the fray. It can happen that a Foobar or two may drop in to say hello
before you successfully box yourself in, in which case use NihoRem combo to put
some serious status hurt on Foobar and then kill it.
Now that you're locked in, prepare for incoming assault from Cuchu. Wearing
Black Belt is imperative in order to shield your chrs from Disablega - other
statuses don't matter as much and they can easily be cleared. Start chipping on
Cuchu's HP until it loses 20% HP, at which point it begins using Malaise for a
moderate HP recovery (again after each next 8 commands). In addition its rephy
and Bio will be only moves that deal damage for the moment. Cuchu can't ignore
EVA, so a good shield will go a long way.
After losing half HP you'll be introduced to Mana Spring (Cuchu no longer needs
MP to cast spells) and Invert - it's likely that effects will kill the chr
targeted, so counter that with Phoenix Down (as a bonus, chr's MP will surely
be back to full). Cuchu also gains Damage Resist, making it slightly bit
tougher. About Foobars - couple more of them will fall down from ceiling and
scurry around behind Cuchu's back. Since they can't reach you, sometimes you'll
be chucked an extra spell in your direction - stop them in their tracks with a
healthy dose of NihoRem.
Toxify gets finally lost... and that's about it - every other attack still
remains at boss' disposal. Maintain Shell at all times, and be vary of attack
pattern for Malaise and Invert. After boss enters critical HP, its defense and
attack powers increase even more, so consider using Gil Toss to inflict some
serious damage. Above all, don't become frustrated over the battle and keep
your cool - Cuchulainn is conquered. After your victory be aware of any
remaining Foobar foes as they don't disappear when Cuchu's defeated.

------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv38
Make sure you have Black Belt, for if you get Disable, sayonara to you.
Checking status affinities, it can only be poked with Slow and Confuse -
Berserk on the beastie could mean more harm than not, so please refrain from
using it. Earth weakness calls for some change of equipment - wield Cypress
Poles for some high class damage. Immediately bash it up with few strikes to
nullify Tiamat's attack bonus when it has full HP. If you don't wanna bother
casting status spells on boss, equip Niho and chuck a Remedy at it. Oooh, now
that is a slap to self that I wouldn't wanna get. After being target of few
spells, Tiamat will Reflect itself.
Cast Decoy on your fighter to have Tiamat focus its undivided attention to that
chr, while you keep wailing on boss. A nice way to keep Tiamat occupied is to
Berserk it, while keeping Reverse status on your fighter - that way each strike
will heal him or her. You can further fortify your position by Protect and
Regen spell (take care to renew your protective buffs when they wear off),
whereas tossing Berserk to fighter is another splendid idea. Swap in
Windbreaker for two times boss uses Aero in addition to being under Shell.
Boss' Disablega will miss, and you will see Rake most of the time, mixed with
occassional Breath here and there when boss crosses certain threshold. If you
get Sap, counter it with Regen for a healthy HP boost. Curaga gambit in place
can recover huge chunks of HP in one go, nulling boss' efforts to bring you
down. You can give Shear a try in bringing down boss' MDEF, which in turn
increases damage Cypress Pole deals.
What else can be told... oh, about boss gaining DEF boost when in critical HP?
Nothing serious, except making him last a bit longer than usual, and that still
can't save it from becoming catfood.

------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv39
Oh my gosh, does it ever quit after getting its ass kicked at Henne Mines? Oh,
it is not the same guy? Okay, I still hate this one. Majority of boss' attacks
consists of chucking status magic your way, and in one quick swoop you can shut
it up. Equip Niho and use either Remedy or Echo Herbs on boss to inflict
Confuse, Sleep and Silence (or only Silence if Echo Herbs were used) - you can
also use respective magics of course, but using Niho is three times faster.
Swap accessories for Rose Corsage afterwards. Now that boss can't touch you
with magic, turn your attention to two Treants that are waltzing nearby. They
won't be much trouble before falling, and be careful for Tri-Attack.
Fortify yourself with Protect, Regen and Haste, and make sure you have some
Handkerchiefs on hand to cure Oil from incoming Sporefall. Even though boss has
Null VIT, you can cast Shell on yourself to have 50% less chance for boss to
hit you with status effects. Take care to renew your protective buffs when they
wear off. Once Wyrm loses 20% HP, it will use Sporefall for some major status
disorder. If chrs get Confuse, quickly go to menu and switch their weapons for
wimpy counterparts until they are no longer under Confuse. Don't waste Remedies
for removing status, use Esuna instead, and Handkechief for Oil. After
Sporefall is used, boss won't use status magic anymore, but it does gain access
to Fireball; Sporefall is incoming again after Wyrm makes 15 commands.
If you don't remove Oil, Fireball will deal obnoxious damage to you; Rake isn't
much threat though. Sporefall can still be used until end of battle, so don't
think you're over with it. Another easy way to fell boss is to keep it asleep
and chuck reflected Aero at it - weakness to wind and Sleep status will give
you huge bonus to damage. It's all in the stuff you come with and weaknesses to
exploit.

Paramina Rift

Comprising a great ravine running through the mountains of the Jagd Ramooda,
this is a barren land covered in hoarfrost and deep snows. The spent shells of
airships hang in the frozen river, and here and there can be seen the ruins of
great cities built during the years if the Galtean Alliance.
Many are the scholars who believe that the Paramina Rift was once a rich and
verdant land, and that a climate change brought about by the Mist made it into
the cold, harsh jagd we see today.

-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-= ASHE'S POSTCARD COLLECTION No.32
Mt Bur-Omisace

The sacred mountain of the Kiltia sect, located to the north of the Jagd
Ramooda. A temple was built here by believers to mark the place where the
founder of the Light of Kiltia began to spread the teachings. There are
accounts of the holy city here dating back to writing from the age of the
Galtean Alliance.
On its long history, Mt Bur-Omisace has never fallen under the control of any
foreign power. On the understanding that Kiltia's followers would exempt
themselves from political dealings in other lands, Kingdom and Empire both
formed a pact to guarantee a holy city's independence, an agreement which
stands to this day.
It would not be an error to call Mt Bur-Omisace itself a shrine to Kiltia.
Apart from the temples, there are only a few residences, with roadside shops
catering to the steady stream of pilgrims.
In recent years, refugees from war-torn lands have gathered here, forming camps
on part of the mountain. The priests of Kiltia give them aid that they might
live here in peace.
As Mt Bur-Omisace is surrounded by jagd, the faithful must cross the Inner
Naldoan Sea by boat in their pilgrimage to the holy city.

------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv40
Cast Protect, Regen, Bubble, Faith, Haste and Bravery on yourself before going
further. Take care to renew your protective buffs when they wear off. Checking
status affinities and considering our options, you can put some stuff on it -
Disease, Reverse, Slow and Silence. Mark's Protect, Haste and sometimes Bravery
will wear off eventually and they won't be bothering you ever again. If you'd
prefer no Bravery, exit and reenter the screen until the status is not there.
Wear Black Belt to be immune to Disable from mark's rephys. Now there's a
couple of things you need to take care of at once - Antlion is surrounded by
some Killer Mantises and you need to get rid of them pronto as well as prevent
Antlion to Cannibalize them. Have one chr toss NihoRem on Antlion to inflict
Disease, Slow and Silence, while other two chrs cast Warp to banish sidekicks.
If Antlion manages to dine once, it becomes lv44 which is still manageable -
for desert on the side it becomes lv52, thus growing progressively harder.
Disease will prevent it from recovering HP from Cannibalize, as well as give
your tank breathing room by blocking most, if not all of its attacks. Cast
Decoy on tank, give him/her Main Gauche and best shield (have those Shield
Block licenses learned) and make sure you keep tank healed for strikes that get
through. Since Disease prevents activation of HP threshold skills and pass-
ables, that means no Enrage and no ability to ignore EVA. Meanwhile other two
chrs are spread out and keep poking Antlion with wind based weapons or magic
until Antlion is no more.
-------------------- CONGRATULATIONS! YOU ARE VICTORIOUS! ---------------------

- Return to Lhusu GCR and warp to Bhujerba. Report to Niray and receive 4300
gil, Bubble Belt and Sickle-Blade. And what of Site 11 Key? You will be able to
claim it when you get to [Phon Coast].

- Bounce back to Mt Bur-Omisace (talk to both Gurdy and Hymms to start the
hunts, if you haven't done so already) and then exit to [Paramina Rift].

------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv40
Cast Protect, Regen, Bubble, Faith, Haste and Bravery on yourself before going
further. Take care to renew your protective buffs when they wear off. Checking
status affinities and considering our options, you can put some stuff on it -
Sleep, Silence and Blind.
Choco's invisibility will wear off as soon as it attacks you, and for Haste and
possible Protect just wait them out. Bird will require a more specific approach
since its element weakness varies. The only non-element damage spell we have at
the moment is Balance, so we'll be using this magic to hit choco when it's
sleeping - combined with Faith it'll do big damage, but you have to do it
right.
OK, when Tricky charges you, begin attacking it as well as letting it hit you
until its HP drops below 50% - at this point mark's HP Devour wears off, Wild
Charge is no longer used and you'll be seeing Choco-Comet now and then (spread
your chrs out!). Immediately when you spot the change in choco's pattern (or
sometime before it loses half HP), throw Alarm Clock with Niho to put it to
Sleep (you'll need to get rid of Larsa and Monid to prevent them from waking it
up).
Now lower your chrs' HP into low ranges to increase the damage Balance can do.
Make sure Faith is on so your damage output is even greater, then pop Reflect
on (don Ruby Rings) and cast Balance off your chrs - bird will get bashed nine
times for some exceptional damage. Be on the lookout and prepare to inflict
Sleep again if choco wakes up before going down.
If Tricky enters critical, it'll gain Paling and White Wind, increase in attack
and defense power, as well as instant rephys. You won't be able to inflict
Sleep for roughly 2 minutes, so just hold your ground and patiently wait for it
to be gone, then repeat the procedure.
And lastly, Trickster will sometimes run away from battle; if it happens, don't
chase it as you'll draw unwanted attention from other enemies. It will come
back to you so stay put.
-------------------- CONGRATULATIONS! YOU ARE VICTORIOUS! ---------------------

- That is one mark down in this area, next one is in [Spine of the Icewyrm],
which is your next destination. On route save your game at [Path of the\
Firstfall].

------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv40
Cast Protect, Regen, Faith, Haste and Bravery on yourself before going further.
Take care to renew your protective buffs when they wear off. Checking status
affinities and considering our options, you can put a number of stuff on it -
Confuse, Disease, Reverse, Slow, Immobilize, Silence and Blind.
When Feral spots you, toss NihoRem to inflict all of the above statuses (except
Reverse) and the stage is set for kicking its ass. Since cat is under Disease,
you'll never see Purify and Balance, chance of getting Petrify is shrugged upon
as it's easily cured with Gold Needle (spread chrs around), you'll only need to
look out for Blaster's Sleep, Slow, Silence and Blind (toss a quick Esuna).
Equip your tank with best shield available, Main Gauche and cast Decoy to have
Feral focus on tank, while tank him/herself and other two chrs kill it
painlessly.

items and Morbid Urn appears in Bazaar. Cough up 250000 gil and buy it to

Arcanas.

-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-= ASHE'S POSTCARD COLLECTION No.33
Stilshrine of Miriam

An ancient shrine deep within the Jagd Ramooda. Like Raithwall's tomb, this,
too, was constructed in the time of the Galtean Alliance, originally to honor
the ancient god of swords and martial might. It is said that a Gran Kiltias of
long ago selected the Stilshrine to house the relics of Dynast-King Raithwall,
though why he would choose this site, and not a temple of his own sect, is
unclear.
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Violators will be shot (again) - HABNo28
Drop till you shop             - no shops, blimey
Weather forecast               - W&TNo29
Chest contents list            - TRENo20
ASHE'S POSTCARD COLLECTION No.33 =-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-

- Access to last area of the dungeon is possible only after some deadly events
at Bur-Omisace, when you need to talk to Acolyte to obtain Stone of the
Condemner. Details will be listed further down in the walkthru.

[Stilshrine of Miriam / Walk of Sky]

- Keep going S.

[Stilshrine of Miriam / Walk of Mind]

- Save at GCR, then go S to enter the shrine.

[Stilshrine of Miriam / Ward of Measure]

- In the middle of this room you'll find 'Pedestal of the Dawn'. Equip Dawn
Shard on party leader (you got it way back in Raithwall Tomb), examine the
switch, pick second option and pedestal will activate properly (if you try
operating it with anything else equipped, three enemies will spawn). You'll be
teleported to another room. Don't forget to switch Dawn Shard off.

[Stilshrine of Miriam / Ward of Velitation]

- Kill enemies as you go and proceed W.

[Stilshrine of Miriam / Walk of Torn Illusion]

- Upstairs, around the room and check out another 'Pedestal of the Dawn', like
in the first room. Equip Dawn Shard on party leader and voila. Return to
previous room.

[Stilshrine of Miriam / Ward of Velitation]

- Take any stairs you desire to exit E.

[Stilshrine of Miriam / Walk of Revelation]

- Look, a Save Crystal... or rather Life Crystal! Something's odd about it...
it's green... it attacks you! Beat the Crystalbug and it will turn into real
SCR. After saving take up the middle W exit.

[Stilshrine of Miriam / Ward of the Sword-King]

- N gate is locked, so tackle S portion. At the end of the path check 'Sword of
Judgment' and N door will now open. Before you depart for the newly shown 'Way
Stone' start poking along the W wall and *wait* few seconds - the wall will
dematerialize and you can take some stairs up into hidden corridors.

[Stilshrine of Miriam / Walk of Torn Illusion]

- Keep climbing the stairs and before you exit out at the top, make sure to put
Float on, or bring out a chr you don't use and go into next area.

[Stilshrine of Miriam / Cold Distance]

- If not floating, you will be affected by Confuse and Berserk trap. Quickly
switch out the chr you used as bait and eliminate slimies along with Matriarch
Bomb if it appeared. There is another trap at the chest you see - open it and
you can get Shell Shield. If you nab Dark Matter, reload and try again. Make
your way back to [Ward of the Sword-King].

[Stilshrine of Miriam / Ward of the Sword-King]

- Go and examine the orange 'Way Stone' inside the now open room.

[Stilshrine of Miriam / Ward of Measure]

- You're back in the first room. Take W stairs down and take W exit (when you
examine the door, pick second choice to advance).

[Stilshrine of Miriam / Cold Distance]

- Immediately take W exit.

[Stilshrine of Miriam / Walk of Prescience]

- Take the topmost of the three passages leading W and you'll come to a statue
'Stone Brave', which is facing S. Turn it in counterclockwise direction once to
have it face E (when it faces right direction, statue's eyes will glow). Then
take S stairs to next area.

[Stilshrine of Miriam / Walk of Reason]

- Carry on, open two huge doors on your way, and start searching for another
'Stone Brave', located on S end of this room. When you find it, it will be
facing E, so turn it counterclockwise once to have it face N. Take N exit from
this room.

[Stilshrine of Miriam / Cold Distance]

- Now it's a wise idea to return to outside and save your game. When you do,
return to this room and take E exit.

[Stilshrine of Miriam / Ward of Steel]

- Go downstairs, open the door, and enter the banzai.

------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv41
Hmmm... *checks HP*... am I playing the right game? After huge HP bonanza from
Elder Wyrm this guy's HP is laughable. Still, there are few things that make
your battle more difficult - magnetic field will significantly slow down your
actions for as long as you have metallic equipment. Hop into mystic armor and
wield weapons not made of metal (for example poles or bows).
Checking status affinities it can only be affected by Slow and Blind, which is
good enough for me. Battle begins with Vinu being under HP Devour effect, which
lasts until it loses 50% HP, so be careful you don't eat too much damage - good
news is that Vinu will be taking as much damage as it dishes. Toss Haste on
whoever gets pinched by Slow from Vinuskar, and use Esuna to heal Petrify or
Sap. If a chr gets Confuse charm from Crown (used when Vinu loses 20% HP),
immediately equip wimpy weapon. After losing 50% HP, Vinu begins using Sword
Dance, so cast Protect if you haven't already - in addition it will now always
hit you with physicals and has a small chance to counter.
Recast Slow when it wears off and keep pushing Vinu's HP down to zero until it
falls back where it came from. You can swipe Thief's Cuffs from Vinu if you're
lucky enough, but don't sweat it if you don't for you will be able to buy them
pretty soon, if you haven't already.
-------------------- CONGRATULATIONS! YOU ARE VICTORIOUS! ---------------------

- When you defeat it, press on E to find third statue. This one is facing N, so
turn it counterclockwise once to have it face W. Nearby is the Urn holding the
map of the shrine. Now return to previous room (you'll see the giant sword
being raised, and thus you can explore new parts of the shrine).

[Stilshrine of Miriam / Cold Distance]

- Go N.

[Stilshrine of Miriam / Ward of Measure]

- Consider saving your game as well, then use yellow 'Way Stone'.

[Stilshrine of Miriam / Ward of the Sword-King]

- Go S towards the giant blade and pass underneath it. Examine S door and pick
second choice to enter... get thy battle Ashe!

[Stilshrine of Miriam / Hall of Worth]

- Anyone have a nice campfire around?

------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv41
Prepare yourself by wearing Nishijin Belt and Ice Shield, and unequip any guns
or measures because Ice Azer heavily reduces such damage. Back in Bur-Omisace
you can purchase Storm Spear and Storm Staff (hidden bonus of upping thunder
damage) and then wield these weapons. This will not be an easy battle because
Mateus can only be affected by Oil and is immune to everything else. It's
different song with its helpers - Ice Azer can be put under Sleep, Immobilize,
Blind, Oil and Sap; so put Azers to Sleep as soon as you can and then blast
them with thunder magic (note that you suffer 5% of damage inflicted). All foes
in this battle have Piercing Magic, so Reflect will not help you. You will be
put to Sleep unless you pack Nishijin Belt like I advised. Even though bosses
have Null VIT, you can cast Shell on yourself to have 50% less chance for them
to hit you with status effects.
Cast Protect, Shell and Haste on yourself (take care to renew your protective
buffs when they wear off) - preps are done, so let us get down to riding this
world of Mateus and bringing it under our command. With Sleep danger out of way
the other status you can look forward to is Sap from Blizzaja (whip on
Quasimodo Boots), which is used once she loses half HP; and Slow from same
magic spell (equip Sash prior to being hit). Boss follows Chain Magick with
Blizzaja, and can now sling magics at you much faster. All ice damage will be
reduced by half, and you can increase damage output by putting Berserk on your
fighter along with Decoy. Mateus has higher prob to evade attacks because of
Parry, and its magic power increases when in critical HP. Not much to worry
about but to continue beating on it until it succumbs in defeat.
-------------------- CONGRATULATIONS! YOU ARE VICTORIOUS! ---------------------

- You now gain the ability to summon Mateus - go S.

Deja-vu!

- View the scene, then check GCR and teleport to Bur-Omisace.

------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv41
NTSC-U/C version: Boss is not alone, for he somehow deployed three additional
Judges behind your back - I wish I could cheat like that in Command & Conquer,
only that I shall command my three girls into kicking boss' ass, thus
conquering the battlezone. Anyway, he is also the last of the bosses that start
with buffs on, and you can't do nothing about it but to wait it out - ya,
Dispel is coming out to your friendly neighbourhood magic store soon. Enough
rambling, let's look what we can do with this guy.
Judges behind you will be throwing Lunge and Water Spout at you (everything can
be blocked), so pick them off one by one immediately. Boss will take some time
to casually walk over to place of battle, so use that time - if boss' Protect
and Shell wear off, Judges will recast it on him, so that gives you another
reason you want to be free of their oppression. Looking at status affinities...
harharhar, now that is a surprise. You can inflict Stop, Sleep, Slow, Blind,
Sap and Berserk... wait a minute, was that Stop I wrote? Why yes, it is!
Once you clear Judges off the chessboard, sling Stop on boss and then just bash
him up; or use NihoRem on him to inflict all statuses at once ('cept Berserk).
Have none of the goodies I keep advising you to have? Here's how battle shall
unfold then - boss' regular attack will occassionally Blind someone (make sure
you do same to him), so Argyle Armlet would be welcome addition. After losing
30% HP, boss cries with Battle Cry, gaining more firepower. Not much change in
battle plans except that he heavily reduces physical damage when in critical
HP, which you can counter by few well placed Firas or similar. Also beware of
increasingly higher combo rate as you are reducing his HP.
NTSC-J version: You get to look forward to a different boss battle. Unlike US
version, head honcho will mostly rely on magic attacks so employing Reflect
would be an excellent choice. Wear Jackboots to be immune to Immobilize and if
you will be using Reflect, remember to switch to healing with items. Even
though boss has Null VIT, you can cast Shell on yourself to have 50% less
chance for boss to hit you with status effects. Once he loses 70% HP, he will
start spamming his spells so a focused assault will destroy his Construction
Yard and you will win.
Here's one thing that confuses me - that is Item+... neither he nor Judges use
items, and when I tried using Hi-Potion on him (all three Potion Lores
learned), he got healed for 600 HP. Should you have any insight on the matter,
sling it in my direction.
-------------------- CONGRATULATIONS! YOU ARE VICTORIOUS! ---------------------

KTJN SIDEQUEST

- Go speak with Ktjn again and she will have made her decision, then she
disappears from the stairs. Based on answers you have given to her she will be
inside [Clan Hall]. Go talk to her once more and she will give you Platinum
Sword. This is the end of her quest.

- You're already in [Clan Hall], so speak to Mont for following rewards:
- for felling Vinuskar: 1100 gil

- Mont will also offer you to hunt for one of his elite marks (which you should
accept):
- Priority Petition No. 7 Carrot (rank 7 mark)
  petitioner is Zammadria in [Nalbina Town / West Ward] (inside aerodrome)

- Go talk to all seven petitioners to formalize the contracts.

- There are new magics (Dispel, Bio, Vanish, Death and Vanishga), techs (Addle
and Bonecrusher), gambits and equipment available, so update accodingly. Also
by taking airship flight from Rabanastre to Bhujerba, you can buy Syphon magic
during travel.

- MAKE SURE YOU BUY SOME BUBBLE BELTS NOW! For some silly reason they're
unavailable for buying when your clan rank is Paragon of Justice.

NABREUS' MEDAL QUEST

- A check first - did you see Ma'kleou yet in [Nabreus Deadlands / The Muted\
Scarp]? It is advisable you do so.

- Enter [Lowtown] and go to Dalan's, who is having a visit by Roh'kenmou. Talk
to him to find out he is after a medallion, which was broken into four parts.
Dalan had first part, and you have the second part (Blackened Fragment as a
reward from successfully hunting Orthros) and third part (Dull Fragment from
Waterway puzzle). Talk to Roh'kenmou again and fork over both fragments (there
really is no use hanging on to them). Remaining piece will require you to do
some legwork.

- Find Filo prowling the SE corner of [South Sprawl] and talk to her. Note that
you MUST talk to Roh'kenmou first before she even helps you look for this
fragment. Next travel to [Southern Plaza] and talk to 'Curious Woman' near the
fountain. Then waltz to [Muthru Bazaar] and talk to people labeled as
'Merchant', with each inquiring about him having dealt with a necklace. One of
them will offer further hints - go to Yugri's now and speak to 'Sotted
Imperial'. Now go find Kytes in [North Sprawl] near Storehouse Five, followed
by talking to Filo in [South Sprawl] once more. Finally return to Yugri's to
have one more word with the Imperial and you obtain Grimy Fragment KI.

- Give the final fragment back to Roh'kenmou - all four pieces together will
form Medallion of Bravery later. Continuation of the quest will be done once we
get to Archades.

- Luccio in [Mosphoran Highwaste / Babbling Vale] is now selling 1000 Needles
tech, as well as some new equipment.

- A lot of marks to be hunted down - begin with Vorpal Bunny in Golmore.

------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv42
Cast Protect, Shell, Regen, Bubble, Faith, Haste and Bravery on yourself before
going further. We'll destroy the dude before your buffs wear off, but if not,
then renew Protect, Shell and Haste only. Checking status affinities and
considering our options, you can put some stuff on it - Slow, Blind, Sap and
Berserk.
We'll destroy Mindflayer with Berserk, but before that toss NihoRem to inflict
Slow, Blind and Sap, while other two chrs use Bacchus' Wine to add Berserk
(alternately use Indigo Pendant and cast Berserk - the acc nulls VIT making
status spells always hit). Now the mark has trouble hitting you with rephys,
even though it attacks twice as fast. Have Power Armlets equipped (rare drop
from Wary Wolf) at all times to be Stop-immune, else you may regret it if the
mark casts Time Requiem (if you don't have Power Armlet, you'll need to
maintain Shell to halve status infliction chances). Once it's under Berserk
influence, pull out your weapons and begin bashing it up.
Be cautious when it near critical HP - let Berserk run out before you apply it
again. Otherwise there's possibility Mindflayer would heal itself to full with
Soul Etude (Mystery Waltz and Hero's March will be cut off with Berserk
casting, but if they succeed... cast Dispel to remove buffs gained and simply
repeat what you've been doing from start of battle).

------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv42
Cast Protect, Regen, Bubble, Faith, Haste and Bravery on yourself before going
further. Take care to renew your protective buffs when they wear off. Checking
status affinities and considering our options, you can put a number of stuff on
it - Confuse, Sleep, Disease, Slow, Disable, Immobilize, Silence, Blind and
Sap.
Dispel beneficial statuses from Atomos, toss NihoRem and you've basically won.
Even when it wakes up, it won't be able to do a thing because of Disable on it.
Regen and Restore will do squat, but Atomos is able to remove bad statuses with
Purify once Disable is gone - White Wind will go into effect immediately,
preventing you from hacking its circuits for 2 minutes.
Atomos has active HP Devour when battle starts (loses the pass-able once HP is
below 50%) and ignores EVA (shields do no good, but Blind will cause attacks to
occassionally miss). If Disease isn't on, rarely mark'll decide to Restore
itself once it loses half HP (when it goes critical, it stops using the skill).
Atomos has no status potential to put on you, so equip desired acc and bash it
up good. Spreading chrs out will prevent Power Stun and Spin Kick to hit them
all (spice it up with Decoy on your tank).

further. Take care to renew your protective buffs when they wear off. Checking
status affinities and considering our options, you can put a number of stuff on
it - Disease, Reverse, Immobilize, Silence and Blind.
You'll be focusing on Disease and Immobilize in order to overpower Bloodwing.
Disease will prevent it from healing with Leech, and Immobilize will allow you
to attack it with ranged weapons without coming too close for it to harm you.
Even though bats can usually be hit with melee weapons, this one has flying
property so you'll be relying on ranged weapons. Have Tourmaline Ring equipped
to void Poison from rephys.
Dispel marks Haste and possible Bravery, then mess it up with NihoRem (don't
bother with Reverse). Equip ranged weapons and stand good distance away from
the bat, then start target practice until it falls from the sky (Immobilize may
need to be renewed once or twice).

------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv43
Cast Protect, Shell, Regen, Bubble, Faith, Haste and Bravery on yourself before
going further. Take care to renew your protective buffs when they wear off.
Checking status affinities and considering our options, you can put a number of
stuff on it - Sleep, Disease, Reverse, Slow, Disable, Immobilize, Silence and
Sap.
Reflect and Invert will save the day in Braegh's case. Heal yourself with
Hi-Potions or don two chrs with Ruby Ring acc and send them in for close combat
(mark has Return Damage), while support chr casts Reflect on self, then equips
Opal Ring and heals the team with Cura or Curaga, whichever is more necessary.
Do not be concerned with status changes or Braegh healing itself with reflected
Thundara, for sooner or later it'll cast Invert which will mark its doom. In
case you're a bit unlucky and Braegh loses half HP with no Invert being cast,
it'll shield itself with Magick Shield for 2 minutes, being immune to all types
of magic attacks.
Invert is a skill that can be reflected (luckily this mark doesn't have
Piercing Magic) and once it lands on Braegh, its HP will be less than 999. All
it takes now are few well placed blows and horse is history.

------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv45
Try to make sure that the area is completely clear of undead enemies, including
on the top plateau with Roblon on it. The mark rarely moves from its spot,
though it will try to cast magic in case one of the chrs gets in range.
Cast Protect, Shell, Regen, Bubble, Faith, Haste and Bravery on yourself before
going further. Take care to renew your protective buffs when they wear off.
Checking status affinities and considering our options, you can put some stuff
on it - Slow, Blind and Sap; not much, but it'll help in the long run.
Finally a mark that cannot status jinx you in any way, so acc of choice will be
Ruby Ring, Opal Ring and Turtleshell Choker. Give two chrs with Ruby Ring and
best shield, then send them in for melee damage, while support chr with Opal
Ring stands back and fires off healing spells, occassionally harming Roblon
with ranged weapons. Toss NihoRem to inflict statuses mentioned above, and let
fireworks fly.
Roblon will sometimes heal itself with reflected Firas, but reflected Blizzara
and Thundaras along with chrs' physicals will keep the gauge on your side.
Roblon also uses Fear, AoE skill which lowers MP - I suggest not to bother with
Charge tech to recover MP, as it will just get emptied again. If your support
chr gets low on MP, use Charge or Turtleshell Choker for some emergency
healing.
Mark's Blind status will ensure some of its rephys miss, and as battle wages
into 2nd halftime, you're introduced to a bit more of mark's physicals - not to
worry, Blind will still cause a miss here and there.
Finally we come into critical HP, where Roblon's attack and defense power
increase, as well as rephy being able to be executed immediately. Keep Slow on
the foe at all times as well as Reflect on your chrs as once again Roblon will
be mostly chucking magic spells. Remove final portion of HP and you win.

The Salikawood / Sun-dappled Path; save39, RDMC
------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv46
Cast Protect, Shell, Regen, Bubble, Faith, Haste and Bravery on yourself before
going further. Take care to renew your protective buffs when they wear off.
Checking status affinities and considering our options, you can put only a few
statuses on it - Slow and Silence.
Carrot presents a good challenge - your acc of choice will be Black Belt to
prevent Disable from Putrid Breath and Power Armlet (rare drop from Wary Wolf)
to null Stop from Time Requiem. Kjrn will be mainly assisting you by putting
buffs on your chrs.
When you see the mark, chuck Dispel on it to remove its buffs and it'll use
Hero's March, which you'll simply Dispel again. Move two chrs into melee range
and have them start attacking, and ensure that support chr is out of Carrot's
melee range - I find it best when I put this chr behind either Carrot's back or
behind both melee chrs.
Support chr's role will be to heal melee chrs of status changes that will be
inflicted with Putrid Breath, and make sure you'll be switching acc in time
before you're hit. Should the mark be put under Slow or Silence, it'll spam
Putrid Breath for a while and then use Purify.
After Carrot loses half HP, it'll use Growing Threat to double its own level
and raise ATT a bit. Its attacks will increase immensely in power so you'll
need to rely on constant healing. Fortunately Putrid Breath is used more often
now, so it may be wiser to keep Carrot under Slow and keep applying it after
Purify does the removal; and consider using Bio or Balance for some magic
damage.
The following tip has been brought to me by users of FF12 GameFAQs board -
Carrot counts as undead creature and as such healing magic and items will
damage it. So set your chrs up with Reflect and then simply bounce Cure type
magics off to hit Carrot three times per cast. Renew won't work, by the way.
-------------------- CONGRATULATIONS! YOU ARE VICTORIOUS! ---------------------

- Report back to receive 5200 gil, Stink Bombs and Putrid Liquid.

JOVY QUEST

- Afterwards seek out Jovy in [Nalbina Town / West Ward] and talk to him. This
is 3rd time out of five.

- That makes all of the marks slain. All that remains from optional stuff is
one esper in Stilshrine. Even though I try to take on everything as soon as I
can, fighting Zeromus at this moment isn't recommended - during the battle you
cannot use magic, and you don't have a steady supply of X-Potion yet. It
doesn't mean it's impossible, though, just very hard - if you go to Nabreus and
chain Banshees there, you can get Black Mask (+53 MDEF) as very rare drop.
Similarly, Maximillian (+58 DEF) is a very rare drop from Elvoret in Necrohol.
I will return to this guy when I have a steady supply of X-Potion available.

- Warp back to Salikawood and proceed to [Living Chasm]. Head for E exit...
it's closed? Talk to 'Moogle Boss' in front and he'll ask you to gather nine
other moogles (a counter appears). They all get marked on your map, so all you
need to do is get there and talk to their pompomasses. There are 3 moogles in
[Path of Hours], 2 in [Trunkwall Road], and 4 in [Garden of Decay]. Back to
Salikawood and start hunting them down. When you find last batch of moogles,
make sure to agree to tag along.

- Path from Salikawood is open. Talk to 'Moogle Boss' and get a present -
Quasimodo Boots. Hey, Christmas comes early this year! If you talk to all other
moogles, they will mention doing the repairs in [Mosphoran Highwaste], [Cerobi\
Steppe] and [Necrohol of Nabudis]. Additionally, fixing the gate has caused
another esper to become available, and it ain't as tough as the bozo in
Stilshrine. But before fighting it, proceed just a few more screens further E
to [Phon Coast], where you will be able to buy some new equipment and spells.

- Exit E to the beach.

nearby the shrine), and lastly with 'Shrine of the Northwest Wind'. Save your
game, then return to [Skyreach Ridge] and proceed N towards [Empyrean Seat].
Get ready!
