------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv47
Protect, Shell, Haste, Bravery and Bubble on your chrs, then Dispel on Exodus
and begin hacking away. Status-wise Exodus can only be affected with Slow -
bleh. Unlike previous optional espers we fought Exodus is going solo, and
before it becomes SOL, it'll put up quite a fight.
For acc you are wise to equip Power Armlet on your tank and Bubble Belt for
your two healers. Also take this advice to heart - after Exodus loses 20% HP,
DO NOT CAST DISPEL on Exodus, ever. If you do, Exodus counters with Flare or
Scathe and you really don't need another extra strong spell pouring down onto
you. But do take the opportunity and use few Shear techs to lower boss' MDEF.
It is also important that your chrs are spread apart to avoid Scathe hitting
everybody. To play it safe, have your tank move in close and dish physical
damage, while you have two healers kitted with ranged weapons on opposite
sides. Exodus can't ignore EVA, so a good shield will go a long way.
Items cannot be used during this battle, and you wouldn't be needing them
anyway. Battle goes pretty smoothly (take note of esper taking as much damage
as it causes) until you chip off first 20% of esper's health. Say hello to
Flare, which will now come in after each 6 commands. Yes, yes, it may be
tempting to use Dispel to remove boss' Reflect, but refrain from doing so - in
addition to Flare or Scathe counter Reflect simply gets recast. If you insist
on pestering boss with magics, use Reflect-THIS! strategy or don Opal Ring
which ignores Reflect status.
With 50% HP gone Exodus uses Unleash and then pulls out its trump card in form
of Scathe - keep those chrs spread out! Like with Flare, Scathe is incoming
after each next 6 commands; esper unfortunately loses HP Devour now.
With critical HP Exodus introduces last ditch effort to be a victor - it will
erect Paling... that's all? It's pretty bothersome to try and wait it out while
being bombed with spells, so instead use Reflect-THIS! strategy or don Opal
Ring and send few non-elemental spells in Exodus' direction until it's gone.
-------------------- CONGRATULATIONS! YOU ARE VICTORIOUS! ---------------------

- You now have the ability to summon Exodus! Return to [Babbling Vale] and warp
to Phon.

===============================================================================
PHON COAST area
===============================================================================

- Here is a little treat for you (credit: KADFC for showing it to me). In [Phon\
Coast / Hunters' Camp] take a chocobo and ride it towards Tchita Uplands. In
Tchita Uplands go all the way E until you end up in [Tchita Uplands / The\
Shaded Path]. Here try to ascend the grassy slope between two smaller rocks,
and a bangaa 'Game Hunter' will warn you about entering Cerobi. Press on anyway
and you'll be able to enter Cerobi Steppe. You also need to make sure you
attempt to climb the slope before the time for chocobo riding runs out.

- Once you're in Cerobi, you'll likely have like maybe 20 seconds left in
riding time. Once you're off the chocobo, make it all the way SE by foor until
you enter Balfonheim.

- In [Balfonheim Port / Sea Breeze Lane] you can talk to few people (you cannot
enter other areas of Balfonheim yet), and when you want to return, simply use
GCR to warp back to [Phon Coast / Hunters' Camp].

- So what is the purpose of this trip? Cerobi Steppe is littered with great
treasures, among which you can find an infinite source of Ribbon.

- You have the ability to try obtaining a Ribbon, an accessory that nulls most
negative statuses (sadly it will not shield you against KO), but you need to
have Diamond Armlet, which is obtainable from [Tchita Uplands / Garden of\
Life's Circle] treasure. Take a trip to [Cerobi Steppe / Crossfield] and start
prying open treasures there while having Diamond Armlet equipped. If you don't
have it yet, wait until clearing next dungeon and you will be able to buy
Diamond Armlet.

- With [Phon Coast] map in your pocket, go N to exit the camp into [Caima\
Hills], then hike NE to [Limatra Hills] and NE into [Rava's Pass]. Save your
game here, then exit N to Tchita.

Tchita Uplands

A hilly region reaching to the south of Archadia. Before the widespread
adoption of airships as the primary means of conveyance, this region was the
highway to the Imperial City, and filled with travelers.
Ruins can be spotted here and there amongst the tall grasses, and researchers
from Archades often come here to delve into the mysteries left by whatever
ancient civilization built them.

The Sochen Cave Palace

A giant underground complex in Archadia, consisting of natural caverns and the
abandoned ruins of an ancient palace. Many of its ways and passages remain
uncharted on current maps. From the style of the carvings adorning some of the
walls, it is thought that the complex was built at some point during the
Galtean Alliance, though no records of its construction remain.
A survey mission was initiated to chart the many corridors here, but a
particularly nasty infestation of creatures has significantly hampered
progress.

------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv48
Five little Mandys on a wall... you're lucky there isn't 100 Mandys! When their
funny introduction is off, Mandys scatter in various directions to buff
themselves up. Now trust me when I say that you do not want to let them do
that. In worst case scenario you're looking at 3x Mystery Waltz, Vespersong and
Warsong - first increases foe's lv by 20%, second increases foe's MAG by 20%,
and third increases foe's STR by 20%, and all of those are permanent effects.
Imagine trying to take on lv99 Mandy group - you will get teared apart.
Checking status affinities all little guys have one thing in common - they can
be affected with Disease, and two other statuses. Mandys themselves can also
throw almost every status in the book at you and oh boy, will you curse a lot.
Or you can Berserk whole group and just take them out one by one, while you
heal madly.
For starters I suggest you have Nishijin Belt on to prevent Sleep. Disable is
more harmful than Sleep, but you will see it far less often than Sleep. Even
though Star has Null VIT, you can cast Shell on yourself to have 50% less
chance for boss to hit you with status effects (will apply for all others as
well). Having the best shield currently available with all Shield Block
licenses learned will also go a long way to blocking Pollen and Scream attacks.
With that out of the way you will need a healthy supply of Remedies, possibly
with all Remedy Lore licences. Now the question comes, who to eliminate
first... I suggest to get rid of guys that do Waltz crap - Topstalk, King and
Star. Of course they won't go down that easily and will put up quite a fight,
what with constant Pollens and Screams coming your way (for chr with Confuse
equip wimpy weapon until status is gone).
If you have NihoRem possibilities, chuck a Remedy on King to Stop it, Star to
put it to Sleep, and Queen for her to undergo Silence. This will also add
Disease to them preventing healing, so why not do the same to Topstalk and
Prince as well? If there is no NihoRem available, things may get little
tougher.
Mandys have high VIT so your status magic may miss often, but you could equip
Mirror Mail and have status magic cast by foes reflected off yourself. Remember
to switch to healing with items in this case, so you don't accidentally heal
any of your foes.
At start of battle quickly give chase after majority of Mandys to prevent them
from using group skills, and instead focus on their enemies (you, that is). Pry
open Star's HP supply and freeze it up a bit with Blizzara spells (if you used
NihoRem to put it to Sleep, so much better) until it is eliminated. With that
status caster is out of picture and you can have first sigh of relief.
Begin shooting after Topstalk next - it is weak to water, so you can have a chr
equip Murasame and slice it apart like a true samurai. It's possible that
Topstalk may kill itself thanks to HP Devour it gains when out of half HP.
That's two down, and King goes next - abuse wind weakness with Gladius and
scatter foe's leaves thru the wind. And now just the healers remain.
Roast Prince with few Fira spells, and then just bash Queen up until it
succumbs to KO as well.
If you still get overwhelmed, try using your espers or in last case, wait until
Mandys are together and then perform a Quickie but also make sure you chain
together enough attacks to trigger Concurrence afterwards.
-------------------- CONGRATULATIONS! YOU ARE VICTORIOUS! ---------------------

- After killing them, take either E or W exit. You can also return to the kid
that gave you the mission and you will get 1000 gil and 3x Remedy.

[Sochen Cave Palace / The Acolyte's Burden]

- Follow the path, take N branch when coming across it. Go N all the way, and
examine SCR. Kill Crystalbug for real SCR to appear. Save thy game, than exit E
to next area.

[Sochen Cave Palace / Mirror of the Soul]

- Open the two doors, then *hug* the right wall until you come to the Urn with
the map of Sochen Palace. There is 'Pilgrim's Door' located in middle of this
area, leading N... but when you try opening it, you can't. Read the inscription
to get a clue on what you must do... Take a look at the map - you will see that
[Mirror of the Soul] is connected to [Falls of Time] with five entrances. From
left to right, I will name them A1, A2, A3, A4 and A5. Likewise, [Falls of\
Time] is connected to [Destiny's March] with five entrances as well. From left
to right, I will name them B1, B2, B3, B4 and B5.

[Sochen Cave Palace / Mirror of the Soul]
[Sochen Cave Palace / Falls of Time]
[Sochen Cave Palace / Destiny's March]

- Take A5 and you will be in [Falls of Time], just above A5. Now here is how
you need to walk to get rid of the waterfalls:
A5, A1, notice about waterfall course being changed, B1, B4, notice about
waterfall course being changed, A4, A2, notice about waterfall course being
changed, B2, B3, you hear 'Pilgrim's Door' open in the distance, A3. Now open
'Pilgrim's Door' and claim a weapon from the treasure.

- That was one puzzle. For the other you have to go to [Destiny's March].
W-most door is called 'Ascetic's Door' and has another stupid mechanism that
won't let you advance. Read the inscription for a clue, and then look at the
map and you will see how a part of the area forms a circle, kinda like a clock.
Let us mark the areas as 3 o'clock, 6 o'clock, 9 o'clock and 12 o'clock. Some
of the doors are marked as 'Door of Hours', and some as 'Ancient Door'. Start
by approaching 3 o'clock from E side, but you must not open any doors to get
there. The easiest way to do it is to take either B3, B4 or B5 entrance coming
from [Falls of Time].

- So, beginning from 3 o'clock, go like this: SW to 6 o'clock, then NW to 9
o'clock, then NE to 12 o'clock, then SE to 3 o'clock. If you do it correctly,
you will hear 'Ascetic's Door' unlock. That is it for now - with both puzzles
solved and a boss coming up it is a good idea to return to [The Acolyte's\
Burden] and save your game. When you do, return to [Destiny's March] and take N
exit.

[Sochen Cave Palace / Hall of Shadowlight]

------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv49
Oh no, it's a zombie! *readies shotgun and blows its brains out* That wasn't so
hard, was it? What? I'm playing wrong game? *Ashe kicks me in the butt* Oh, you
can do that as many times as you want!
After a not so impressive Ahriman's enter-da-stage let us take a look at its
status affinities - just Slow... but better that than nothing. Flip NihoRem on
it (I hope you acquired Niho by now) or manually cast it until it is affected.
First strikes from boss will not be dangerous, some crappy lv2 magic and
occassional strike. You can wear Mirror Mails and have boss hurt itself with
reflected magic, and clear Doom with Remedy. Since Ahriman is undead, casting
Cura (not Curaga) off yourself will get the job nicely done as well (arrange
gambits for healing with items)... oh, and wear Jackboots for Immobilize
immunity. Beware of Phantasmal Gaze and remember to equip wimpy weapon in case
you get Confuse charm (have lowest VIT chr wield ranged weapon to keep him/her
away from two main fighters). Even though boss has Null VIT, you can cast Shell
on yourself to have 50% less chance for boss to hit you with status effects.
After Ahriman's missing 40% HP, it will Divide itself and bring in a fake.
Faker can use most abilities that real deal can, except that it has only 700 HP
and can be affected by more status changes. Don't bother with it, instead
prepare Cura and target it at Ahriman/s - one cast will be enough to defeat the
faker.
Be careful now - Ahriman will ignore both EVA and VIT, so its attacks will
start hitting a lot more often. The suckiest thing is Phantasmal Gaze always
finding its mark... aaah, just cope with it for now. Ahriman also cuts any
damage received by 30%, so put up your dukes! Laugh at it as it tries to use
Immobilizega unsuccessfully.
At 40% HP remaining Ahriman summons three fakers, which can be squashed with a
nice Cura again. Not much is different until 20% HP left, where boss summons
six fakers. Here's where things get a bit odd - faker will sometimes use Boon,
but on my chrs and not on the main boss. When you clear them out with Cura,
beware of Maser Eye, strong dark physical attack. Should you decide not to
worry about it, leave one fake alive until original is defeated. Set up one of
your gambits to hit a foe with less than 1000 HP with 1000 Needles - once five
fakers are gone, switch this gambit so that a Potion is thrown onto faker
letting you know which is which. Afterwards switch the gambit off and kick
original Ahriman's ass back where it came from.
-------------------- CONGRATULATIONS! YOU ARE VICTORIOUS! ---------------------

- Take E exit after the battle.

go.

-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-= ASHE'S POSTCARD COLLECTION No.37
Old Archades

District on the outskirts of Archades. With the transfer of governance to the
Imperial system, a new city was created, the existing city blocks now belonging
to the old quarter.
At the time, the underprivileged lived here along with nobles who had lost
power with the rise of the Empire, while those with power lived in the new
city.
Now, several centuries later, little has changed. The residents of the old
quarter are largely itinerants and those others outside the protection of
Imperial law. Unlike the new city where buildings tower towards the sky, the
old city remains brick and stone. Everything feels neglected, abandoned to a
fate of slow decay.
With officials less than inclined to worry about the old quarter's governance,
little or no effort has ever been made to revitalize the area.

town, and you have - three in fact. Jules will ask you to complete a simple
task of talking to someone. If 'Bag of coins' is the one you need to take care
of - find Beasley, then return to Jules. He can be found sitting on pair of
boxes when en-route to SCR. In case of Shady Seeq selling moogles, go talk to
the dancing chaps; and if 'Ex-broker' is the target, you need to talk to 'Fresh
ardent'.

parties will begin fighting each other, thus drawing the attention of Imperials
guarding the way to Archades. You are now free to enter it.

-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-= ASHE'S POSTCARD COLLECTION No.38
Archades

The capital of the Archadian Empire. Still small when it first formed as a
city-state, it grew tremendously during the long peace fostered by the Galtean
Alliance. When the Empire was formed, the city center was relocated, forming
the Archade we know today.
Though poor in both natural resources and land, Archades came to prominence as
a city of innovantion and learning. All information and technology gathers
here, and the famed mages and artificers born within her walls are legion.
Knowledge, then, is the true strength of the Archadian Empire.
The city of Archades forms an octagon with the Imperial Palace as its center.
Around the Palace sit the Senate Chambers and other administrative quarters,
beyond which lies a booming mercantile district. The buildings in the city
center are quite tall, with the lower floors being used mainly as residences.
The difference in heights between the various building makes this a city of
small airships, that being the most efficient means of accessing all levels of
the metropolis.
More than half the population of Archades is hume, and while at one time all
lived near the ground, of late, those of power or particular wealth have taken
to living in the higher apartments and traveling exclusively by provate
airship.

------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv51
Again - Protect, Shell, Haste, Bravery and Bubble on your chrs *BEFORE* you
enter the room. During the battle magic field makes you unable to use magics,
so you will need to rely on items for revival and HP recovery. Though this
isn't my usual suggestion, here it is - since you can't use MP, launch a
Quickie right off the bat to inflict severe damage on Zeromus and use reserve's
MP for additional Quickie.
Most annoying status in this battle will be Stop, so Power Armlet to the max.
If you have Shell Shields, now's the time to equip them - remember, Shell
halves base chances for statuses to hit. Healing will be done with X-Potion
gambit, and make sure you've learned all Potion Lores.
Dark Lords will spawn periodically during the battle to aid Zeromus - they will
mostly cast Toxify and use Lunge. You can render boss' sidekicks harmless by
using NihoRem combo (advisable statuses to put them under are Stop, Sleep and
Disable). Zero itself is not hard on physicals (begins with HP Devour), he will
pester you more with gravity spells and buffing itself up. Boss begins the
battle with several buffs and there is nothing you can do about it but grit
your teeth and put up with it. Zeromus can't ignore EVA, so a good shield will
go a long way.
Serious obstacle awaits when you remove 20% of boss health - it bears the name
Piercing Graviga. Your HP must be above 50% or you're KOed - this is where
X-Potion gambit will be most important and why Bubble Belt isn't exactly
recommended (more HP damage means more X-Potions used). Graviga will be
launched again after each next 8 commands.
With half HP lost Zeromus uses Greater Barrier (I hate Damage Resist, I really
do), HP Devour bites the dust and Graviga's pattern changes to being used after
each 6 commands.
So what else can be said... keep Dark Lords in check with one of three statuses
I mentioned above (arrange your gambits so that chrs won't be attacking targets
that aren't dangerous) and observe your HP to not fall below 50%. Pretty
standard battle for pretty standard esper.
-------------------- CONGRATULATIONS! YOU ARE VICTORIOUS! ---------------------

back to Archades.

-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-= ASHE'S POSTCARD COLLECTION No.39
Draklor Laboratory

Weapons research laboratory located a short distance from the administrative
district in the northeast of Archades, sponsored by the Archadian Imperial
Army, with Dr. Cidolfus Demen Bunansa as its head researcher and maker of
policy.
Research is divided among airship design projects, sundry weapons projects and
magickal endeavors.
In recent years, particular attention has been paid to magicite research, with
great strides being made in the manufacting of magicite and improved methods
for drawing energy from the stones.
A strict security system is in place to ensure that none of the knowledge in
Draklor Laboratory leaves its doors without authorization.

------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv51
Protect, Shell, Haste on your chrs, then charge into heat of battle. Take care
to renew your protective buffs when they wear off. The battle itself is pretty
basic - you have four Rooks that surround boss and act as his support. At first
they will cast Regen, Protect, Shell and Curaga at boss, and then proceed with
attack pattern I noted down when writing Rook's statistics.
I advise to leave boss alone for now - don't even cast Dispel to remove his
buffs as he'll regain them eventually, so why bother at all? Plus after he has
been a target of several attacks, he will put up Paling to null physicals.
Boss packs exceptionally high DEF and MDEF, so expect your attacks to deal low
damage. His position is fortified even further when he readies Greater Barrier
- as with Paling, skill is eventually used if you attack him with at least one
Rook still alive. Don't attack him until Rooks are gone, no Paling and no
Greater Barrier.
Checking status affinities, he can be affected with Silence and Berserk (this
can also be your cue to not see Greater Barrier, but are you willing to risk
taking increased damage?), and Rooks with Doom. Not really worth of NihoRem, so
I suggest not bothering with it.
As battle starts, immediately show your undivided attention to Rooks and begin
chewing down on their HP. When 1st Rook falls, a small scene plays and battle
then resumes. If you deal any blows to Cid, expect Paling and Greater Barrier
to go up - Paling will wear off after about 2 minutes. Doctor's attacks ignore
DEF and are 100% accurate, so having a shield is useless. Wield two-handed
weapons and continue beating down Rooks until all are gone. Note that when two
Rooks are defeated, their attack pattern breaks and remaining two Rooks will
then be able to execute regular physicals instantly. Pick up the pace and hurry
up in killing them.
With his support gone, Doctor is all by his lonesome - wait until he pops Haste
on himself and then Dispel him, but if he is under Silence, he will skip Haste
phase. Next thing he will do is slowly start walking towards one end of the
room - use this time to put a serious dent in his HP. He unleashes bigass
attack once he stops, then resumes poking you with shots - next Tokamak is
incoming after Doctor shoots you 24 times, so that should give you plenty of
time to finish him off. Two things make it easier for you - he cannot combo his
attacks, and battle ends when he loses 75% HP.

-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-= ASHE'S POSTCARD COLLECTION No.40
Balfonheim Port

Prosperous port of the Naldoan Sea renowned for its rich fishing grounds. In
addition to fishing, the port is known for its shipwrights and their numerous
contributions to the advancement of seacraft. Though demand has dropped with
the spread of airships, the wrights are still able to turn a profit on their
craft.
The power of Balfonheim rests with the sea captains and pirates of wealth.
Though belonging in name to Archadian Empire, well-placed regular bribes have
ensured the city autonomous governance.
The city itself is small, being a classic port town, with many stone-cobbled
alleyways between building which hug the curve of the hills. Fresh seafood can
be found in the market stalls daily, along with many other items brought by
traders and pirates.
Several waterways tun through the city, some carrying drinking water, others
used as canals for the transport of goods.
The manse of Pirate King Reddas stands in the western quarter of Balfonheim.

- Go to [Clan Hall] and speak to Mont for following rewards:
- for felling Ahriman: 1600 gil
- for felling Mandragoras: 1600 gil

- Mont will also offer you to hunt for two of his elite marks (which you should
accept):
- Priority Petition No. 8 Ancient Man of Mystery (rank 7 mark)
  petitioner is Montblanc in [Rabanastre / North End]
- Priority Petition No. 9 Belito (rank 5 mark)
  petitioner is Montblanc in [Rabanastre / North End]

- Go speak with all seven petitioners to formalize the contracts.

- A reminder that Clan Provisioner has Faith, Bravery and Bubble magic for
selling, if you haven't bought them yet.

- It is time for a little subquesting.

SEVEN SISTERS QUEST

- Go to any aerodrome and board a ship by leisure option (I began from Nalbina
to Rabanastre). Once aboard, go to [Sky Saloon] and talk to Chief Steward.
Choose "Who's this...Rande?" to get some scoop and obtain Ann's Letter KI. One
down, six to go.

- Here are the possible 7 routes you can take, equaling 7 sisters - you must
talk to Chief Steward on each of these flights and choose to show her the
letter. They go in order Ann, Liddy, Twarra, Carryl, Sanne, Lyseth, Cisset.
Once 7th sister is located, you get Ring of Renewal.
  Nalbina to Rabanastre
  Balfonheim to Archades
  Balfonheim to Nalbina
  Bhujerba to Balfonheim
  Bhujerba to Rabanastre
  Archades to Nalbina
  Archades to Rabanastre

- That wraps up this quest.

- Now go to Giza Plains during the Dry.

GIZA PLAINS area
===============================================================================

COCKATRICE QUEST

- Enter [Nomad Village] to check up on little furry pals. Hey, where'd they go?
All cockatrices have escaped. Terra mentions about a magic feather (which we
already have - it is Feather of the Flock; if you don't have it, look up in
the walkhru for info on getting it). First warp to [Eruyt Village].

===============================================================================
ERUYT VILLAGE town
===============================================================================

- Go to [Fane of the Path] and talk to Chit, then Mjrn. You will see some
'Sparkling Light' behind you. Check it out to obtain Dewdrop Pebble, then talk
to Mjrn and offer it to her. Talk to her again and she will request more
pebbles. DEWDROP PEBBLE IS A MISSABLE ITEM! Yoichi Bow you get from this quest
can be bought elsewhere.

- There are 2 more on [Fane of the Path].
  - near Alja
  - near pacing wood-dweller

- There are 6 on [The Spiritwood].
  - on the stairs while descending from [Fane of the Path]
  - near 3-way cross just before entering [Fane of the Path]
  - near Rael
  - near wood-dweller in front of spring (examine the light first, and then you
    need to ask her to get it for you)
  - on the stairs a bit S from the spring
  - NE dead end

- That is all of them - return to Mjrn and fork them over, then talk to Chit,
who will drop something. Examine 'Sparkling Light' nearby and pick up 10th
Dewdrop Pebble, and give it to Mjrn. You are awarded with Yoichi Bow. Now onto
Rabanastre.

===============================================================================
THE ROYAL CITY OF RABANASTRE town
===============================================================================

- Go to [North End] and look for a cockatrice Renn. Try talking to it and it
will run away. You won't be able to catch it just by running after it, so you
will need to seek cover behind pillars where possible. When Renn is about to
walk by, slowly walk outta your hiding place and talk to Renn, then choose
"Erm...no?" answer. Again go to the place where you originally found Renn, only
this time it will be on ledge across. Talk to it and pick first choice to
obtain Diamond Sword... but if Chit isn't back yet, you need to do that first.
Now onto Jahara.

NEBRA RIVER QUEST

- You must complete Draklor Laboratory first and finish up Cactuar quest, so
that Ruksel appears in [Dalmasca Estersand / South Bank Village]. He'll be
standing on one of the piers next to Nebra. Talk to him and he will ask you to
find him a fishing rod. Travel to Balfonheim and talk to 'Fishing Enthusiast'
in [Balfonheim Port / Chivany Breakwater] and ask him about the fishing rod.
When he talks about getting hungry, walk to the aerodrome's entrance (but don't
enter) and then return to where the guy was sitting. Rod will be leaning
against the wall, so grab and you obtain Muramata.

- Return to Ruksel and talk to him to fork over Muramata. Now the fishing can
begin - yay, I am so *not* excited. Talk to Ruksel again and choose your
destiny - for now only Downstream is available.

- So how does fishing work? Each fish is represented as a set of button
commands and you need to input all those commands in order for Ruksel to catch
it. Fish can travel in four directions: from left to right, from right to left,
from top to bottom, from bottom to top. If you mess up command order or take
too long in inputing them, fish will escape. Randomly the fish may turn out to
be empty bottle when caught - it still counts as a successful catch, though!
Each time you go fishing, six fish will try to make by - if you manage to catch
all six, you get the option of acquiring additional reward, denoted by a
blinking light in middle of the screen. However, two conditions must be
fulfilled first: Gilgamesh must be defeated for the 2nd time and you need to
acquire Matamune.

- Here's how to get Matamune - Gilgamesh must be defeated for the 2nd time, and
Muramata given to Ruksel in [Dalmasca Estersand / South Bank Village]. Keep
fishing until you obtain five colored bottles - solve their riddles to obtain
five messages. Solve their riddles as well, and then travel to [Barheim Passage\
/ The Zeviah Span] - you need to enter small portion which is only accessible
from [Barheim Passage / West Annex] and you obtain Matamune from the most
unsuspected visitor. Hah!

- Matamune, once given to Ruksel, will allow you to reel in perfect fishing
rewards which I was describing about two paragraphs back.

- Now let me break down each of the five fishing sections:

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DOWNSTREAM | initially available
Commands   | C, right, X, S - Common Fish
           | C, X, S, up - Common Fish
           | down, X, C, S - Common Fish
           | S, T, X, C - Common Fish
           | T, C, X, S - Common Fish
           | T, X, S, down - Common Fish
           | X, C, up, T - Common Fish

Rewards    | 100 gil - 34% chance to get
           | Hi-Potion - 33% chance to get
           | Water Stone - 33% chance to get
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
MIDSTREAM  | unlocked once you make five perfect fishing trips on Downstream
           | (they do not have to be consecutive)

           | L2, down, R1, C - Common Fish
           | R2, S, X, L1 - Common Fish
           | T, C, up, down, X - Delicious Fish
           | T, L1, right, S - Common Fish
           | X, S, R2, up - Common Fish
           | X, T, C, down, S - Delicious Fish
Direction  | horizontal - 40%
           | vertical - 60%
Rewards    | 100 gil - 33% chance to get
           | Fish Scale - 34% chance to get
           | Water Magicite - 33% chance to get
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

           | T, C, down, up, X - Delicious Fish
           | T, down, left, X, C - Delicious Fish
           | up, R1, T, left, C  - Delicious Fish
           | X, C, R2, up - Common Fish
           | X, T, C, down, S - Delicious Fish

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
HIDDEN     | Matamune required; unlocked once you capture Cactoid Compact on
SHOALS     | Upstream
Commands   | down, up, T, X, R2 - Delicious Fish
           | left, R1, T, X, C - Delicious Fish
           | R2, R1, T, L2, C - Delicious Fish
           | T, C, up, S, R1, L1 - Nebra Succulent
           | up, R1, T, left, C  - Delicious Fish
Direction  | horizontal - 40%

           | Cactoid Commendation - 10%; one time only
           | Hi-Potion - 45%
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
DEN OF THE | Matamune required; unlocked once you capture Cactoid Commendation
RIVER LORD | on Hidden Shoals
Commands   | down, R1, C, L2, right, X - Nebra Succulent
           | R1, L2, up, S, R2, L1, X, right - Nebra Succulent*1
           | T, C, up, S, R1, L1 - Nebra Succulent
           | T, R2, C, L1, X, S - Nebra Succulent
           | up, R2, right, L1, X, R1 - Nebra Succulent
           | X, R1, down, L1, R2, S - Nebra Succulent

           | mystery and claim the legendary rod Matamune!

- So, what do you really get outta all this? Once King is caught, you will
obtain Lu Shang's Badge, one of three loot items needed for Wyrmhero Blade.

- Additionally, Ada will purchase fish from you.
  amount of Common Fish x 10 gil = total amount of gil
  amount of Delicious Fish x 100 gil = total amount of gil
  amount of Nebra Succulent x 200 gil = total amount of gil

PHON COAST area

===============================================================================

- In [Hunter's Camp] go to the house of Shady Bangaa bunch and speak to
Huntmaster. Since you have proven yourself by felling Mandys, they are willing
to let you join, but not before you pass another test. You are to travel to
[The Vaddu Strand] and hunt down rare game Thalassinon.

- There is a total of 80 rare game enemies in FFXII - of those, 49 can spawn
infinite times. 31 rare game enemies, however, will spawn only once and then
never again when you claim the trophy they drop after defeat.

- Hoppalongcassidy to [The Vaddu Strand] and go as far E as you can. Then stand
on the ledge facing W and wait until Thalassinon spawns down on the beach. Go
kill it and it drops Shelled Trophy KI. Save 11, RDMC.

- Return to [Hunters' Camp] and talk to Huntmaster, then to Atak, Blok and
Stok. They will update Shifty-Eyed Man's store in this area depending on how
many trophies you give to them. You can give 30 trophies to say Atak, and the
other two will never get any. Atak specializes in weapons, Blok in armors and
Stok in items. My opinion is - all weapons and armors Atak and Blok will offer
can be found elsewhere, so stick with Stok.

- Talk to Huntmaster repeatedly to get a general idea of how trophy rare game
spawns. 'Enthusiastic Streetear' close to Notice Board as well as two other
people will be giving you vague hints about where might a possible Trophy rare
game be.

- Outfitters gets its own section in the guide, as will rare monsters.

- Additionally, by killing Trophy rare game foes you can gain some more rewards
from Hunt Club Owner in [Archades / Grand Arcade]:
- 6 trophies: Aries Gem, Libra Gem
- 11 trophies: Taurus Gem, Scorpio Gem
- 16 trophies: Gemini Gem, Sagittarius Gem
- 21 trophies: Cancer Gem, Capricorn Gem
- 26 trophies: Leo Gem, Aquarius Gem
- 31 trophies: Virgo Gem, Pisces Gem
Credit: Brady's guide

-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-= ASHE'S POSTCARD COLLECTION No.41
Cerobi Steppe

Hilly higlands region of the east of Archadia, through which the highroad to
Balfonheim Port passes.
Air currents are notoriously unstable between Cerobi and Balfonheim, making
land routes here as popular as those of air.
In the past, villagers in the region erected windmills to catch the winds from
the Naldoan Sea, and used them to mill grain from the harvest. With
advancements in the use of magicks and machineries, however, the windmills fell
into disuse and now stand merely as a reminder of the past.

------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv51
Cast Protect, Shell, Regen, Bubble, Faith, Haste and Bravery on yourself before
going further. Take care to renew your protective buffs when they wear off.
Checking status affinities and considering our options, you can put a number of
stuff on it - Confuse, Sleep, Slow, Silence and Blind.
Dispel Haste in case Vyraal is under its effect, and then toss NihoRem to
inflict above statuses. Silence will seal off Haste and Immobilize, and you'll
need to wear Bowline Sash to avoid Confuse from rephys - Blind will keep you at
bay with Sonic Fangs and Fireball missing sometimes (be on lookout for KO
effect of Sonic Fangs). Keep it asleep and you'll win with little to no
problems (get rid of Viera Adventurer in this case).
Vyraal is also very vulnerable to wind spells. When you see mark casting
Immobilize, get ready to give chase because it will run away from you during
battle. Once you lose track of it, Vyraal casts Haste and Restore on itself,
then returns to fighting you; eventually it'll gain Damage Resist as well. When
it enters critical HP, it'll envelop itself in Magick Shield until it's
defeated.
-------------------- CONGRATULATIONS! YOU ARE VICTORIOUS! ---------------------

- After battle you receive Viera Rucksack KI. Report back to recieve 3500 gil,
Halberd and Crystal Shield. You will also receive Dragon Scale KI. With it
return to [The Northsward] and examine 'Windmill No.10'. After a brief event
Wyrm Philosopher will show up - agree to give him Dragon Scale, and instead he
forks over Ageworn Key KI. He will say that since you didn't have any trouble
finding Vyraal, you won't have any trouble finding the ancient wyrm the key is
supposed to lead you to... he has no idea where the wyrm is, though. The hint
about wyrm's lair is given by 'Stranded Merchant' in [Old Archades / Alley of\
Low Whispers] - he'll talk about not going anywhere since he heard about
ancient wyrm down there.

- Defeating Hell Wyrm is one of the requirements for Yiazmat hunt, but that
hunt itself only becomes available when you've cleared Pharos.

- If you wanna fight Hell Wyrm now, I suggest you get something that absorbs
holy - and that would be Sage's Ring, which you can steal from trophy rare game
Arioch in [Nabreus Deadlands / The Slumbermead]. It has 40% chance to spawn in
NE corner of the area. Since we'll be going there eventually, hold your
chocobos for a while.

------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv51
Cast Protect, Shell, Regen, Bubble, Faith, Haste and Bravery on yourself before
going further. Take care to renew your protective buffs when they wear off.
Checking status affinities and considering our options, you can put a number of
stuff on it - Sleep, Slow, Silence and Blind.
If possible, try coming to this fight with levels that end in numbers 1, 3, 5,
7, or 9, so Sleep magic is rendered useless. For starters toss NihoRem to
inflict above statuses and stage is set. Wear Fuzzy Miter to avoid Petrify from
rephys and Stone Breath, and while's its asleep, don Ruby Ring and employ
Reflect-THIS! strategy by casting Aeroga on your chrs to bounce it onto
Lindwyrm for some bigass damage.
Silence shuts up the beast and makes it unable to cast magic spells - take note
that Lv.2 Sleep and Lv.4 Reverse can't be reflected. If Lindwyrm pulls off
Restore, it'll use Greater Barrier (remove buffs with Dispel) and gain Damage
Resist - Sleep status ensures that won't happen too soon. Best shields will
block most of marks physicals for 1st half of battle, and in 2nd half Blind
takes care to cause physicals to miss. Attacking and defense power increase
when it nears defeat, but all in all, not a tough battle to win.
-------------------- CONGRATULATIONS! YOU ARE VICTORIOUS! ---------------------

- After battle you receive Rusted Scrap of Armor KI. Report back to receive
4200 gil, Barrel Coat and Hi-Ether.

- Go to Sochen now and enter it from [Tchita Uplands].

------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv51
Cast Protect, Shell, Regen, Bubble, Faith, Haste and Bravery on yourself before
going further. Take care to renew your protective buffs when they wear off.
Checking status affinities and considering our options, you can put a number of
stuff on it - Confuse, Disease, Slow, Silence and Blind.
Start the heat with having Dispel remove potential Bravery and by using NihoRem
and inflicting above statuses. Mark has no status effects that can throw at
you, but you'll need to keep Overlord's Bravery under check later in battle (no
worries with it if Silence is added). Blind will make rephys, Tri-Attack and
Pyromania miss from time to time, and Disease prevents acces to Smite of Rage
and Rage skills.
Overlord is strong and hits hard, but not long ago you purchased Curaja which
will keep you in top shape. Insecure Seeq is no fighter and you're likely to
see it fall soon in battle.
At half HP Overlord gains Damage Resist and as it nears defeat, its defense and
attack power increase... and that's it for scare factor. Kick its ass.

if your chrs are too far aways from Goliath.

afterlife (attacking and defense power increase when nearing defeat).

------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv52
Cast Protect, Shell, Regen, Bubble, Faith, Haste and Bravery on yourself before
going further. Take care to renew your protective buffs when they wear off.
Checking status affinities and considering our options, you can put some stuff
on it - Slow, Silence, Sap and Berserk.
Dispel Fury's buffs and use NihoRem to inflict above statuses, then slice it up
with Murasame (bunny is weak to water element). Boss has high evasion and parry
rate, and will frequently counter. Be sure to Dispel it both times when it uses
Hero's March, and reapply Slow and Sap.
Power Armlet to null Stop from Time Requiem is a must - you wouldn't want to
fall victim to this annoying status. Boss rephys may cause a chr to go Berserk,
so to ensure it happens to your tank, whip Decoy on.
After Fury loses half HP, it'll keep using Wine to Berserk itself - have a
dedicated chr always Dispel it, so Fury keeps wasting turns to use Bacchus'
Wine. Its rephys are now insta-executed and it turns into mean knocking machine
- with Curaja gambit backing you up you'll win easily.

area.

------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv52
Cast Protect, Shell, Regen, Bubble, Faith, Haste and Bravery on yourself before
going further. Take care to renew your protective buffs when they wear off.
Checking status affinities and considering our options, you can put a number of
stuff on it - Confuse, Reverse, Slow, Immobilize, Silence, Blind and Berserk.
As soon as mark appears, heal your low-HP chr or put him/her back in reserve if
you've been using wimpy chr. Have Power Armlet on to null Stop from mark's
rephys, then start hacking away at mark. Having Holy Lance (rare poach from
Gizamaluk) is a nice way to end the battle quickly.
Use NihoRem to eliminate mark's ability to cast spells, become immobile, miss
often with physicals (you can block them with shields until mark loses half HP)
and attack slower. Scythe will rarely empty MP pool of a chr with Annul, and
curing Doom will be a cinch with Remedies.
When mark's HP < 50%, it gains Paling, or immunity to physicals for 2 minutes.
For a moment keep using Bio or Balance (whichever is stronger), it now ignores
EVA (but can still miss with physicals); and when mark's HP < 20%, here comes
increase in attack and defense power. None of that stuff is dangerous to you,
so move in and kick butt. Another quick way to win is to Reflect yourself, then
bounce off Curaja until it falls defeated.

------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv52
Attack command is sealed in this battle thanks to magic field. To counter this
restriction, switch your gambit's action 'Attack' to 'Souleater'. As far as
buffs go, consider using Protect, Shell, Haste and Faith on your chrs - as for
the boss... only Slow and Sap.
Battle begins as Chaos summons four Chaosjets - they will try to put buffs on
Chaos and frequently try to Silence you in case magic casting is detected with
Chaosjets around. Each of Chaosjets is weak to one element, so use appropriate
element magic against them or destroy them with non-element magic (Bio).
When minions are gone, cast Dispel on Chaos, making sure to cure Disable as
you go (or equip Black Belt to be immune).
Take the opportunity and use few Shear and Expose techs to lower boss' MDEF,
then cast Slow on Chaos. It is also important that your chrs are spread apart
to avoid Aeroga and Aeroja hitting everybody. To play it safe, have your tank
move in close and dish physical damage, while you have two healers kitted with
ranged weapons on opposite sides (this will also keep Fearga to hitting mostly
one character).
Chaos also has HP Devour ability at start of battle which allows its rephys to
hit twice as hard at expense of boss taking as much damage as it dishes. When
you chip off first 20% of esper's health, say hello to Aeroga, which will now
come in after each 8 commands. Be on the lookout for Whirlwind, which removes
75% of chr's MAX HP - if KO happens, toss Phoenix Down.
With 50% HP gone Chaos uses Aeroja (Bowline Sash to prevent Confuse!) and
begins using its trump card Fearga - here's where you should really take care
not to have everyone grouped together. HP Devour is gone and boss now ignores
EVA. Aeroga and Aeroja will be incoming after each 16 commands.
With critical HP Exodus loses Whirlwind and uses Enrage, as well as gaining
hardened defenses. Switch to Reflect-THIS! strategy (one of your chrs dons Opal
Ring to keep the team healthy) and send few non-elemental spells in Chaos'
direction until it's gone.
-------------------- CONGRATULATIONS! YOU ARE VICTORIOUS! ---------------------

- That was 5th and final boss in the long trek thru Necrohol. Defeating Chaos
also wraps up Nabreus' Medal quest. Next stop is Nalbina.

------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv53
Cast Protect, Shell, Regen, Bubble, Faith, Haste and Bravery on yourself before
going further. Take care to renew your protective buffs when they wear off.
Checking status affinities and considering our options, you can put a number of
stuff on them - Slow, Silence and Sap on Ba'Gamnan, and Sleep, Reverse, Slow,
Silence, Blind, Oil and Sap on all sidekicks.
When battle begins, Dispel all four enemies and start hacking (Monid is
fighting on your side). Use NihoRem on all enemies to inflict above statuses
(except Reverse) - I would get rid of Gijuk to stop the usage of Fang items,
then eliminate Bwagi (thus kicking out magic potential), followed with Rinok
and finally Ba'Gamnan.
None of the bosses have Null EVA, so a good shield will keep you going long
way. Main boss' rephy can Silence you, so chuck Echo Herbs on affected chr.
With Gijuk and Bwagi out of the picture, you'll be experiencing physicals only
from remaining opposition, making it a nice and easy work for you.
-------------------- CONGRATULATIONS! YOU ARE VICTORIOUS! ---------------------

- You will receive 5100 gil and Megalixir.

- Warp to Lhusu Mines now.

------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv58
Cast Protect, Shell, Regen, Bubble, Faith, Haste and Bravery on yourself before
going further. Take care to renew your protective buffs when they wear off.
Checking status affinities and considering our options, you can put a number of
stuff on them - only Slow on Gil, and Sleep, Slow, Silence, Blind, Poison and
Oil on Enkidu.
Battle begins - smack Enkidu with Dispel, and use NihoRem on it to inflict
above statuses, then get rid of it with Firaga barrage. This eliminates
combined attacks of both bosses, insta-KO attacks (Sonic Fangs) and gives you
more breathing room. Gil doesn't have Null EVA, so you can don your tank with
best shield and Main Gauche to block Gil's attacks.
For each 20% of Gil's HP you can steal from him - so five times during this
battle. You can steal two unique pieces of armor, not available anywhere else,
during 4th and 5th stage of battle. In 4th stage you can swipe Genji Shield,
and in 5th stage Genji Gloves. Make sure you Dispel Gil after 3rd, 4th and 5th
phases, for he will gain progressively more good statuses on himself. Once
Enkidu is history, Gil is so much easier.
Slice Thrice is his most heavy attack for time being, until he has less than
20% HP left. He will quickly shield himself with Perfect Defense, and then use
Illusion twice. After second Illusion he becomes vulnerable again and you can
smack him into oblivion. The battle is not yet won, though.
-------------------- CONGRATULATIONS! YOU ARE VICTORIOUS! ---------------------

- He is not defeated yet. Return to previous screen to save your game, then
return here and travel W.

[Lhusu Mines / Site 9]

- Head SW towards the place where you fought Antlion. About halfway there seek
out 'Wrought Iron Gate' and use Site 11 Key to open it.

[Lhusu Mines / Site 11]

- Make your way around the area and use E exit to return to [Site 9].

[Lhusu Mines / Site 9]

- Look for 'Gate Switchboard' and operate it to lift nearby door, thus creating
a shortcut. Return to previous screen.

[Lhusu Mines / Site 11]

- Proceed to NW corner and operate another 'Gate Switchboard' to lift the door,
then travel E.

[Lhusu Mines / Lasche Span]

- Travel SE.

[Lhusu Mines / Site 5]

- You will locate 'Site 5 Cart', which you can use to travel to [Site 11] and

------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv61
Cast Protect, Shell, Regen, Bubble, Faith, Haste and Bravery on yourself before
going further. Take care to renew your protective buffs when they wear off.
Checking status affinities and considering our options, you can put a number of
stuff on the dog (Gil is immune to all bad stuff) - Sleep, Slow, Silence,
Blind, Poison and Oil on Enkidu.
Battle begins - Dispel on Enkidu, then NihoRem on it and spam Firaga as quickly
as you can so it bites the dust. You may lose chr here and there thanks to
Crushing Fangs (Phoenix Down / Raise save the day). Enkidu's Dash will give
some buffs to the dog, which should be removed with Dispel right away.
If possible, try to come to this battle with levels like lv59, or lv67 - this
way you render couple of Gil's attacks useless.
Bosses' combo attacks will drive you nuts, so do keep Bubble and Protect up.
Once Enkidu is history, Gil becomes easier - without his dog he ain't so
tough... or so I thought. Gil is very good at comboing attacks together, and
for 1500 dmg per slice it quickly adds up. And if you don't have to worry about
his "Lv.X" attacks, you can land in many attacks as he wastes time using them.
Keep constant Curajas a must while you're driving Gil towards his doom.
Like previous battle, you can steal an item for each 20% of Gil's health. In
4th stage you can swipe Genji Helmet, and in 5th stage Genji Armor. Wear Power
Armlet when Gil enters 3rd stage to avoid Stop from his rephys, and watch out
for Bitter End skill.
When he has less than 20% HP left, he will quickly fortify himself with Perfect
Defense, and then use Monarch Sword twice (he's likely to knock someone out -
this time reviving may be done quicker with Phoenix Downs). After second Sword
he becomes vulnerable again and you can smack it into oblivion.
-------------------- CONGRATULATIONS! YOU ARE VICTORIOUS! ---------------------

- After battle check 'Sword of Legend'... hm, I say we were duped. Return to
Rabanastre.

------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv62
Hell Wyrm has a long HP bar. Below the top bar you will see 50 blobs, totaling
for 51 bars alltogether. Each one represents around 175112 HP, for a total of
8930711 HP. Crazy number, huh?
Sage's Ring / Maximillian / Brave Suit, best katanas, Power Armlet, Ribbon and
Bubble Belt is the type of equipment I would recommend having for this battle.
Wyrm indeed has lots of HP, but it is very predictable to fight and with a bit
of setup I will help you win.
One of your chrs should wear Ribbon or Power Belt at all times to be immune to
Stop, and then set up a gambit for this chr to cast Bubble on self and throw
Chronos Tear on allies under Stop. Yes, there is only 9 chances you will be
affected with Stop through the battle, but you may not always be lucky to
switch equipment just in time (you can also try maintaining Shell to halve the
chances for Stop to work). Put Bubble Belt on other two chrs, and then arrange
a Curaja gambit for HP < 60% for one of these two chrs only. That way he/she
will be curing most often and thus draw much hate to him/herself.
Typically, almost any strong weapon will be good, as long as it is doesn't deal
dark damage, and katanas also tend to combo often (they are worth using despite
of best katanas not having as high ATT as 2Hswords).
Checking status affinities we see that Wyrm can be put on Oil and Berserk. But
I ask - is that really what you want? Wyrm will be attacking twice as fast,
though it's true you will not be seeing anything else except its regular
attack. Ah, about that - it has a small chance to KO you, so beware.
Enter the battle and immediately chuck Dispel to remove Wyrm's buffs, cast
Protect and Haste, then start hacking at its HP. Use Expose a couple of times
because Wyrm gains Damage Resist when it loses half HP. Shields are useless in
battle as Wyrm has Null EVA and will thus always hit you. For starters you will
be seeing Wyrm's physicals.
When it loses 10% HP, Wyrm charges for Judgment - here's where White Mask comes
in because it will absorb the damage. If any chrs get put to Stop, Chronos Tear
gambit will take care of it. When Judgment is used, you may want to try Berserk
on one of two chrs who do not heal for some swift justice from your side. After
second Judgment Wyrm starts to use magic attacks and Rake. Battle will look
mostly the same until boss loses half HP - at this time all of your attacks
will deal 30% less damage to Wyrm, but thanks to Expose you will still be doing
maximum damage (that would be 6999 - not as great as 9999, though).
Keep counting those Judgments - when 7th is used, Wyrm begins assaulting you
with Rake exclusively and will leave you alone with magic for a while. Keep
Protect up and arrange second chr with Curaja gambit - even though Rake has no
visual confirmation of being able to do so, this attack can combo up to 12
times on you.
After 8th Judgment is used, Rake goes buh-bye and Stone Breath becomes Wyrm's
choice dish on attack list - Petrify to the max! Heal Petrify manually just as
it is about turn chr to Stone to avoid wasting time for Esuna.
9th and last Judgment comes - Stone Breath waves adieu as well, but Wyrm gains
Invert. Woohoo, I presume. Boss will now go like this - Invert, lv3 element
magic, Invert, lv3 element magic, Invert, repeat. Be advised that it can now
cast magic instantly, so having all three chrs with Curaja gambit will be a
smart choice to make. You will be rolling in MP all the time now, so use it or
lose it. Remove final 10% of Wyrm's HP and you win.
-------------------- CONGRATULATIONS! YOU ARE VICTORIOUS! ---------------------

this quest. So what good did all that do... let's go visit Mont in Rabanastre.

The Feywood

An ancient wood deep in the jungles of Golmore. The combination of dense Mist
and regular snow, the latter a product of the region's elevation, is enough to
keep away even the viera.
Many of the trees have stood for several thousands of years, and some have
begun to petrify. Numerous plants once thought extinct grow here, and many rare
birds and animals can be seen in their primitive forms, unchanged for
millennia.

------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv64
In addition to buffs you put on before battle, have Bowline Sash equipped to be
immune to Confuse. Even though boss has Null VIT, you can cast Shell on
yourself to have 50% less chance for boss to hit you with status effects.
Raff will fall from tree with several buffs on as well, so you will make a wise
choice by chucking Dispel on it to have those removed. You can wield weapons
with wind element to inflict superior damage to Raff, or employ the tested
Reflect-THIS! strategy by casting Reflect on yourself before you enter the
battlefield, and then have all 3 chrs unleash Aeroga on themselves for Raff to
be hit nine times. Be aware that your MP is being drained fast so immediately
input next Aeroga punishment, but even if it won't go through, don't worry
about it. I have provided enough intelligence for you to know what to expect
and when.
Checking status affinities we see that it can be affected with Slow, Silence,
Blind and Sap. I wouldn't count on using weapons that can Silence (Mage
Masher), instead use NihoRem and watch all four statuses be added at once. In
case you don't have Niho, Faith will help you have more success in inflicting
Silence. Don't bother with other statuses, Silence is the most beneficial
status you can possibly have on Raff.
When Raff gains Silence liberation, watch it fall apart - it cannot use
Disablega, Sleep, Toxify, Drain, Syphon, Curse and Call for Help, meaning you
just eliminated 70% of boss' arsenal. All that remains is Volley (can Sap) and
Dance (can Confuse, but for that we have Bowline Sash on). Raff under Silence
will also be using those two attacks most of the time, but that is a sacrifice
I am willing to take if it means I won't see darn Curse.
If NihoRem isn't available and Silence didn't succeed, you will have a slippery
battle on hand. I suggest equipping Mirror Mail to bounce back Sleep and
Toxify, and you will need to do quite a bit of accessory switching to be immune
to all other status crap Raff melts out - as it has Null VIT passive ability,
you will get affected. Make sure your chrs are spread out around Raff so that
Curse doesn't get everybody - have ranged weapons equipped and poke Raff from
distance and so you will only need to take care to switch accessory on one chr.
When Raff loses 40% HP, it will use Cry for Help to summon three Malboros for
some extra stinkage - eeeew. Dispatch them immediately or they will mess you up
with Bad Breath (which strangely inflicts only three statuses) - quickest way
is banishing them with Warp Mote if one is available.
With half HP lost Raff can execute spells instantly which isn't that big of a
deal and gains access to Drain. Latter doesn't drain much HP anyway, so again
you win in the situation. Keep cranking Raff's HP down into critical HP to have
it do... absolutely nothing at all. Remove last 20% of HP for you to emerge
victorious.
-------------------- CONGRATULATIONS! YOU ARE VICTORIOUS! ---------------------

- Return to SCR and readjust your gambits again so that you use magic for
healing and removing statuses, then proceed S from [Redolent Glade] into [White\
Magick's Embrace].

- Hug the E wall to find the Urn with Feywood Candle, which reveals hidden
areas on map of Feywood. Take S exit to [Ice Field of Clearsight].

- Check out the map and you will find four star-shaped buildings - these are
called 'Shrine of the Lost'. You need to check out the middle of one of these
shrines and see if there is a 'Feywood Glyph' on ground. If there isn't, move
onto another shrine.

- So what is so interesting about the glyph? If while standing on glyph you
rotate the camera around your leader, you will notice that screen will form an
illusion of a nice place - this is the direction which you must take to find
next 'Feywood Glyph'. Follow the direction you have been given into next
shrine, examine the glyph on ground, look for nice place and so on. Do so three
times (you will place three target [red !] icons on the map) and you will be
able to exit into [The Edge of Reason].

- Oh, here's a tip - the order is different each time, so what may have worked
for me will not necessarily work for you.

- Here there are five 'Shrine of the Lost' buildings. Repeat the instruction
you have been given (you will need to get three glyphs again, just a bit more
running to be done), and you will be able to examine 'Gate Gigas' on SW end -
to open it, you need to summon Belias, then examine the door and pick second
choice.

- I have battled the five Mandys in [The Sochen Cave Palace] and saw their
entry added under Feywood monsters. I was baffled because I did not know what
to do to get them to appear. Thanks to Ultimania I now know the way and here's
how you do it.

- Mandragora Prince, Alraune King, Onion Queen, Pumpkin Star and Topstalk spawn
in [Ice Field of Clearsight]. To get them to appear you need to slay every
single monster in this area (29 enemies total), then exit and reenter. Quickly
run from shrine to shrine and do not stop! Several of these guys know Mystery
Waltz, which increases enemy's level by 20% permanently, and if you take too
```

```
long to locate them, you may run into lv99 enemies. Hey, once you reach lv99,
try and go fight them.

- After spawning (by killing all enemies in the area) the 5 elite vegetables in
Ice Field of Clearsight, you can force the 5 to respawn by going/fleeing N two
screens to [Redolent Glade], then returning without having to kill all the
regular enemies again. And this way it is possible to chain these vegetables.

- Anyway, let us continue our search for Giruvegan.

-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-= ASHE'S POSTCARD COLLECTION No.43
Giruvegan

Ancient city said to lie deep within the Jagd Difohr. A dense Mist conceals its
actual locations. There are some who claim that it holds the secrets of a
legendary civilization that flourished before men knew the workings of the
world, but none remain who know the truth.
Many are the expeditions sent to find this place and record its knowledge, but
most have disappeared in the Feywood, or despaired while attempting to
understand what artifacts have been found. To this day, we are no closer to
discovering Giruvegan, or illuminating its mysteries.

Giruvegan / Gate of Water; Save 13, RDMC.
------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv64
Take care to renew your protective buffs when they wear off. Reflect-THIS!
strategy comes to the rescue - Reflect on your chrs and then cast Curaja on
yourself for Dae to be hit nine times. Reapply and you just bombed its ass back
to stone age.
But you demand an honorary battle for Knight of the Round table? Okie dokie,
you asked for it. Coming into the battle with buffs I suggested will be first
step, and second is to equip Black Belt.
Checking status affinities you can affect Dae with Confuse and Silence. Latter
will only prevent Darkra, but something is better than nothing. Battle itself
consists of several stages and all shall be covered here.
Fight begins with Dae getting Haste on itself so promptly remove it with
Dispel. Battle continues with Dae using mainly physicals and chucking Smite of
Rage on chr who does the most healing. Lower its DEF with Expose until tech
starts missing, meaning you have achieved maximum efficiency. Once you snip off
20% of its HP, it will cast Darkra (or skip it if under Silence). This denotes
coming of several new skills: Ice Break and Tremor. For latter you can either
have Dragon Shield on, or cast Float on yourself and wield Ice Shield (I
recommend second option).
Tri-Attack gets lost when Dae loses 40% HP, but instead it can now always hit
you thanks to Null EVA. Just great news... With 60% HP lost expect Pulsar Wave
to be mixed in, so make sure you have Black Belt on. When boss enters critical
HP range, spread out your chrs to have one or two avoid incoming Rage
punishment. Most attacks get lost except for Smite of Rage and boss gaining the
ability to use physicals instantly. Its attack and defense also improve
drastically with the high probability to comboslice you, so consider using some
magic to wrap things up but if you have used Expose enough times prior to that,
difference will not be that significant. If you have some gil to spare, now
would be a good time to toss some at Dae until it's defeated. Hey, at least it
will now have money to pay for goods in stone age... not that it will do it
much good.
-------------------- CONGRATULATIONS! YOU ARE VICTORIOUS! ---------------------

- Killing Dae will spawn next 'Way Stone'. Return to previous screen to save
your game, then return to 'Way Stone' and warp further W.

[Giruvegan / The Trimahla Water-Steps]

- There are seals located here, preventing you access further. To break the
seals, you'll need to seek out the corresponding gate stone and press it - gate
stones are usually guarded by two Mythril Golems. Begin by going S, and
checking first gate stone you'll see - it is 'Avrio Gate Stone'. Go S as far as
you can and press 'Chthes Gate Stone'. The small clearing between 'Avrio Gate
Stone' and 'Chthes Gate Stone' will hold the Urn with map of Giruvegan, but
only after you defeat Shemhazai. Now work your way towards W end of the path
and kick the asses of two Mythril Golems. Try walking off the ledge toward S
and a path will appear leading further.

[Giruvegan / The Aadha Water-Steps]

- Go S and push 'Paron Gate Stone'. This is the only gate stone in Giruvegan
that can be triggered only once. Then take the other path and keep following
it. As before, work your way towards the inner of the circle - you'll come
across two more gate stones, which you will of course push. They are 'Parelthon
Gate Stone' and 'Tychi Gate Stone'. Turn around and make it to the NW end of
the path. Here kill two Mythril Golems and then try walking off the ledge to
the W and a path will appear leading further.

[Giruvegan / The Haalmikah Water-Steps]

- Go NW and open 'Bulwark Chronos' door to spot a SCR. Finally, I might add -
cast Protect, Shell, Haste, Bravery and Bubble on yourself, then save your
game. Open 'Bulwark Hemera' to proceed further.

[Giruvegan / Gate of Fire]

- Remember how we triggered the secret path to show up twice so far? You'll
need to do it again on this screen. If you look around, there's almost nowhere
you can try walking off the ledge, except for one part of this screen. Look for
it and make secret path appear (it'll point to NE). Walk along it and face next
boss.

------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv65
Wow, three times the bananas from last boss. A magic field will prevent use of
techs, but you needn't worry about it as we'll bash Tyrant off the platform
without techs. Take care to renew your protective buffs when they wear off.
So let's see its status affinities... looks bad, Confuse only. Seems like we'll
have to make due without some nifty status fun. Equip Mirror Mails and arrange
your gambits to heal yourself with X-Potion (make sure you set HP threshold
with HP < 60%), while wearing Pheasant Netsuke; or have your healer equip Opal
Ring while you dedicate two other chrs on casting Blizzaga. You will employ
Reflect-THIS! strategy once more by casting Blizzaga on yourself and keep
spamming it until it falls off.
Tyrant will not stand by idly and watch you tear it apart, instead it will try
to put up a fight. With Mirror Mail on you bounce back all magic spells except
Piercing Graviga which nails you for 50% of MAX HP. It's used fairly rarely in
first half of battle (each 12 attacks), but lot more in second half (each 4
attacks). Also, Tyrant will get healed by reflected Thundaga but it is not used
that often that it should give you a second thought on having Mirror Mails
equipped.
Wearing shields won't protect you from being hit with physicals, as boss packs
Null EVA, but I recommend to sticking with Flame Shield to halve Fireball's
damage. Sonic Fangs has a small chance to KO one chr, so be on the lookout for
that.
The differences between first and second half are as follows: Fireball is used
more often, Piercing Graviga will come crushing in your direction after 4
attacks, and Tyrant is able to cast magic instantly. Be careful when Tyrant is
low on HP, as it can combo attacks up to nine times (occassional Poison should
be treated with Antidote).
NTSC-J version: difference is that Piercing Graviga comes on you after eight
attacks instead. Everything else remains the same.
-------------------- CONGRATULATIONS! YOU ARE VICTORIOUS! ---------------------

- After battle go back previous screen to save your game, then return here and
check newly spawned 'Way Stone' to be warped to next part of dungeon.

Here are the explanations of what do various abbr mean.

SCR - Save Crystal
T1 ~ T10 - Treasure 1 ~ Treasure 10 (look into Treasure section)
I, II, III ~ XXIV - Way Stones
GTS - Gate Scorpio
GTC - Gate Cancer
GTA - Gate Aries
GTP - Gate Pisces
GTSA1 - Gate Sagittarius I
GTSA2 - Gate Sagittarius II
GTL1 - Gate Leo I
GTL2 - Gate Leo II
GTG1 - Gate Gemini I
GTG2 - Gate Gemini II
GTLI1 - Gate Libra I
GTLI2 - Gate Libra II
GTV1 - Gate Virgo I
GTV2 - Gate Virgo II
GTAQ1 - Gate Aquarius I
GTAQ2 - Gate Aquarius II
GTCP1 - Gate Capricorn I
GTCP2 - Gate Capricorn II
GTT1 - Gate Taurus I
GTT2 - Gate Taurus II
Ultima - place where you battle esper Ultima
Omega Mark XII - place where you battle Omega Mark XII

Several of Gate Stones will start a timer, forcing you to get to respective
gate and deactivate it before time runs out. Here's all the time limits you may
face when you dive into Great Crystal:
Sagittarius Gate Stone - 72 secs timer when activated
Gemini Gate Stone      - 144 secs timer when activated
Leo Gate Stone         - 216 secs timer when activated
Libra Gate Stone       - 72 secs timer when activated
Virgo Gate Stone       - 108 secs timer when activated
Capricorn Gate Stone   - 180 secs timer when activated
Aquarius Gate Stone    - 288 secs timer when activated
Taurus Gate Stone      - 252 secs timer when activated

------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv66
Hmmm, I give her 3 out of 10 points. For what, you wonder? Ah, never mind that,
let us see how we can def... I mean, acquire her. Don't wield any elemental
weapons and do not use any element magic, as she might absorb that element.
Have Rose Corsage equipped to null Silence, and try to always maintain Bubble
status to be immune to Disease (in addition to Bubble, have Protect, Shell,
Haste and Bravery - take care to renew your protective buffs when they wear
off). If you don't have Bubble magic, that is quite alright - in this case set
up Vaccine gambit to be healed of Disease.
Preparations are met, now let me run into her hug... errr, you will want to
check her status affinities, yes? Only Immobilize - that's not worthy of
NihoRem moment, and it wouldn't do much good anyway because her bowguns have
really long range. And boy she starts out with so many PA it makes my head spin
- even though she ignores EVA, wearing a shield with some MEVA is good to give
you a chance at blocking Flare and Shock.
When battle begins, Dispel her Haste (my, she is in a hurry!) and then use
Expose couple of times to reduce her DEF as it will help you out in the long
run. She will frequently use Syphon and Silencega - latter is warded off with
Rose Corsage, and for former you will fight it with Charge in case she drains
too much of your MP (having higher MDEF reduces amount of drained MP). Battle
picks up once she loses 20% HP - say hello to Shock which will hit you for
about 2000 damage. With next 20% HP lost she stops using Syphon and begins to
pester you with Flare for around 3000 damage - she also gains Damage Resist
which is partially countered by your Expose assault at start of battle. There
will be eight Shem's commands before you see another Flare and Shock - Flare,
four commands, Shock, four commands, Flare, repeat.
Battle goes roughly the same until she enters critical HP stage, at which point
her MAG and DEF gain a significant boost, plus she gets to cast her magics
instantly. Consider using some non-element magic to clear out last portion of
her HP (Bio), or use some techs - I like to use Gil Toss a couple of times to
wrap up the battle quite nicely.
NTSC-J version: in Japanese version Shemhazai also has access to Scourge spell
once she loses 40% HP. I haven't seen the attack in NTSC-U/C version, even
though I spent at least a couple of hours while battling her.
-------------------- CONGRATULATIONS! YOU ARE VICTORIOUS! ---------------------

- You gain the ability to summon Shemhazai. This has also caused the Urn with
map of Giruvegan to spawn in [The Trimahla Water-Steps], but you will collect
it later. Press on S, open 'Bulwark Aeon', and at the end check 'Empyrean Way
Stone'. Pick first, then second choice to engage. You will get Treaty-Blade KI
and Treaty-Blade weapon. DO NOT USE 'TELLURIAN WAY STONE' YET - return to Great
Crystal by using N-most 'Way Stone', as we shall go get Ultima esper.

------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv69
The sexy lady awaits to be crushed - 10 out of 10 stars! Sorry, Ashe... Let's
begin with preparations... regarding statuses, Ultima is susceptible only to
Blind. Your equipment must include White Mask or Sage's Ring (eliminates
Redemption and causes Holyja to be used in longer intervals). Alternately
consider using best ninja sword you have, and equipment which powers up dark
element - Black Robes or Zeus Mace.
You will need to arrange your gambits quite a bit - for revival arrange Arise
and Phoenix Down gambits, for healing Curaja and X-Potion, and for removing
status changes Esuna.
We come to status buffs for your chrs - Protect, Shell, Haste, Bravery and
Bubble on your chrs. Cast Dispel on Ultima and start hacking away. If you get
affected with Sap, just let it be.
Ultima loses 20% HP and she prepares Holyja if there's a chr who doesn't absorb
holy. By the way, I advise against screwing with her and suckering her into
using Redemption or Holyja cos you may find yourself with unfortunate Game
Over. Keep it cool and you'll win. Also at this time magical field with HP Sap
effect will fall (read "Notes" section of this boss entry to find how the
fields cycle). Heal with items when there's MP Sap and Magic seal fields, for
all other fields you can use magic to heal your wounds - when Magnetic field
falls, remove heavy armor and equip light or mystic armor.
Wear White Mask to absorb Holyja damage as HP recovery, but be careful for
possible Reverse status after being hit. *Immediately* cast Esuna to remove the
status (only Ribbon can block it). Otherwise, by keeping holy-absorbing
equipment on you won't see Holyja until Ultima loses 50% HP.
Greater Barrier makes its entrance now - toss Dispel and eat Holyja. To play it
safe for incoming Renew and Curaja, have your tank move in close and dish
physical damage, while you have two healers kitted with ranged weapons on
opposite sides.
After each second Holyja Ultima gains Attack CT = 0, which denotes you'll be
bombed with Reflectga - Renew - Curaja combo if Reverse landed on at least one
chr. So if Ultima casts Reflectga, counter immediately by using Dispelga on
your chrs or have a chr don Opal Ring and have him/her heal the team in times
of need.
I suggest doing this - remove one chr from main team and put him/her in
reserve, while remaining two chrs assume the roles of attacker and healer. Then
in case if Reverse affects those two chrs, you bring out the third which is
unaffected and use Esuna to remove Reverse. Pretty sneaky, eh?
When you push her into critical HP range, her attack and defense powers
increase, so finish her off with Gil Toss or dark element magics. All in all,
Ultima isn't a hard esper to defeat, but those magic fields are the reason that
makes this fight so interesting and intense.
-------------------- CONGRATULATIONS! YOU ARE VICTORIOUS! ---------------------

- You now have the ability to summon Ultima! We have collected 10th esper.
Return the way you came.
