===============================================================================
THE ANCIENT CITY OF GIRUVEGAN dungeon
===============================================================================

[Giruvegan / Gate of Fire]

- Make way E toward [The Haamilkah Water-Steps].

[Giruvegan / The Haamilkah Water-Steps]

- Travel E.

[Giruvegan / The Aadha Water-Steps]

- Make it to E exit.

[Giruvegan / The Trimahla Water-Steps]

- Get to the Urn on the small clearing I mentioned before, then use 'Way
Stone' at the top to return to [Gate of Water].

[Giruvegan / Gate of Water]

- Travel E and use 'Way Stone'.

[Giruvegan / Gate of Earth]

- Use GCR and warp to Balfonheim.

===============================================================================
THE PORT AT BALFONHEIM town
===============================================================================

- When you arrive, start shopping for new equipment, gambits, magic (Arise,
Esunaga, Protectga, Shellga and Darkga) and techs (get Wither). You can also
fill out all gambit conditions for actions to be taken when buying gambits.

- Head for Reddas' place (SW-most part of Balfonheim, also look for [red X] on
your map) in [Saccio Lane]. Talk to 'Manse Watch' at the entrance to enter and
see some scenes. Reddas joins as Guest chr and Strahl gains the ability to
travel thru jagds - this also adds several Strahl anchors all over the world
making it easier for you to travel there.

- Enter right [Port Villa] and equip Vaan with Diamond Armlet, then open
treasure pot and you may obtain Ensanguined Shield.

- You can buy Diamond Armlet from shop in [Dalmasca Estersand / South Bank\
Village]. This accessory vastly enhances items found in treasures scattered in
dungeons.

- Baknamy Merchant in [Necrohol of Nabudis / Hall of Effulgent Light] is
selling Telekinesis tech, Ring of Renewal, Magepower Shishak, Maximillian and
Demon Shield, so it is worth your while to visit this guy.

- Burrogh in [Barheim Passage / The Lightworks] is selling Hermes Sandals,
Golden Skullcap and Glimmering Robes.

- Lohen in [Dalmasca Westersand / The Western Divide] is selling Agate Ring.

- Take an airship flight between Bhujerba and Balfonheim. Once aboard, you can
buy Indigo Pendant accessory which makes it far more easier for magic to land,
and this is esp useful for status magic.

- By clearing Great Crystal and having Treaty-Blade in your possession you now
have second chance to get a Ribbon - travel to [Ozmone Plain / Haulo Green].
Here you usually find six Red and Black Chocobos - kill them all, then zone two
areas away to have chocos respawn and come back. There is a 1/256 chance that
Lv99 Red Chocobo will replace one of chocos, and this is the one you are after.
Be advised that it may take a long time for Lv99 Red Chocobo to spawn, and do
not be fooled by its HP gauge that says 99999 HP. This choco has infact 239686
HP and will put up quite a fight, which is made hard by bird constantly
spamming Choco-Comet - expect to take 4000-5000 dmg per strike. As the skill
deals physical damage, equip shield with high EVA (Ensanguined Shield maybe)
and start cranking down on its HP. Once you defeat it, it drops Ribbon 100% of
the time.

- In addition to above tips, you can do the following trick: when you enter
[Haulo Green], kill six chocobos, go away two screens and come back into [Haulo\
Green]. Chocobos have respawned, but now you do the following... Petrify all
chocobos you find and let the counter run out so they turn to Stone - keep
walking between the two places chocos appear at in [Haulo Green] and they will
keep respawning *without you needing to zone two areas away for a respawn*;
eventually you'll be lucky enough to get Lv99 bird to pop.

- Now that you have 10 espers (AND finished Mindflayer hunt - if you didn't do
it yet, now's the time), go to Jahara and talk to Geomancer Yugelu in [Jahara /\
Lull of the Land] for him to send a warrior and unlock the blasted door in
[Henne Mines / Ore Separation] that was preventing us access further.

===============================================================================
THE ROYAL CITY OF RABANASTRE town
===============================================================================

- Go to [Clan Hall] and speak to Mont for following rewards:
- for felling Rafflesia: 1800 gil
- for felling Daedalus: 1900 gil
- for felling Tyrant: 1900 gil

- Go to [The Sandsea] and accept new bills.
- Bill No.25 Deathgaze (rank 7 mark)
  petitioner A Traveler is in any of five [Aerodrome]s
- Bill No.26 Diabolos (rank 7 mark)
  petitioner Miclio is in [Bhujerba / Miners' End]
- Bill No.27 Piscodaemon (rank 5 mark)
  petitioner Ivaness is in [Mt Bur-Omisace / Temple Grounds]
- Bill No.28 Wild Malboro (rank 6 mark)
  petitioner Rena is in [Eruyt Village / The Spiritwood]
- Bill No.29 Catoblepas (rank 6 mark)
  petitioner Supinelu is in [Jahara / Lull of the Land]
- Bill No.30 Fafnir (rank 7 mark)
  petitioner Ieeha is in [Mt Bur-Omisace / Temple Approach]

- Go talk to all six petitioners to formalize the contracts (instead of Ieeha,
you will need to talk to Relj; and A Traveler is a kid in a family of three).
OK, let me start reeling them in - starting with Deathgaze.

- This mark is found in [Skyferry / Air Deck], but the process is a bit long;
after you talk to the kid (petitioner), you have 4% chance for mark to appear
on your next flight (but you must NOT take Strahl; and I suggest taking private
cabin) - if you arrive at your destination with no interruption, talk to the
kid again and you chances jump to 8% (your chances keep doubling until 64%, and
then no more); now simply keep choosing the flights and eventually you will run
into the mark.

------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv70
Cast Protect, Shell, Regen, Bubble, Faith, Haste and Bravery on yourself before
going further. Take care to renew your protective buffs when they wear off.
Checking status affinities and considering our options, you can put some stuff
on it - Reverse, Silence and Sap.
Begin the assault by using Silence on the mark (prevents all of its magic
attacks, including super annoying Curse) and then Dispel its buffs. Paling will
go up instantly, so you will have to rely on magic. Gaze's HP Devour wears off
after mark loses half HP. Crushing Fangs deal either huge damage or KO, and
Fireball is also a big threat. Wear Bubble Belt ot maintain Bubble status to be
immune to mark's Disease from rephys. Do take care not to wander too far from
Gaze, unless you want it to completely refresh its HP with Renew.
First time Gaze reaches critical HP, it uses Restore to recover some HP - no
biggie. When critical HP is entered gain, Gaze will cast Reverse on itself, and
then immediately put up Magick Shield. Wait until Reverse wears off (or use
Remedy on Gaze) and finish it off with physicals.
-------------------- CONGRATULATIONS! YOU ARE VICTORIOUS! ---------------------

- Report back to receive 3400 gil and 2x Elixir.

------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv70
Cast Protect, Shell, Regen, Bubble, Faith, Haste and Bravery on yourself before
going further. Take care to renew your protective buffs when they wear off.
Checking status affinities and considering our options, you can put only Slow
on Diabolos.
Mark will be a bit tough to crack, as it can dish many statuses on you. Bubble
will be important to maintain for preventing Disease (from Curse) and keep
Shell up as well. For acc equip Bowline Sash when Curse comes crashing down.
At start cast Dispel on Diabolos to remove its buffs, afflict it with Slow, and
send a tank with best shield and Main Gauche (Decoy!) close to Diabolos to keep
it occupied. Mark's physicals can be blocked until it loses half HP, and for
all battle it has Return Damage.
Once you're past half HP, switch to Flame Shields when Pyromania is cast. At
critical stage Dia has always active Paling, so you'll need to finish it off
with magic attacks - consider reflecting Bio spells off your chrs. Battle is
won and little kids need not fear the demon anymore.

------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv70
Cast Protect, Shell, Regen, Bubble, Faith, Haste and Bravery on yourself before
going further. Take care to renew your protective buffs when they wear off.
Checking status affinities and considering our options, you can put some stuff
on it - Slow and Blind.
Mark has little HP, but you'll need to be taking care of lots of statuses.
Bubble will negate Disease from Fog, Black Belt nulls Disable from Pulsar Wave
and Shell to halve the chance for the rest (Sap is negligible, and for Death
use Arise of Phoenix Down); Black Mask will absorb Darkra's damage.
Don't run around too much so that you avoid getting caught up in battles with
other foes, and Pisco's Invert will help more than harm you.
Pisco will mainly throw status effects at you (be careful with Death) with a
mix of Darkra and Pulsar Wave inbetween (Pisco can execute spells instantly!).
When it gets low on HP, it will use Etude to heal completely, March to gain
buffs (Dispel them!), and finally Waltz. Not much else has changed battle-wise,
so finish it off.

------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv70
Cast Protect, Shell, Regen, Bubble, Faith, Haste and Bravery on yourself before
going further. Take care to renew your protective buffs when they wear off.
Checking status affinities and considering our options, you can put only a few
statuses on it - Slow, Silence, Blind and Oil.
Wild Malboro presents a good challenge - your acc of choice will be Black Belt
to prevent Disable from Putrid Breath and Bowline Sash to null Confuse from
mark's rephys.
When you see the mark, use Warp to banish 3 Malboros poking around nearby,
followed with Dispel on Wild. Keep it under Slow and Blind at all times - mark
nulls EVA, but will still sometimes miss with physicals. Move two chrs into
melee range and have them start attacking, and ensure that support chr is out
of Wild's melee range - I find it best when I put this chr behind either Wild's
back or behind both melee chrs.
Support chr's role will be to heal melee chrs of status changes that will be
inflicted with Cloying or Putrid Breath, and make sure you'll be switching acc
in time before you're hit. Should the mark be put under bad status, it'll spam
Putrid Breath for a while and then use Purify (at one side this is bad, but at
other it's good as it won't be using physicals).
After Wild loses half HP, it'll lose HP Devour and stop using Cloying Breath -
no other changes worth mentioning. With critical HP it'll use Soul Etude to
completely recover HP and then gain Paling for 2 minutes.
Since Wild can be put under Oil and is vulnerable to fire, you can use
Reflect-THIS! strategy and spam reflected Firagas until Wild bites the dust -
you're likely to kill Wild faster than it can use Soul Etude in this case.

critical HP.

get to you in this place, but its Shock can... however, since mark's magics can
be reflected, put on Reflect or Ruby Ring and just watch fireworks fly. Speed
up the process by reflecting Thundaga off yourself and Fafnir is defeated.

===============================================================================
THE FEYWOOD area
===============================================================================

- King appears in [The Edge or Reason], and one thing that is difficult is
getting it to appear. You have to kill *every enemy* in both [The Edge or\
Reason] and [Ice Field of Clearsight]. This if further made difficult by
useless minimap and fog obstructing your view (so much for clearsight).

- There are 31 enemies in [The Edge or Reason] and 29 enemies in [Ice Field of\
Clearsight]. If you stay in one area for long time, enemies eventually start to
respawn. So how will you know when to quit if by chance you lose count or are
too late? I will offer some advice on how to help yourself.

- In [The Edge or Reason] following enemies appear:
  - 1x Giruveganus
  - 5x Behemoth - from A to E
  - 9x Preying Mantis - from A to I
  - 16x Basilisk - from A to P

- In [Ice Field of Clearsight] following enemies appear:
  - 2x Behemoth - from A to B
  - 15x Preying Mantis - from A to O
  - 12x Basilisk - from A to L

- So for example, for [Ice Field of Clearsight] make a checklist with enemies
names like this: Behemoth A, Behemoth B; Preying Mantis A... all the way to
Preying Mantis O; and Basilisk A... all the way to Basilisk L. When you are
ready, enter the area and start sistematically scouting the area for enemies -
make sure you check them out to see enemy's name and then tick off its name off
the list. So if you happen to run into Basilisk M, you will know you have been
in the area too long and enemies have started to respawn.

- Begin the slaying of enemies in [The Edge or Reason], then continue in [Ice\
Field of Clearsight]. Once you are done, return to [The Edge or Reason] and
look for mark to prowl near S edge of the area.

------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv71
Cast Protect, Shell, Regen, Bubble, Faith, Haste and Bravery on yourself before
going further. Take care to renew your protective buffs when they wear off.
King is immune to all negative statuses, so no help from them this time.
Bubble is very important to maintain in the battle, so that you void potential
Disease from King's rephys - equip Black Mask to absorb Darkga's damage, and
cycle between equipment when other element magics are used. Keeping chrs spread
out will ensure one (or two at most) is hit at a time. For White Breath's
danger of Stop it's better to arrange Chronos Tear gambit.
Dispel King of its buffs and start the assault. King is much the same as Fafnir
was, except that it has more HP, even stronger attacks, and a few more spells
at its disposal. King's element spells will hit you for about 1200 damage and
Ardor for 1500 - toss some Shear and Expose techs its way to increase damage
potential you can do, as it will come in handy soon. Fow whole battle King has
Return Damage active, and Spellspring ensures it'll never run out of MP.
Remove Slow with Hastega, and keep chrs spread apart to not get all of them in
Stop at one fell swoop, otherwise it will spell the end for your party. After
losing half HP, King will use Greater Barrier (and gain stupid Damage Resist),
followed shortly by Paling, and when Paling wears off, Magick Shield goes up -
it will alternate between the two.
While Paling is in effect, use spells to inflict some serious damage on the
bastard, and use physicals with Magick Shield active. After losing half HP
King's spells gain insta-cast time, so be doubly careful; since King has some
big spells on its disposal, that means you'll often run into spell lag, which
can be both great and bad. Great if you're at full health and you're getting
bombed with Holy or Ardor, and bad if you're KOed, but your Arise is in spell
queue and you're scrambling all possible resources. This battle is one of the
times when having a decent levels for reserve chrs can save your bacon.

- Report back to receive 250 gil (!) and 2x Bacchus' Wine (!!!). What the heck,
mate!? Relax... listen to man's story. Does it strike a resemblance to
something you have already seen? There is a rock which resembles a wyrm in
Bur-Omisace, so warp there.

MT BUR-OMISACE town
===============================================================================

- Enter [Temple Approach] and look for 'Wyrm Snout' rock. Examine the spot and

===============================================================================
HENNE MINES dungeon
===============================================================================

[Henne Mines / Staging Shaft]

- Travel N and *make sure* you save your game, as there is no save point before
Zodiark battle.

[Henne Mines / Ore Separation]

- Travel E.

[Henne Mines / Phase 2 Dig]

- Enemies here are lv64, so they are quite hard - but they do provide good EXP,
so it is worth your while to spend some time here building up your levels. Go
as far E as you can and check in the corner of the room for the Urn holding
Henne Candle, which reveals the rest of the map of [Henne Mines].

- Along W edge you can come across the point of interest 'Discarded Paper',
read it and you will get a hint about some discarded treasure. The hint is very
vague at best, and the loot it refers to is located in [Special Charter Shaft].

- Also in this area you can find Zodiac Spear. You must have Diamond Armlet
equipped when you examine the treasure. Coming from the entrance of [Ore\
Separation] it appears in a second invisible side room (by invisible I mean
that it doesn't show up on the map). Good luck getting it - treasure has 10%
chance of spawning and instead of Zodiac Spear you can end up with Elixir or
some gil - essentially your chances of getting Zodiac Spear are 0,1%.

- Other great finds in this area include Brave Suit, Gold Hairpin, Platinum
Dagger and Ring of Renewal - move on to S exit.

[Henne Mines / Crossover C]

- Travel to SW exit.

[Henne Mines / Pithead Junction C]

- Take S exit.

[Henne Mines / Phase 2 Shaft]

- Travel thru enemy hordes to E exit.

[Henne Mines / Special Charter Shaft]

- LOT of undead prowl this section. Great finds in this area include
Ensanguined Shield, Lordly Robes, Sage's Ring, Judicer's Staff, Brave Suit,
Renewing Morion, Ribbon (3rd opportunity for a Ribbon) and Fomalhaut.

- If you go all the way to the top and reach the dead end, you will see a
sparkle on the ground. Examine it and you will obtain 3x Bacchus' Wine and 2x
Megalixir - this was the loot talked about in 'Discarded Paper'.

------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv73
Zodiark battle is broken down in four stages.
1st: Zodiark's HP is between 100% and 80%
2nd: Zodiark's HP is between 80% and 50%
3rd: Zodiark's HP is between 50% and 20%
4th: Zodiark's HP is lower than 20%

Equipment you wear has direct effect on the battle. Here Demon Shield and Black
Mask are two equips that alter flow of battle. Zodiark does not use Banish Ray
if all battling chrs absorb dark damage through equips I mentioned before. If
Zodiark cannot use Banish Ray, this causes Darkja to be used sooner. And it
also gains passive ability Regular Attack CT = 0.

Darkja is tipically followed in four commands by Banish Ray, but again, only if
at least one chr doesn't absorb dark. Darkja's usage comes as following:
1st: after every 20 commands (16 commands if Banish Ray isn't used)
2nd: after every 14 commands (regardless of Banish Ray)
3rd: after every 16 commands (7 commands if Banish Ray isn't used)
4th: after every 8 commands (regardless of Banish Ray)

Banish Ray may also randomly be used in 2nd and 4th stage against chr that
doesn't absorb dark. In 1st and 3rd stage you can also count how many attacks
Zodiark used and just before Darkja should be used, switch dark absorbing
equipment out to sucker it into shooting Banish Ray - before you're hit,
quickly put dark absorbing equip back on. If this happens, it takes additional
8-14 attacks (that is how much I observed) before Darkja is cast. And be
advised, it may also not always work in suckering Banish Ray this way.

Zodiark gains Paling in 4th stage. After it wears off in 2 minutes, it gets
almost immediately renewed. Almost as in - if Zodiark is charging an action
(Scathe for example) as soon as Paling goes, it'll be vulnerable for few
moments until Scathe's animation goes off, and then regain Paling. Also, as
Zodiark enters 4th stage, it won't gain Paling immediately. It has to go thru
Shift and Battle Cry animations, so you can get few hits in before that
happens.

I already explained about Regular Attack CT = 0 (can't use Banish Ray, etc...),
but what about Magic CT = 0? Until Zodiark casts Faith on itself for the first
time, it'll have this passive ability. In any case, Zodiark gains both
abilities in 3rd stage when it uses Limit Break.

Now let's talk about that stupid Magick Shield. You probably didn't know that,
but never ever use Dispel or Dispelga against Zodiark. If you do, it'll start
using Magick Barrier as soon as 2nd stage after it puts Faith on itself.
Magick Barrier will wear off after 2 minutes or if Zodiark feels the need to
cast something on self (like Faith if it wore off). Magick Barrier does NOT get
renewed as long as you refrain from using Dispel or Dispelga.

It is possible to use Nihopalaoa's Hi-Ether on Zodiark to drain its MP so it
can't use Lv. spells, but it's only good for 1st stage, as Mana Spring is used
pretty soon.

When you're in 4th stage, you're facing Zodiark with Paling, Reflect, Faith and
Bravery on, with Darkja incoming every 8 turns. A deadly combination, but it is
recommended not to use Dispel on him. In addition to triggering Magick Shield
you will also trigger Darkja sooner - as fast as after next four attacks after
it's been last used. Okay, so you manage to Dispel it and its buffs, it puts up
Magick Shield, throws Darkja and then removes Magick Barrier because it'll
start buffing himself up again.

Faith increases Darkja's chances to KO you from 50% to 75% base chance, but you
can reduce that to 37% (or 25% even, if Zodiark isn't under Faith) by equipping
Shell Shield or being under Shell. As for blocking Scathe - it is made quite
easy with Aegis Shield and Gauntlets.

To defeat Zodiark in last stage, consider using Scathe Motes you have laying
around, or equip Opal Ring and throw Bio or Scourge in its direction (Flare and
Scathe also work, but I don't like their long animations). Additionally Reflect
all three chrs (Mirror Mail), give one Opal Ring and command him or her to spam
Curaja on your party, while other two cast Bio or Scourge on the party as well
thus blasting Zodiark three times.

Congratulations - you have obtained Zodiark, Keeper of Precepts.
-------------------- CONGRATULATIONS! YOU ARE VICTORIOUS! ---------------------

- You now have the ability to summon Zodiark! Not too shabby, huh? Defeating
Zodiark also removes the wreckage on S end of [Phase 2 Shaft] where exit to
Feywood is, also allowing you to operate 'Gate Switchboard' nearby if it is
blue (if 'Gate Switchboard's are on red state, you won't be able to operate
this one). Take the other door into [Crossover C].

Pharos - First Ascent / They Who Thirst Not; Save 18, RDMC.
------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv74
Come into battle with Protect, Shell, Haste, Bravery and Bubble on your chrs.
Take care to renew your protective buffs when they wear off. Dispel Hydro's
Haste if it's in effect and consider your next options. Checking status
affinities we see that only Confuse, Sap and Oil work on it. But since boss is
also undead, it is vulnerable to healing magic so we shall employ Reflect-THIS!
strategy. Once all of your chrs including Reddas are under Reflect, start
spamming Curaja on yourself and watch Hydro get plastered twelve times.
Since you're abusing magic, Fearga is likely to be used - this skill takes off
95% of target's MAX HP, essentially making it a sitting duck. Use Charge to
quickly recover some lost MP and start Curaja cycle over again.
With 40% HP lost Hydro gains more powah and begins to ignore EVA making your
shields useless, but keep that Demon Shield in place to absorb damage from
Darkra. Be on the lookout for Sonic Fangs and Crushing Fangs, as both can
inflict KO when you least expect it.
As for accessory I recommend Bowline Sash to null Confuse - other statuses you
may get are easily curable with respective magic, but cure Doom at very last
moment.
As Hydro is left with only 30% HP, it loses many of its attacks and is left
with Bio, Darkra and regular physical attack... as a countermeasure it can now
execute all those attacks instantly, and will get progressively more and more
successful at chaining a lot of combos.
Unlike most other bosses it doesn't gain any real dangerous PA when in critical
HP except for physicals hitting stronger. That gives you the edge you need to
finish it off with some well-placed Curaja spells or just good ol' physicals.
-------------------- CONGRATULATIONS! YOU ARE VICTORIOUS! ---------------------

- After battle walk E for a scene.

- Now you're really inside Pharos and victory fanfare for introducing the first
climbing play. You would do well to pay attention to all Carven Pillars you see
and remember the crap they spew or just read on for further information.

- On your long climb thru the tower, you will sometimes have to open a door
with colored symbol on it. Remember the order of the colors well, for you will
need them to solve final Pharos puzzle.

[Pharos - First Ascent / The Wellspring]

- GCR is inside on NW corner as well as nonfunctional 'Way Stone' and you start
at F01. Around the central area you can find 'Altar of Night', three in total.
They have a place for something to be inserted. Take a look at the map and you
will see that central circle is broken up in three sections, each being
connected with [Wellspring Labyrinth]. If you read 'Carven Pillars' around the
area, they will tell you that you need Black Orbs dropped from enemies around
the area. So your task is to go around and kill foes - sometimes a black pearl
will rise from the ground on the spot where a foe was killed. Approach this
pearl and press Action to obtain Black Orb. To get further, you need to collect
at least 3. Take the exit S from 'Way Stone'.

[Pharos - First Ascent / Wellspring Labyrinth]

- Map of the dungeon can be found in S part of F01 inside the Urn. Once you
gather at least 3 Orbs, you need to insert them into three 'Altar of Nights'
(one pearl per altar). Altars are found inside the circle area in [The\
Wellspring] (one altar in SE section, one in W, and one in N). When all pearls
are inserted (choose 'Use a black orb.' option to insert it into the altar),
you can take E exit called 'Threshold of Night' to next area (choose second
option to open the door). Remember the color of the emblem on the door!

[Pharos - First Ascent / Dunes of Profaning Wind]

- Approach the farthest stone to trigger next boss battle.

Pharos - First Ascent / Dunes of Profaning Wind; Save 19,RDMC.
------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv74
Protect, Shell, Haste, Bravery and Bubble on your chrs, and as for equipment -
have Goggle Mask to be immune to Blind, and Fuzzy Miter to guard against
Petrify. Even though boss has Null VIT, you can cast Shell on yourself to have
50% less chance for boss to hit you with status effects. Take care to renew
your protective buffs when they wear off. Dispel Panda of its buffs and throw a
look at status affinities - Confuse, Silence and Oil doesn't make a jump-for-
joy gesture. Have some shields with good EVA equipped and start bashing away at
Panda (if you wield element weapons, have 'pipce' with wind element). Or use
Reflect-THIS! strategy and bounce Aeroga at Panda's ass.
After losing 20% HP Panda's regular attack becomes twice as strong thanks to HP
Devour, so don't get too cocky - if you get spinned with Slow, counter it with
Haste. When we reach 50% HP lost, Perfect Defense will go up. I bash my head
against the wall trying to understand why I cannot steal during this stage. I
mean, is Steal considered a physical attack or what? Stone Gaze and Flash are
not used for the moment, so expect damaging moves only. Anyway, after two
minutes are gone, Panda's protective shields are gone and it can be hurt again.
Boss now ignores EVA making your shields useless, so consider equipping some
2Hweapons with higher attack. HP Devour is also gone, but Damage Resist is
gained instead. Reflecting Aeroga is still the best course to victory. Should
you insist on fair battle, know that Panda will be using skills most of the
time and it can combo up to phenomenal 11hits.
Insignificant increase in physical damage will not pose much of a threat in
reducing final 20% of boss' HP.
-------------------- CONGRATULATIONS! YOU ARE VICTORIOUS! ---------------------

Pharos - First Ascent / Marsh of Profaning Wind; Save 20,RDMC.
------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv75
Slyt is an interesting fella - I killed Reddas before entering the stage, and
switched out Fran and Vaan. While Ashe was standing by her lonesome on small
dry piece of land in the middle (I wonder if she was waiting for so(me)body to
take her on a date), all Slyt ever did was circle around her, never attacking.
I used Dispel to rid Slyt of Haste, and then I used NihoRem to inflict it with
Confuse, Disease, Slow and Oil, finishing it up by lighting a bonfire under its
ass by spamming Firaga. Since Slyt was hovering above water ground, damage done
was 6999, but that is a small sacrifice to pay.
Come into battle with Protect, Haste and Bubble, and take care to renew your
protective buffs when they wear off. Sometimes Slyt becomes smart enough to
come after the attacker, in which case it may possibly leave water ground and
be hovering above ground only. When it does that, it will lose most of PA
(which are usually in effect when Slyt is above water ground). However if Slyt
moves back above water ground, it uses Enrage again and regains Regen, if you
used Dispel to remove it. Disease status will prevent Slyt regaining any HP,
though.
When it loses 50% HP, it will inflict more damage with physicals, but otherwise
it doesn't gain any other PA. Keep up the assault with reflected Firaga or
using fire weapons and Slyt falls before long.
-------------------- CONGRATULATIONS! YOU ARE VICTORIOUS! ---------------------

Pharos - Second Ascent / Cleft of Profaning Wind; Save21,RDMC.
------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv75
Come into battle with Protect, Shell, Haste, Bravery and Bubble on your chrs,
then cast Dispel to remove Fenrir's buffs. Take care to renew your protective
buffs when they wear off. Checking status affinites we see that you can put it
to Sleep and Oil, but fire magic is ineffective. In fact all element magic is
useless against Fenrir, except earth... and as luck would have it, there are
only earth based weapons. Use NihoRem on Fenrir to put it to Sleep and perform
an Oilslick, but you may also want to use several Shear attacks to make it more
vulnerable to magic damage.
Instead you shall use Reflect-THIS! strategy once more and spam Bio on your
chrs under Reflect. You will want to get rid of Reddas or else he will
constantly mess up your attempts to keep Fenrir asleep.
Battle begins by kitty using Wail which does some good damage and inflicts
Blind and Silence (Goggle Mask and Rose Corsage equipment will make you
immune). Other good attacks you can look forward to is Ice Break and boss'
likelihood to comboslice you many times. Unlike bosses before, a good shield
with high EVA will keep you safe from harm for most of the battle (Fenrir never
gains Null EVA), so pop Decoy on that tank of yours and watch Fenrir hit it
rather unsuccessfully. As a physical fighter Fenrir will parry your attacks a
lot, as well as counter them often, so be on the lookout and keep Curaja gambit
rolling.
When you remove half HP, Fenrir uses Wail again and then casts Bravery. Remove
this status immediately because I assure you that you don't want to get hit in
the face by constant barrage. Wail is now used after each 10 commands,
following with Bravery after each two Wails. Smite of Rage will deal big damage
but only strikes once so no biggie there.
Once we drift into critical HP stage, cat only gains the ability to execute
regular physicals instantly. But being low on HP also increases its chances to
successfully chain attacks together, thus ripping you a new one. Make sure this
doesn't happen by keeping it asleep and blasting it with Bio or using Gil Toss
a couple of times.
If you had minimap sealed while climbing this stage of Pharos, you have all
battle options available. Sealing Attack command as well as items will have no
serious harm to your battle plans. Sealing magic won't give you a chance to
mass-spam Bio, but you still have your techs, items and Attack command
available. If by chance you have Reflectga Mote in items, use that and follow
it up with Scathe Mote.
-------------------- CONGRATULATIONS! YOU ARE VICTORIOUS! ---------------------

[Pharos - Third Ascent / Spire Ravel - 1st Flight]

- F80 is start of next area. To get the map of this area, you need to make
wrong choice twice, for example pick 'Green Sigil' twice to be warped to F79.
Here seek out the Urn and open it to obtain map of [Third Ascent], then engage
the various undead bozos and keep killing them until the door is unsealed. If
you read the pillars around here, they tell you hints about how to touch the
glyphs (or if you recall the color order from the doors you were opening...).
Check 'Black Sigil' found on NW corner and pick first choice to be baleeted to
F81.

- F81 - Go to SE corner, and you will get the option of smashing 'Fool's
Facade'. Do it and there's 'Green Sigil' (there is another 'Fool's Facade' to N
of this 'Green Sigil'). Pick first choice to be baleeted to F83.

[Pharos - Third Ascent / Spire Ravel - 2nd Flight]

- F83 - Go in either corridor and smash thru two 'Fool's Facade' walls to reach
next sigil batch. Fiddle with 'Red Sigil' and pick first choice to be baleeted
to F84.

- F84 - Fiddle with pink 'Sigil of Sacrifice' (reason: we sealed minimap while
we were climbing in second leg of our journey). Pick first choice to be
baleeted to F86. If you sealed weapons, touch white sigil; if you sealed items,
touch yellow sigil; and if you sealed magic, touch purple sigil.

- F86 - Go N and smash thru fake wall, then find 'Way Stone' inside (the hint
on 'Carven Pillar' is babbling about something colorless and this 'Way Stone'
has no color, making it the one you need to touch). Pick first choice to be
baleeted to F88.

- F88 - Beware - boarding 'Dais of Ascendance' will thrust you into next boss
battle, so make sure you cast Protect, Shell, Haste, Bravery and Bubble on your
chrs before entering. Once you are ready, get on lift and make your way to F90.

------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv76
NTSC-U/C version: How can it punch things with that stuff on arms? It's
probably imaginary. Cast Dispel to remove Hashmal's Protect and the stage is
set. Immediately bash Hash with few attacks to eliminate its attack bonus with
full HP and then stop for a while. Let's take a look at status affinities...
Oil only, and it's immune to fire damage at that.
Hash begins with crapload of PA on it, and the ones of interest to me is that
you will face lots of counters during battle. Prior to battle equip Dragon
Shield to nullify damage from Roxxor and Quakeja (or cast Float during battle,
though I prefer Dragon Shield), then wear Bubble Belt for immunity to Disease
from physicals - and as for Slow from Quakeja... that can be fixed quickly with
Haste. Even though boss has Null VIT, you can cast Shell on yourself to have
50% less chance for boss to hit you with status effects.
With 20% HP gone say hello to rocks and Roxxor. Don't you know that people in
glass houses shouldn't throw stones? Don't underestimate Hash as it can combo
quite often and it deals good damage with that. You could resort to using
Reflect-THIS! strategy and bounce Aeroga magic on Hash for some quick removal
of HP.
When half HP is gone, Hash gets to hit harder with physicals and will begin
using Quakeja. Now both Roxxor and Quakeja will take sixteen commands before
being used again, making this for a rather relaxed battle. Remember to remain
healed as Hash punches through your defenses. If you don't have Bubble Belt or
Bubble magic, do remain alert if you get affected by Disease and cure it
quickly. In critical stages Hash's ATT and MAG increase to keep you on your
toes. Keep pinching down Hash's HP until it falls defeated.
NTSC-J version: The battle is quite different than US version. Come into battle
with Protect, Shell, Haste, Bravery and Bubble. Hash begins by casting Haste,
to which you should respond by casting Dispel to remove that and Protect. With
20% HP lost Roxxor comes rolling in your direction, then again after next four
attacks. Unlike US version, boss cannot combo its physicals.
When Hash loses half HP, it will fortify itself with Haste and Protect once
again, then follow up with Quakeja. Remove Slow inflicted and keep wailing on
boss to bring down its HP. Roxxor and Quakeja are now used after each eight
commands.
With only 20% HP left to go, Hash uses last ditch effort by Perfect Defense,
making itself immune to any harm. The effects gained are gone as soon as boss
uses Quakeja, making this a rather silly move to use. Remove final HP reserves
and you win.
-------------------- CONGRATULATIONS! YOU ARE VICTORIOUS! ---------------------

- You gain the ability to summon Hashmal, and that makes 12 espers so far.

------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv76
If you didn't buff yourself prior battle, cast Protect, Haste, Bravery and
Bubble on your chrs, then Dispel Judge's buffs and stage is set. Main villain
is boss, and my girls are damsels in distress. Take care to renew your
protective buffs when they wear off.
Checking status affinities we see that only things that work are Oil and
Silence, and since our friend doesn't have any element affinities at all, you
can light it up quite nicely with reflected Firaga. Yes, Reflect-THIS! strategy
works out great in this battle.
If you're Knight of the Round, such cheap tactics are probably not in your
repertoire, so you will want to dispose of Judge in honest way. Know that
Judge's attacks can be blocked, so a good shield will stop many attacks.
Before he loses 50% HP, you're looking at mostly single target attacks, with
Circle of Judgment sometimes mixed inbetween.
At half HP lost a small scene plays, then battle continues with boss regaining
Haste and all bad statuses gone from him. Magick Shield will envelop the boss,
protecting him from magical harm. He'll immediately chuck Guilt (used again
after each 12 commands) and he loses Lunge and Kick, so now he'll be using
mostly specials. Don't let him chain up too much attacks on single chr, so move
your Curaja gambit on higher scale than usual. For now rely on physicals and
defeat him.
If you don't manage to defeat it before Magick Shield wears off, I suggest that
you reapply Oil (NihoRem) and shoot few more Firaga spells to finish him off.
Battle ends when Judge enters critical HP.
-------------------- CONGRATULATIONS! YOU ARE VICTORIOUS! ---------------------

- After short intermezzo (enter Swan Lake here) it's action time again.

------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv76
Cast Protect, Haste, Bravery and Bubble on your chrs, then Dispel Doctor's
buffs and... hm, where is Famfrit? It'll appear in due time - patience, young
padawan.
Okies, let us see intelligence on status affinities... Oil, and Oil again???
Won't do you much good against Doctor, but Fam's weakness is fire so it'll work
out nicely when it appears. Take care to renew your protective buffs when they
wear off, and wear Rose Corsage when Fam enters the fray.
As battle begins, not much is going on - boss will use only regular physical
attack until he loses 20% HP. Use the time to chuck few Expose attacks on
boss' ass so you can deal more punishment. Once you poke his HP bar over the
20% HP lost limit, Gatling Gun is used and you should equip Flame Shield to
halve the damage - next Gatling Gun is incoming in 20 commands, but by then you
will dish out more damage to Doctor, forcing him over half HP lost.
Now a small scene will play with Famfrit entering the battlefield. Doctor's
buffs get renewed, so take care to Dispel Fam, then use NihoRem on Fam to Oil
it (Dispel currently won't work on Doctor). If you have Viking Coat, equip it
to be immune to water, thus making Briny Cannonade and Waterja useless.
With Fam out Paling and Magick Shield surround the main boss. Even when they
wear off 2 minutes later, they immediately get renewed... so your task is set -
Fam must die! You can either employ Reflect-THIS! strategy and bounce off
Firaga spell, or use fire based weaponry. Latter may be more preferred, as
couple Firagas could bounce onto Doctor, and with two foes pounding on you,
healing with X-Potions may not be quick enough.
Doctor uses Cyclotrone after each 20 commands he makes, so be on the lookout.
If you Dispel Fam of its buffs, Doctor may sometimes waste a turn to chuck
Haste, Protect or Shell on Fam - in this case just Dispel Fam again.
When Fam loses 20% HP, it begins using Briny Cannonade, and Waterja after half
HP lost. Both attacks have 12 commands range before they're used again. Keep
pouring Firagas in Fam's jar until it loses all HP and falls in defeat. Yes,
yes, getting drunk will do that to you.
With his support gone, it doesn't take long for Doctor's protection to
dissipate. Remove his buffs if they're still present. He gains a crapload of PA
(look into intelligence above) but that shouldn't worry you as most PA he gains
are not really needed for him. Attack+, DEF, MAG and ATT increase when in
critical HP, Return Damage and higher counter chances are the only ones worth
mentioning. Take note that Doctor will alternate between his bigass attacks
after each 20 commands, so don't take too long to defeat him.
-------------------- CONGRATULATIONS! YOU ARE VICTORIOUS! ---------------------

- You gain the ability so summon Famfrit. And thus is your esper collection
complete! Afterwards save your game when prompted.

- Go talk to Rikken and speak with him twice, and he'll offer you a bit of
sport. You must accept his challenge in racing him, Raz and that bombshell of
Elza. Doesn't matter if you win or lose - at the end of race he will spill his
guts on the bill he posted. Accept it and the hunt is on!

FOO(L)TRACE QUEST

- Yay, another way to waste your time! You need to complete Pharos and your
clan rank must be Riskbreaker - after you come to Rikken to accept Pylraster
hunt from him, he'll ask you if you're up for some sports challenge. Sure, why
not?

- You will be racing against Rikken, Raz and that Elza the Bombshell. The goal
is to alternate pressing between X and Circle buttons rhythmically and make it
to the finish line. I didn't really bother by any strategic movement along the
lines of blocking opponents, instead I focused on button pressing and just
before finish line started pressing a bit faster to ensure victory.

------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv76
Equip Bubble Belts and cast maybe Protectga only. I had my chrs get KOed at
least 20 times in this battle. Pyl's buffs are swiftly removed with Dispel.
Then it is brawler time - begin trading blows with Pyl (whenever it lands a
successful blow, Pyl takes as much dmg as it caused to your chr), having Arise
and Curaja/Renew gambits in place. Launch few Expose and Shear techs to lower
Pyl's resistance (depends if you're going in for physical or magic assault).
Crushing Fangs have KO chance or big damage (if KO fails). Screwtail is small
area damage, but Ram can hurt for up to 8000 damage. This isn't the worst yet,
though - once Pyl smokes 50% HP, it will use Growing Threat to become lv99 and
thus having much better stats. Beware of Rage area attack, and its attacks are
way stronger now, it combos a lot, and its resilience improves when very low on
HP. Equip Gungnir weapons to deal substantial damage to Pyl until it falls.
The easiest way to fall this beast is in the fact that it doesn't have Null EVA
and as such you can have tank with Decoy, best shield and Main Gauche block
most of Pyl's attacks. While Pyl is busy trying to hit the tank, other two chrs
move in behind its back and start delivering justice to the target.
-------------------- CONGRATULATIONS! YOU ARE VICTORIOUS! ---------------------

-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-= ASHE'S POSTCARD COLLECTION No.49
Subterra

This is subterranean section of the Pharos tower, and this here makes it a very
boring description again.

ASHE'S POSTCARD COLLECTION No.49 =-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-

- This part of Pharos is available only after completing the events on top of
Pharos.

- WARNING! THE MAP PORTION CALLED "ABYSSAL" HAS A TREASURE POT WITH CIRCLET
ACCESSORY, LOCATED IN SOUTH PART. Only one other pot containing Circlet exists
in the game, so you have two chances to obtain Circlet.

[Pharos - Subterra / Penumbra - Interior]

- Note that minimap goes ballistic. Now pay attention - around these parts you
have highly challenging enemies and they can quickly swarm your party. Ixion
can appear on any of the floors Penumbra, Umbra or Abyssal. There is a small
twist to where he appears.

- Penumbra, Umbra and Abyssal floors each have four side rooms (NE, NW, SE and
SW) as well as central circular room. These sections are called 'Interior',
'South' (SE and SW rooms) and 'North' (NE and NW rooms). Unknown floor can be
accessed only one time, when you are on a hunt for Shadowseer.

- Currently you can only travel to Penumbra... so how to open the path deeper
down? If you go to any of side rooms, you will find 'Pedestal of Night' inside
(four pedestals per floor). You need to feed them Black Orbs in order to
illuminate the surroundings - once all 4 pedestals have enough Black Orbs, the
elevator can travel deeper. DO NOT OVERFEED the pedestals or your Black Orbs
will be wasted. You can get Black Orbs by defeating enemies in these side
rooms, and you get to killing part by checking walls of side rooms and look for
doors you can open and 'Fool's Facade' walls that you can destroy. If you run
into Phoenix, look just a bit below for strategy on how to beat its ass.

- In addition, treasures on these floors hold many a great one. Here is where I
snatched my first Ribbon (Ribbon is obtained in [Abyssal - North] in NW room;
this makes your 5th chance to get a Ribbon), and you can get Lordly Robes and
Deathbringer among other things. If you run into Magick Pot, stay your ground.
Switch off your gambits so chrs don't attack it by accident. Get close to it
and it will beg for Elixir. Before you do so, I suggest eliminating any and all
resistance in neighboring rooms. When ready, feed it one Elixir. It will become
happy and start prancing around. Give chase and opt to kill it as swiftly as
you can, before other enemies have a chance to respawn. You can steal Elixir
back from Magick Pot, and it drops 123 LP when you kill it.

- Here is amount of Black Orbs you need per floor.
  Penumbra - 18 for NE, 9 for NW, 3 for SE, 6 for SW
  Umbra - 15 for NE, 9 for NW, 15 for SE, 18 for SW
  Abyssal - 15 for NE, 21 for NW, 27 for SE, 12 for SW
  Unknown - no Black Orbs needed, Phoenix must be slain if you wish access

- Sometimes you will find a Massive Black Orb, which is bigger than usual ones.
If you manage to bag that one, you will get up to 99 Black Orbs (even though
the counter will sometimes say that you obtained say 150 Black Orbs, 99 is the
maximum you can get). Now, back to our hunt.

- Your aim is to fight Ixion on [Abyssal] instead of [Penumbra] or [Umbra], as
it will have only 166559 HP instead of 306559 HP, should you choose to fight it
on earlier floors.

- Keep traveling between Abyssal and [Pharos - First Ascent / The Wellspring]
areas until Ixion pops up in [Pharos - Subterra / Abyssal - Interior]. You will
know so by there not being any enemies around. Ixion's spawn chances increase
by 6% every 12 seconds you spend in the area, reaching 100% after 204 seconds.

------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv77
Cast Protect, Shell, Regen, Bubble, Faith, Haste and Bravery on yourself - take
care to renew your protective buffs when they wear off. Checking status
affinities and considering our options, you can put a number of stuff on it -
Slow, Silence, Oil and Sap.
Equip best armor you have or Rubber Suit to block Ixion's thunder based rephys,
wield Holy Lances to exploit holy weakness, Dispel mark's buffs and then
Silence it. For acc give two chrs Ruby Ring and third chr Opal Ring, then
assign the latter to the healing duty (always keep him/her under Reflect).
Ixion has Return Damage so you'll be taking 5% of the damage inflicted as well
- add some Expose techs to the mix. Due to Silence Ixion will be using only
physicals until it hits 50% lost. Then it uses Purify to remove Silence and
envelops itself in White Wind, followed with Magick Shield.
Mark now begins to use many magic spells and you need to look out for Curse and
Fearga (have Charge gambit set), while elemental spells will get reflected back
to mark. Reapply Silence is fruitless as Purify and White Wind will follow
immediately, as is trying to rely on magic due to Magick Shield which is added
after following the successful magic hit. Equip Nishijin Belt to be Sleep
immune in Sleepga ordeals, and you may need to sometimes use Echo Herbs to
remove Silence in case everybody gets affected - Smelling Salts will save you
from Curse's Confuse.
When it's in critical HP, defensive power increases and I still recommend you
put up with bashing it up with physicals. None of marks magic spells are used
anymore, it will be poking you with rephys exclusively. Have two chrs be
healers in case loss of HP proves too much for one healer and soon Ixion
returns to the planet.
-------------------- CONGRATULATIONS! YOU ARE VICTORIOUS! ---------------------

- Report back and receive 3000 gil, Sapping Bolts and Ragnarok. Return to this
area afterwards.

- When you are back in [Penumbra - Interior], floor it for NE room.

[Pharos - Subterra / Penumbra - North]

- Poke around the side walls and keep making your way further, until you find
one more door to open. Once you do, Phoenix will greet you on other side.

------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv78
Protect, Shell, Haste, Bravery and Bubble on your chrs, Dispel on Seer and
start hacking away. This will be a difficult battle, but at first it doesn't
appear so. I recommend to have following equipment - White Mask, Black Mask,
Demon Shield and Aegis Shield.
When battle starts, have White Mask and Demon Shield to absorb damage from
Darkness and Shining Ray. Rephy here and there... once you knock off 20% of
mark's HP, he becomes immune to everything and will begin calling in allies for
aid.
First one is Pandaemonium, then Slyt, then Fenrir, and finally Phoenix. Once
Panda falls, Slyt appears and so on, until you kill Phoenix. These guys use the
same attacks as before, except that they have a little less HP. While you are
busy fending off Seer's helpers, he will be casting Dispelga to remove your
buffs and meddle your chrs with Slowga, Immobilizega, Darkga, Fearga, Invert
and Curse. It's wise idea to keep chrs spread out so that only one gets hit at
a time.
When Panda hits 50% HP lost, it will erect Perfect Defense for 2 minutes
(boring); Slyt is easy to get rid of, as is Fenrir - but be quick in casting
Dispel on Phoenix to remove Bravery. Once Phoenix falls, Seer's immunities are
thing of the past and he can be hurt again.
Seer's attacks change a bit now - Holy, Shock, Scourge, Flare and Scathe, with
old addition of Darkness and Shining Ray. Now's the time to don Aegis Shield,
Sage's Ring and Black Mask. Seer's defenses and attack power grow stronger as
it nears defeat, but that is nothing to worry about since you have the chances
to block many of his attacks. Keep up the assault and you win.
-------------------- CONGRATULATIONS! YOU ARE VICTORIOUS! ---------------------

- Report back to receive 20000 gil and 2x Megalixir.

klam75 submitted following strategy:
I did the fight three times, just to try different strategies (always in one
sitting, and the best time was 2 hours & 15 minutes. I only used four people
for the fight with the following equips:

Ashe: lv99 with Dueling Mask, Maximillian, Tournesol
Basch: lv99 with Dueling Mask, Maximillian, Zodiac Spear
Penelo: lv99 with Crown of Laurels, Mirage Vest, Yagyu Darkblade
Vaan: lv94 with Crown of Laurels, Lordly Robes, Masamune

Ashe, Basch & Penelo were the main party, all equipped with Bubble Belts. Vaan
was in reserve with Protect, Haste, Bravery, Bubble & Berserk (no Shell, which
would reduce the chances of Berserk hitting). Everyone else with Protect, Shell
& Haste. In my first go around, I did have Bravery buffed on Penelo, so she
would hit for max damage with Darkblade, but when she got KOed, it seemed to
take forever for her to rebuff (damage difference wasn't that great anyway,
there were times she would hit the max anyway).

For main Party:

Foe: HP < 50000 -> Dark Matter (Fully Charged)
Ally: Status = KO -> Arise
Ally: Status = Stop -> Chronos Tear
Self: MP < 10% -> Charge (changed to Hi-Ether at end)
Ally: Status = Reflect -> Dispelga (Ashe only)
Ally: HP < 50% -> Curaja
Ally: Status = Petrify -> Gold Needle
Ally: Status = Sap -> Esunaga (only for Ashe & Penelo)
Ally: Any -> Protectga (Ashe only)
Ally: Any -> Shellga (Penelo Only)
Self -> Haste (All)
Foe: Highest HP -> Expose (Ashe & Basch, turned off when it missed)
Foe: Highest HP -> Attack

For Vaan Only:

Ally: Status = KO -> Arise
Ally: Status = Stop -> Chronos Tear
Ally: HP < 50% -> Curaja
Ally: Status = Petrify -> Gold Needle
Self -> Bubble
Self -> Haste
Self -> Bravery
Self -> Berserk
Foe: Any -> Attack

I cast Dispel on him first, and started to trip as many traps as I could (or at
least in the area I wanted to fight in, which is a tip from the Mark Hunting
Guide. In my first fight, I tripped a trap late and got hit with Reverse &
Disable).
I tried to spread the team out so they would be in range for Curaja & buffs,
but far enough where they wouldn't put under Stop by White Breath, kind of like
a triangle in front of him. Then let Ashe & Basch hit Yiazmat with Expose until
it missed, then turned the Expose gambit off.
After I got two bars off, I switched Basch for Vaan (who was fully buffed and
with Berserk). The idea was for Vaan to stay in long enough to do some major
damage. With Yiazmat's defense exposed all the way he was doing 9999 damage per
hit, for anywhere from 2-6 hit combos.
You could have Vaan at HP critical for faster speed & higher combos, but I
would have had to have someone else decoyed & reversed for this, and I wanted
to conserve MP. Once Vaan was KOed, I pulled him out & replaced him with Basch.
I used Arise on Vaan after he was switched out immediately. It might be notable
that Yiazmat ignored Vaan whenever he was rebuffing & concentrated only on
anyone who was attacking.
For the entire fight, I tried to switch armor to Windbreakers before Cyclone,
but you don't get much time to do that after you see 'Yiazmat readies Cyclone'.
Though if you are in the middle of a spell that requires some animation, it
will buy a couple of seconds to get to the party menu. Also, since I switched
off the Shellga gambit when Vaan was in (so I could increase chances of Berserk
hitting the first time), I would equip a Shell Shield to anyone when Yiazmat
would spam Deathstrike. True to the mechanics guide, Deathstrike only KOed
someone with Shell on about 1/2 the time.
It took about 1 1/2 to 1 3/4 hours to get him down to 10 bars this way, because
Vaan could take down a quarter bar at a clip if you get lucky with the amount
of combos he does. But then all hell broke loose, because Yiazmat started to KO
people with his regular attacks as well as Rake, and I got really unlucky with
Deathstrike hitting.
Also, once he reached HP Critical, Yiazmat will use Growing Threat to double
own level and huge combos for 1500 - 2000 (probably more than that) damage
started coming. Once I got him down to 5 bars, I was spamming Arise & Curaja
like a madman. Which is also where my MP was depleting rapidly (having
Hi-Ethers & Megalixirs help, but you could always Syphon off someone who isn't
a big magic user).
At this point you could either turn off all buffs, and keep an Arise & Attack
gambit or Decoy & Reverse two members, while your berserked Masamune user
attacks non-stop. I didn't have a whole lot of luck with either strategy, and
it took a while to get Yiazmat's health to the point where I could finish him
with a Dark Matter for 42,000 damage. Be careful of Yiazmat's last five bars -
it will cast Reflectga on your team, which you should Dispel immediately (in
case you're using Renew to heal yourself, switch to Curaja - it would be a real
bummer to recover all of mark's HP).
Again, there is a video on YouTube by Maltzsan, showing how to finish the last
1 1/2 bars with Decoy/Reverse on two members, and Vaan in HP Critical, Berserk,
with the Masamune. Having high levelled reserves definitely helps for the end,
so you can at least switch someone in to use Arise on fallen members, and be
able to take a hit or ten during it.
I don't have any great suggestions about the end of the fight, because this was
on par with taking on Omega, as far as people getting KOed & amount of damage
being done. Having the battle speed cranked to highest also helps throughout
the fight.
-------------------- CONGRATULATIONS! YOU ARE VICTORIOUS! ---------------------

- When Yiazmat falls, congratulate yourself on the battle well fought. Return
to Mont and he will give you 30000 gil and Godslayer's Badge. Let's kill the
final big foe Omega Mark XII! Go to Giruvegan and from there to Great Crystal.

------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv82
This bad boy can put up a serious challenge, but if you make things easy on
yourself, it will not take long to kick its metallic ass. Equip all chrs with
strongest weapons you have (but they must not be of elemental nature) and kit
them with Bubble Belt.
Arrange these four gambits for all characters:
Ally: Any -> Arise
Ally: Any -> Reverse
Ally: status = Berserk -> Dispel (optional)
Foe: nearest -> Attack
Before you approach Omega, switch gambits off on all chrs, then count how many
of those green glyphs there is before you make it to Omega's platform. Stand in
middle of 3rd farthest glyph from Omega's platform and turn gambits on. Once
Reverse is cast on all chrs, charge Omega's platform and just let your chrs
take care of everything. After about 10 minutes of hacking and slashing Omega
(kinda) explodes and leaves behind a loot bag.
-------------------- CONGRATULATIONS! YOU ARE VICTORIOUS! ---------------------

- And so the final big badass of FFXII falls before the might of my girls. DO
NOT FORGET TO PICK UP LOOT BAG AFTERWARDS TO COLLECT YOUR OMEGA BADGE. There is
a very low chance that it might also leave behind Mythril Sword, but don't
sweat it if it doesn't - sword is not worth the effort of going after Omega
again by reloading and retrying the battle.

- It is very difficult to reach final clan rank - Order of Ambrosia. To get it,
you need to fulfill following conditions:
  - obtain 1000000 clan points (heck, I had 10000000)
  - Sky Pirate's Den must be full
  - defeat all 45 marks

- Once you have all that, go to Rabanastre and see Mont in [Clan Hall], then
speak to him to receive following rewards:
- for Order of Ambrosia rank: Centurio Hero's Badge, 3x Teleport Stone

- Yeah, that's your *ultimate reward* for all that effort, a stinking badge.
You know what would be cool? If I could change all of those clan points for
gil... now that would really be something.

- Go to any merchant and sell off Omega Badge, Godslayer's Badge and Lu Shang's
Badge. This will cause Dragon Crest bazaar item to appear - cough up 65535 gil
(yep) and Wyrmhero Blade is yours. Sword itself isn't too shabby - 130 ATT with
holy element, 50% to EVA, 80% to combo, and gives Bravery and Faith. Two things
suck - it has 99 CT, and you obtain it after all the strongest enemies have
already been defeated. It's just too bad... *chucks Wyrmhero Blade in your
random direction*

- There is only one more dungeon to go until end of game. When you're done, go
to airship terminal, save your game, board Strahl and choose Bahamut as your
next destination. Take note that there is no save point inside Bahamut and once
you enter, you will not be able to return.

------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv99
Ah, round 2 - too bad it's his last! Let us look at his status affinities -
Slow, Silence and Blind. Excellent - apply NihoRem and watch his succumb to
darkness. Yoohoo, I'm over here! Take care to renew your protective buffs when
they wear off.
Have a good shield equipped and you will be able to block many of his attacks.
Spread your chrs out to avoid group punishment from Circle of Judgment. Keep up
the offensive until he loses 50% HP, at which time a scene will play.
When it's over, all negative statuses are removed and he regains Haste. Swiftly
remove it with Dispel, only to have Judge completely recover his HP. There is
really nothing you can do to prevent it, as he gained Magic CT = 0. Along with
this he now cuts all damage taken by 30% and will always hit you. Reapply
NihoRem to have a chance at his attacks being a miss.
Immediately after Renew he will squash you with Innocence (used after each 16
commands), but otherwise not much has changed until he loses half HP again. He
will use Enrage and seriously start bugging you with constant chains from his
physicals. As he can chain up to 12hits, move Curaja gambit higher on the
foodchain.
Within critical HP bounds both his ATT and DEF increase, so you may want to
wrap up the battle by some magic chucking or using Gil Toss. Hey, since you're
past the point of no return, what good will money do to you?
-------------------- CONGRATULATIONS! YOU ARE VICTORIOUS! ---------------------

- After the battle cast Protect, Shell, Haste, Bravery and Bubble on your chrs,
then operate 'Lift Controls' again.

------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv99
An unexpected turn of events will make this battle be four against one. The one
here is the boss, as for the 4th on your side, well... see for yourself.
Checking status affinities we see Slow, Blind and Sap, quickly fixed with
NihoRem. C'mon sucker, try to hit me now, hehe.
Still, don't underestimate him as he can put up a fight with long combos which
are surely to drain lot of chr's HP. Take care to renew your protective buffs
when they wear off.
When battle starts, use your tank with good shield to draw attention and to
block many of boss' attacks. Keep putting chunks of his HP away until he loses
50% HP. Small scene will play and when it ends, boss gains Haste buff. Dispel
it accordingly and eat up Mach Wave. Boss will now always hit you, so reapply
NihoRem to have a chance at him missing - in addition all damage done to him is
cut by 30%. Did I already say how much I hate that PA?
Keep bolting him until he enters critical HP range - this is when you say hi to
Force of Will. He will now alternate between Will and Wave after each 12
commands, so don't take too long in defeating him. Higher ATT and low HP make a
deadly combo when he chains lots of attacks together. Use Gil Toss or chuck
some magics as he doesn't halve or absorb anything.
You can also employ Reflect-THIS! strategy and end the fight rather quickly,
though you may still get to see Wave and Will used.
NTSC-J version: The only difference I noted was Mach Wave also being used while
boss' HP is between (50% > HP > 20%).
-------------------- CONGRATULATIONS! YOU ARE VICTORIOUS! ---------------------

- After initial battle is over, scene will play and you are thrust into next
battle immediately.

Take care to renew your protective buffs when they wear off, for they will be
quite important to maintain in this battle. Let's see about status affinities -
Slow and Oil, while Sephira is immune to everything. Novus' physicals can be
blocked thru whole battle, so have good shields equipped.
For now have Jackboots on to null Immobilize - before you start doing anything
to Novus, your objective will be to eliminate all Sephiras. Dispel your ally of
his status enhancements (you don't want him to push Novus' HP too much down)
and apply Protect and Shell to him, if either is missing.
Since Sephira doesn't do anything except regular attack, it will not take you
long to defeat them all - you may need to do a little bit of running around.
Each defeated Sephira will start to circle around Novus until all five are
gathered together. While you are killing them, Novus uses mainly physicals and
sometimes lv3 element spell to stir the situation.
Gettind rid of his cronies will disable Novus from using Crimson and Azure
Vortice, though it does grant him the ability to use bigass attacks more
frequently. Begin the assault on Novus and chip off first 20% of his HP to get
poked with Contempt.
At this time he uses Greater Barrier and strength of his physicals is
increased. Chuck Dispel to remove Protect and Shell and get ready for a small
scene when you shoot off 35% of his HP. When scene ends, boss regains status
buffs and is rid of Slow and Oil you put on it. Throw another Dispel
immediately and follow up with NihoRem - meanwhile you get blasted with
Inviolable Will, and then Novus uses Magick Barrier. Eh, even if you don't
succeed in Dispel attempt, do not worry - for the moment equip Mirror Mail or
Ruby Ring. Novus will be using magic attacks exclusively until he loses 80% HP
- but since we killed Sephiras you have to expect Will and Contempt alternating
after each 12 commands. Switch off gambits with magic healing and rearrange
them with X-Potions. Shoot Berserk on your ally and let him rip into Novus' HP
reserves, while you can do the same if you want. But I consider it more fun if
I let Novus blast itself with magic after Magick Shield wears off.
With critical HP Novus will now ready Tree of Sephira (one time bigass attack),
and follow it up with Limit Break - this allows him to use magic and regular
attacks instantly, so you will be facing quick barrages from him. His ATT also
increases, but DEF does not, so this is your lucky strike. Wail on him a couple
of more times and the fight is over.
-------------------- CONGRATULATIONS! YOU ARE VICTORIOUS! ---------------------

[Sky Fortress Bahamut / Cannon Superstructure]

- Unfortunately it is still not over. Gawrsh - brace yourself for final battle!

----------------------------- PLACE OF ENCOUNTER ------------------------------
Sky Fortress Bahamut / Cannon Superstructure; Save 09, BEMC.
------------------------------ GET READY! FIGHT! ------------------- party lv99
How can he fly with all that crap on his back? For the equipment have the
following: Rubber Suit, White Mask, Bubble Belt (he doesn't inflict any status
changes), Flame Shield, Ice Shield, Ensanguined Shield. Boss fight is divided
into five stages and I will do my best to guide you thru all of them. Since he
has Dispelga, I wouldn't bother with too many buffs unless you wield equipment
that grants you such statuses.
STAGE 1, 100% > HP > 80% - Battle begins! Boss will pelt you mainly with Divine
Sword and regular physical attack, with lv3 magics mixed in. Take care to
switch equipment in time to reduce or null the damage - Dispel his Haste as
well. Have Curaja or Renew gambit set with HP < 60% just in case, and begin
bashing into Undying's HP reserves.
STAGE 2, 80% > HP > 60% - Congrats, you've knocked off 20% of its HP. Battle
heats up with Megaflare, so equip shields with high EVA and you may block the
attack. Next Megaflare is incoming after 12 commands, and the rest of attacks
are still the same as 1st stage.
STAGE 3, 60% > HP > 40% - Here's where things will start to heat up. Boss will
use Chain Magick (begin casting Dispel!), follow with Faith (hope that your
Dispel removes it in time), then Magick Barrier and finish it up with Ascension
- like with Megaflare, equip shields with high EVA and you may block the
attack. Boss loses Divine Sword and will now start a spamathon of Piercing
menagerie. This is the time to equip White Mask, Rubber Suit, Flame Shield or
Ice Shield (depends on what he'll throw at you). Physicals are NOT used, so DEF
is unimportant at the moment. Ascension and Megaflare will be coming like this
- Ascension, 12 commands, Megaflare, 20 commands, Ascension, repeat. Take care
to equip high EVA shields for these attacks. While you're being showered with
magic attacks, bash away next 20% of Undying's HP.
STAGE 4, 40% > HP > 20% - You're almost there! This stage begins with Enrage,
then Bravery (Dispel it!), Force Barrier and Gigaflare Sword (high EVA shield).
Megaflare is no longer used, but Gigaflare and Ascension will be switching
places after each 52 commands (with 26 commands pause between them). No magic
is cast during this stage, so up your DEF and buff yourself up. Either cast
magic at Undying or wait two minutes for Paling to dissipate and then round him
up into critical HP.
STAGE 5, HP < 20% - The final stage! Perfect Defense is immediately used, and
you get bombed with Gigaflare Sword (last time it is used). Boss continues the
assault with mix of physicals and magic attacks (remember to equip accordingly)
- beware or Gigaflare after next 8 commands. With good shields you can block
even this attack for no damage at all. Gigaflare is used again after next 32
commands, but by then Undying will long be history in the making.
-------------------- CONGRATULATIONS! YOU ARE VICTORIOUS! ---------------------

You've beaten the game. Congratulations! Sit back and enjoy the ending.

-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-
WEAPON DAMAGE FORMULAE
-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-

a) When 'Unarmed':
   <DMG = [11 x RND(1~1.125) - DEF] x STR x (LV+STR)/256>

   When 'Unarmed' with Brawler license learned:
   <DMG = [(LV+STR)/2 x RND(1~1.125) - DEF] x [STR x (LV+STR)/256>\
\
b) When armed with 1Hsword, 2Hsword, spear, bowgun or rod:\
   <DMG = [(ATT x RND(1~1.125) - DEF] x [1 + STR x (LV+STR)/256]>\
   - exceptions are Healing Rod and Rod of Faith\
\
c) When armed with pole:\
   <DMG = [(ATT x RND(1~1.125) - MDEF] x [1 + STR x (LV+STR)/256]>\
\
d) When armed with mace:\
   <DMG = [(ATT x RND(1~1.125) - DEF] x [1 + MAG x (LV+MAG)/256]>\
\
e) When armed with katana or staff:\
   <DMG = [(ATT x RND(1~1.125) - DEF] x [1 + STR x (LV+MAG)/256]>\
\
f) When armed with axe, hammer or hand-bomb:\
   <DMG = [(ATT x RND(0~1.111) - DEF] x [1 + STR x (LV+VIT)/128]>\
\
g) When armed with dagger, ninja sword or bow:\
   <DMG = [(ATT x RND(1~1.125)] - DEF] x [1 + STR x (LV+SPD)/218]>

h) When armed with gun, measure, Healing Rod or Rod of Faith:
   <DMG = [(ATT x RND(1~1.125)]^2>

-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-
COMBINATION HITS & CRITICAL HITS
-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-

a) Weapons that can combo are:
   Unarmed, 1Hsword, 2Hsword, spear, pole, mace, katana, axe, hammer, dagger,
   ninja sword.

b) Weapons that can score critical hits are:
   Bowgun, bow, gun, measure.

c) Weapons that cannot combo or score criticals are:
   Rod, staff, handbomb.

d) Chart showing combo probability:

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Hit # | HP > 25% | 25%< HP <12,5% | 6,25%< HP <12,5% |  HP < 6,25%
------|----------|----------------|------------------|-------------------------
 2    | 40.0%    | 14.7%          |  1.4%            |    0%
 3    | 38.2%    | 30.8%          |  7.5%            |    0%
 4    | 16.6%    | 29.3%          | 17.5%            |  0.2%
 5    |  4.3%    | 16.7%          | 24.7%            |  1.2%
 6    |  0.8%    |  6.4%          | 23.3%            |  4.3%
------|----------|----------------|------------------|-------------------------
 7    |    0%    |  1.7%          | 15.3%            | 10.8%
 8    |    0%    |  0.3%          |  7.2%            | 19.2%
 9    |    0%    |    0%          |  2.4%            | 24.4%
 10   |    0%    |    0%          |  0.6%            | 21.7%
 11   |    0%    |    0%          |    0%            | 12.8%
------|----------|----------------|------------------|-------------------------
 12   |    0%    |    0%          |    0%            |  5.3%
------|----------|----------------|------------------|-------------------------
Av.hit| 2.873    | 3.752          | 5.509            | 9.028
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
So basically you have more chances to start comboing like crazy if your HP is
low. This also explains why you see enemies combo your chrs whole lot more when
in critical condition.

e) When Genji Gloves accessory is equipped, weapon's chances (in %) for
comboing is multiplied by (1,8). Without Genji Gloves the multiplicator becomes
(0,7). Weapon's comboing chances will be added to Equipment section.

f) Enemies can combo when doing regular attacks, but what you may not have
known is that they can also combo some of their skill attacks. The difference
is that you will not see any 'hit' indicator coming up, and the enemy can keep
doing it up to its maximum capacity. So for example, if you have an enemy that
can combo a regular attack of up to 6hits with 20% chance, this enemy also has
20% chance to hit you up to six times with the skill attack. These are:
- Gnaw
- Kick
- Rush
- Ram
- Lunge
- Poke
- Divine Sword
- Rake
- Slap

-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-
QUICKENING
-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-=-

a) Each chr can learn up to three Quickenings by acquiring respective licenses
on License Board. Once a Quickening slot is acquired, it disappears from other
chrs' License Boards.

-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    ASHE                     | FRAN                    | PENELO
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1 | Northswain's Glow        | Feral Strike            | Intercession
2 | Heaven's Wrath           | Whip Kick               | Evanescence
3 | Maelstrom's Bolt         | Shatterheart            | Resplendence
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    VAAN                     | BALTHIER                | BASCH
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
1 | Red Spiral               | Fires of War            | Fulminating Darkness
2 | White Whorl              | Tides of Fate           | Ruin Impendent
3 | Pyroclasm                | Element of Treachery    | Flame Purge
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------

b) Level 1 Quickening requires 1 Mist Charge.
   Level 2 Quickening requires 2 Mist Charges.
   Level 3 Quickening requires 3 Mist Charges.

c) While you are doing first hit, you will always have 4 secs on game clock.
The amount of time you spend inputing the command is halved, and this time is
added to remaining time left, and so on.

Example:
- You have 4 secs on timer, and need 1 second to make an input.
- Remaining time left is 3 seconds.
- Game halves that second, which makes 0,5 second left.
- 0,5 second gets added to remaining time left.
- You now have 3,5 secs on timer to make your next command.

d) If chr has at least one mist bar expended, he or she may get the option for
'Mist Charge' to appear when you press R2 button to shuffle between possible
command inputs. The chance is based on amount of chrs in your active party.

- if solo  : 1/6
- if 2 chrs: 1/7
- if 3 chrs: 1/8

e) All Quickies deal *physical* damage.

f) When Quickening command is chosen, its CT is zero (0).

g) Quickie's level dictates its attack power (POW).
   Lv1 Quickie: 90 POW
   Lv2 Quickie: 140 POW
   Lv3 Quickie: 230 POW

h) Damage formula for Quickie is:
   <DMG = RND(1~POW) x RND(1~STR)>

i) Concurrences are attacks that occur if enough Quickies has been performed
beforehand. They are as follows:
- Black Hole  : 253 POW
- Luminescence: 251 POW
- Ark Blast   : 205 POW
- Whiteout    : 175 POW
- Windburst   : 155 POW
- Torrent     : 130 POW
- Cataclysm   : 110 POW
- Inferno     : 90  POW

j) Concurrence only happens if you perform say enough lv1 Quickies. Amount
needed is as follows:
- Black Hole  : 4x lv1, 4x lv2, 4x lv3
- Luminescence: 3x lv1, 3x lv2, 3x lv3
- Ark Blast   : 2x lv1, 2x lv2, 2x lv3
- White Out   : 5x lv3
- Windburst   : 5x lv2
- Torrent     : 2x lv1, 3x lv2
- Cataclysm   : 7x lv1
- Inferno     : 3x lv1

l) Damage formula for Concurrence is:
   <DMG = POW x Lv(enemy)>
