29. Map of Rabanastre Palace
    - if you forget to get the map from urn in [Royal Palace / Cellar Stores],
      you can buy it from Cartographers' moogle in NE corner of [Old Archades /\
      Alley of Low Whispers] for 100000 gil

30. Ktjn's sidequest
    - depending on amount of points you score when answering her questions she
      can be found in seven different parts of Rabanastre
      #1 inside Clan Hall (+4 pts)
      #2 in front of entrance to Clan Hall (+3 pts)
      #3 various parts of Rabanastre (pts range from -2 to +2)*3
         - one of dead ends in [Muthru Bazaar]
         - in front of aerodrome
         - near the entrance to Yamoora's Gambits
         - W part of [East End], close to [Muthru Bazaar]
      #4 inside Migelo's Sundries (-3 pts)
      #5 in fronto of Migelo's Sundries (-4 pts)
    - it would take a lot of patience and replays to get all of those scenes,
      so don't ask me what she says in them
    - additionally, if you get her to stand in front of Clan Hall, you're able
      to talk to her directly; don't get inside Clan Hall until after
      plastering boss of Mt Bur-Omisace and finishing Ktjn's quest, and the
      lines you usually hear from 'Conspicuous Bangaa' will be said by Ktjn
    - credit: Brady's guide

31. Getting back in Rabanastre during Rogue Tomato hunt
    - if for whatever reason you need to go back in Rabanastre before killing
      Rogue Tomato, stand in either of the two lines by talking to the 'Queue
      Watch'; wait patiently until the line clears and when asked if you want
      to enter, say yes

32. Scenes in boss battles on top of Pharos and Bahamut
    - while fighting Judge Master G. and if Basch is in your party, the boss
      will use scene A (applies for both battles)
    - while fighting Judge Master G. and if Basch is not in your party, the
      boss will use scene B (applies for both battles)

33. Jinn in Rabanastre
    - when the storyline unfolds far enough that Giza Plains gets the Rain,
      seek out Jinn in [Rabanastre / Southern Plaza]
    - he can be found pacing near the fountain
    - no longer to be found here after weather rotation starts
    - credit: Brady's guide

34. Travelers in Giza Plains
    - when the storyline unfolds far enough that Giza Plains gets the Rain,
      go to [Giza Plains / Nomad Village]
    - you'll find a couple of travelers close to SCR
    - no longer to be found here after weather rotation starts
    - credit: Brady's guide

35. Sadeen's end
    - after returning Ring of the Toad to nomad's elder, return to [Giza Plains\
      / Nomad Village] during the Rains and talk to Sadeen to give him the rest
      he seeks

36. Deathgaze's attack
    - while you're doing Deathgaze hunt and it finally shows up on the airship
      you're taking, don't charge into the battle just yet
    - take your time and talk to people to see their scared reactions
    - also take the chance to seek shelter in your cabin
    - there's seven possible scenarios, depending on which skyferry is attacked

37. Airship conversations
    - there's seven possible scenarios, depending on which skyferry you took
      via 'leisure craft'
    - take your time and talk to people to see their reactions
    - some people's lines change after you've taken specific skyferry more
      times

38. Traveler's family blah-blah
    - the family of the same kid who's petitioner for Deathgaze hunt will have
      different convos depending on where you are storywise
    - to get the conversation, just talk to them inside aerodromes
      #1 after Barheim Passage ordeals
      #2 after nabbing Dawn Shard (3 different scenes)
      #3 after plastering boss of Mt Bur-Omisace
    - credit: Brady's guide

39. Is Dyce dycing with Vaan?
    - when story takes you to the Tomb of Raithwall, always ignore Dyce on all
      accounts when you meet him, or talk to him at least once
    - when you meet him for the final time in Balfonheim, and if you always
      ignored him, he will use response A
    - when you meet him for the final time in Balfonheim, and if you talked to
      him at least once on previous occassion, he will use response B
    - credit: Brady's guide

40. Tetran's demise?
    - first time you meet Tetran is on Leviathan; you can decide to open the
      cell he's trapped in and talk to him or ignore him totally
    - if you didn't talk to Tetran, then he uses response A when you get to
      Eruyt Village
    - if you did talk to Tetran, then he uses response B when you get to Eruyt
      Eruyt
    - credit: Brady's guide

41. Victory celebrations
    - sometimes when you defeat a particularly difficult foe, a message showing
      "Congratulations" will appear on screen
    - meanwhile your chrs may perform victory celebrations with whatever weapon
      they were holding at the time that foe was defeated
    - same class of weapon will have same victory celebration, ie Tournesol's
      dance will be the same as Save the Queen's
    - if you always use same characters with same weapons, and you've already
      killed all foes that have "Congratulations" screen, then you will have
      missed out on victory celebrations of other chrs using different weapns

42. Teleport Stone woes
    - warp to Archades via GCR and talk to 'Prideful Boy' in [Archades /\
      Tsenoble] nearby to get chewed out for using warping

43. "Getting chewed" scenes
    - during battle with Air Cutter Remora, turn around and try to run away to
      [Nalbina Fortress / Aerial Gardens]
    - after Migelo asks you to find Kytes, take a detour to [Rabanastre /\
      Southern Plaza]
    - after Masyua in [Giza Plains / Nomad Village] tells you to find Jinn for
      her, exit the village towards N
    - while doing storyline events in Archades and Bal asks Vaan to collect
      Pinewood Chops, turn around and return to Old Archades
    - when you enter Lhusu Mines (storyline events) with Lamont as guest chr,
      turn around and return to Bhujerba immediately
    - credit: Brady's guide (first four entries)
    - credit: joetex72 (fifth entry)

44. Party-leader-affects-scenes
    #1 [Garamsythe Waterway / East Spur Stairs]
       - when Fran and Balthier join your party for the first time and after
         you're given the tutorial on gambits, examine 'Fallen Soldiers' nearby
         for a minor scene
       - scene varies depending on who the current leader is (3 total)
       - credit: KADFC
    #2 [Phon Coast / Rava's Pass]
       - talk to 'Viera Wayfarer' with Fran as leader, then switch to different
         leader (2 different scenes in total)
       - credit: Brady's guide
    #3 [Giza Plains / Crystal Glade] (during the Dry)
       - talk to 'Viera Wayfarer' with Fran as leader, then switch to different
         leader (2 different scenes in total)
       - she's gone after plastering Gil Snapper
       - credit: Brady's guide
    #4 [Henne Mines / Pithead Junction A]
       - talk to 'Wounded Imperial' with Fran as leader, then switch to
         different leader (2 different scenes in total)
       - he is gone after defeating Tiamat
       - credit: Brady's guide

45. Supinelu sucks
    - when you're going thru Ozmone Plain looking for Jahara, you'll eventually
      run into a garif picking on a chocobo
    - if this garif doesn't die by the time you reach Jahara, Supinelu will use
      scene A
    - if this garif croaks by the time you reach Jahara, Supinelu will use
      scene B

46. Gurdy's inquiry
    - if by the time you're to leave Jahara for Eruyt Village you've never
      ridden chocos, decline the free offer Supinelu made as well
    - when you reach [Mt Bur-Omisace / Temple Grounds], Gurdy will ask you why
      do you keep avoiding chocobos
    - credit: Brady's guide

47. Dalan's advice
    - depending on your point in storyline, Dalan may have some advice for you
    #1  after coming back to Rabanastre from Rogue Tomato hunt
    #2  after getting Sunstone
    #3  after Barheim Passage ordeals
    #4  after Sword of the Order is given to Azelas
    #5  after Bal and Fran join in Rabanastre's Sandsea
    #6  after escaping from Leviathan
    #7  after nabbing Dawn Shard
    #8  after Larsa joins in Jahara
    #9  after getting to Mt Bur-Omisace
    #10 after plastering boss in Mt Bur-Omisace
    #11 after Draklor Laboratory
    #12 after nabbing Treaty-Blade
    #13 after appearance of Bahamut
    - credit: Brady's guide

48. "The Stories Kid"
    - depending on your point in storyline, the kid's story will evolve
    - he's found in [Rabanastre / East End]
    #1 after you have control of Vaan for first time
    #2 after coming back to Rabanastre from Rogue Tomato hunt
    #3 after Barheim Passage ordeals
    #4 after nabbing Dawn Shard
    #5 after Draklor Laboratory
    - credit: Brady's guide

49. Migelo's worries
    - after you gain all party members permanently, go talk to Migelo
    - there's two different scenes
    #1 if you have obtained Dawn Shard
    #2 if you don't have Dawn Shard yet
    - credit: Brady's guide

50. Ba'Gamnan scene in Lhusu Mines
    - when doing storyline battle against Ba'Gamnan and his sidekicks, defeat
      all of them to see a scene where Ba'Gamnan runs away (scene A)
    - if you run away from him and make it all the way to [Lhusu Mines / Shaft\
      Entry], you will get scene B
    - credit: MrHangman

51. Missable chocobo scenes
    #1 Scene A (after plastering boss of Mt Bur-Omisace)
       - take a chocobo from Mosphoran Highwaste and ride it all the way to
         [Phon Coast / Pora-Pora Sands]
       - along N edge of the area you can find choco tracks, but 'Game Hunter'
         will not permit you to pass until you get to [Hunters' Camp]
    #2 Scene B (after seeing storyline events in [Phon Coast / Hunters' Camp])
       - take a chocobo and ride it towards Tchita Uplands
       - in Tchita Uplands go all the way E until you end up in [Tchita Uplands\
         / The Shaded Path]
       - try to climb the slope between two small rocks, ignore bangaa 'Game
         Hunter's warning, and press on to be able to enter Cerobi Steppe
    #3 Scene C (after seeing storyline events in [Phon Coast / Hunters' Camp])
       - complete directions given for scene B
       - in Cerobi Steppe make it all the way SE until you enter Balfonheim
       - in [Balfonheim Port / Sea Breeze Lane] you can talk to few people (you
         cannot enter other areas of Balfonheim yet)
       - simply use Gate Crystal to return to [Phon Coast / Hunters' Camp]
     - credit: KADFC

52. Missable scene in front of Barheim Passage
    - before you depart for Rabanastre Palace dungeon, go to [Dalmasca\
      Estersand / Passage Entrance]
    - get close to Shifty Seeq and Bumbly Seeq to trigger a short scene
    - scene is missed after escaping from Barheim Passage
    - credit: silentexistence

53. Missable scene when entering Nalbina Town from Mosphoran Highwaste before
    defeating Judge Master B. in Mt Bur-Omisace
    - you must do this before you help July
    - enter Nalbina from Mosphoran Highwaste and the two guards (Gibbs and
      Deweg) will ask you how did you manage to survive in there, and just how
      the heck did you enter it
    - you're offered two choices when answering the question
    - credit: B. B.

54. 6 different scenes before acquiring Matamune in Barheim Passage (you need
    to obtain Barheim Key and must defeat Gilgamesh in both battles)
    - after you solve the misteries of the five bottles you caught when
      fishing, make way to [Barheim Passage / The Zeviah Span]
    - you need to enter small portion which is only accessible from [Barheim\
      Passage / West Annex]
    - when you enter the room, a small scene plays, and depending on who your
      onscreen chr is, they vary slightly
    - credit: flak76e

55. Missable scene when fighting Zalera in Barheim Passage
    - after you get Barheim Key, make your way to Zalera
    - during battle you're given 5 minutes time limit in which you have to
      defeat the esper
    - wait for time limit to expire and you'll be thrust out of battle back
      into [Barheim Passage / Terminus No. 7 Adjunct]
    - you'll witness a scene
    - the chance to see this scene expires if you defeat Zalera
    - credit: Liu Domi

56. Missable Fran/Balthier scene after Barheim Passage
    - after you escape from Barheim Passage and return to Rabanastre, your
      party disbands
    - go to tavern Sandsea and ascend the stairs to find Balthier and Fran
    - a short scene will follow
    - the chance to see this scene expires after you deliver Sword of the Order
    - credit: Bx.C

57. Missable scene at start of game after killing the three rats
    - when Vaan and Kytes walk out of Garamsythe Waterway, head towards Muthru
      Bazaar
    - you must do this before talking to Migelo
    - Vaan will comment about 'making himself scarce' in relation to the
      Imperial he stole money from

58. Missable scene with Judges in Jahara
    - if you return to Jahara after visiting Eruyt Village for the first time
      and talking to Jote, you will find Judge Hausen near Supinelu in [Jahara\
      / Lull of the Land]
    - talk to him and he gives you 3x Hi-Potion and Ether
    - the chance to see this scene expires after completing Henne Mines
      storyline events
    - credit: Jason P.

59. Missable scene with Earth Tyrant quest
    - enter [Dalmasca Westersand / Wyrm's Nest] before starting the quest
    - the chance to see this scene expires after you collect the Wind Globe
    - credit: flak76e

60. Draklor Laboratory scenes
    - when you first enter it on 66th floor and walk to the west, there is a
      small scene where the camera shows the dead Imperials
    - scene is different depending who your party leader is
    - 6 possible scenes in total
    - credit: Bjarne B.

61. And some explanation of notes for the end
    *1 If you do NOT wear Diamond Armlet, Circlet is yours.
       If you wear Diamond Armlet, you may obtain Ring of Renewal instead.
       To ensure getting Circlet, do NOT wear Diamond Armlet.
    *2 If you wear Diamond Armlet, you will obtain Knot of Rust.
       To ensure getting Circlet, do NOT wear Diamond Armlet.
    *3 Exit Rabanastre and come back for Ktjn to pop up in one of these four
       spots. Exit Rabanastre and come back and her position may change to one
       of other three spots.

41.)                           BESTIARY - G4100
===============================================================================
===============================================================================

This will be the biggest section of the guide - in here you can find info on
all 448 foes that a player can encounter while playing FFXII. This is just a
random piece of trivia - I was quite surprised to find out that the foe with
highest EVA in the game is... Flowering Cactoid with 40 EVA. Heh!

Major credit to FFXII Battle Ultimania.

Now comes the explanation of various entries for a sample foe.
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------
#01 First it's the number of the foe (in Clan Primer), followed by its name.
    Some foe entries have more subdivisions, like for example Cactoid and
    Cactite. In such cases all of them go under same entry.
    - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
#02 "G:" stands for foe's "Genus"
    "C:" stands for foe's "Classification"
    "D:" stands for foe's "Derivation" - valid only for (Trophy) Rare Game!
    "R:" stands for foe's "Rarity" - valid only for (Trophy) Rare Game!
    - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
#03 "Non-aggro"  foe is a foe that originally does not attack your chrs unless
                 it is provoked in some way (like using an offensive action
                 against it, or casting magic in foe's vicinity)
    "Aggressive" foe is a foe that will start attacking your chrs once one of
                 them comes close to the foe
    - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
#04 "Flying: no"  designates a foe that can be hit with all types of weapons
    "Flying: yes" designates a foe that can be hit with ranged weapons only
    Note: Magic works against both types of foes, while some techs only work on
    flying foes, some on ground foes, and some on both types.
    - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
#05 "Movement: GR" designates a foe that moves over ground on its own feet
    "Movement: FL" designates a foe that moves over ground by floating
    "Movement: FY" designates a foe that moves over ground by flying (take
                   caution that not all foes of this type have "Flying: yes")
    "Movement: TE" designates a foe that can move over ground by teleporting
    - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
#06 "V" stands for "Version" of the foe. Some foes can be encountered in
    multiple locations - even though it is the same foe, their stats may not be
    the same. In such cases multiple entries are made to distinguish between
    versions. "Version" of the foe always starts with "a" and then continues.
    Whenever you see letters in parenthesis during the "Items", "Passive
    Abilities" and "Attack list" part of an entry, it means that it belongs to
    that version of the foe.
    - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
#07 "LVL"     stands for "Level" of the foe
    "HP"      stands for "Hit Points" of the foe
    "MP"      stands for "Mist Points" of the foe
    "STR"     stands for "Strength" of the foe
    "MAG"     stands for "Magic Power" of the foe
    "VIT"     stands for "Vitality" of the foe
    "SPD"     stands for "Speed" of the foe
    "ATT"     stands for "Attack Power" of the foe
    "DEF"     stands for "Defense" of the foe
    "MDEF"    stands for "Magic Defense" of the foe
    "EVA"     stands for "Evasion" of the foe
    "EXP.PTS" stands for "Experience Points" of the foe
    "LP"      stands for "License Points" of the foe
    "CPT"     stands for "Clan Points" of the foe
    "GIL"     stands for "Gil" of the foe
    - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
#08 "Element bonus: ---" means that a foe is infused with the power of this
    particular element. If foe possesses skills of this element type, they will
    be 50% more powerful.
    - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
#09 "Elemental Affinities" deal with foe's vulnerabilities to the 8 elements.
    "weak"    means that foe takes double damage from this element
    "-"       means that foe takes regular damage from this element
    "halves"  means that foe halves damage from this element
    "immune"  means that foe is immune to damage from this element
    "absorbs" means that foe absorbs damage from this element as HP recovery
    - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
#10 "Status Affinities" deal with foe's vulnerabilities to status changes.
    "DEA" - Death        | "PET" - Petrify         | "STP" - Stop
    "DOO" - Doom         | "CON" - Confuse         | "SLE" - Sleep
    "DIE" - Disease      | "REV" - Reverse         | "SLO" - Slow
    "DIA" - Disable      | "IMM" - Immobilize      | "SIL" - Silence
    "BLI" - Blind        | "POI" - Poison          | "OIL" - Oil
    "SAP" - Sap          | "LUR" - Lure            | "REF" - Reflect
    "PRO" - Protect      | "SHL" - Shell           | "HAS" - Haste
```

```
    "BRA" - Bravery      | "FAI" - Faith           | "INV" - Invisible
    "REG" - Regen        | "BER" - Berserk         | "WAR" - Warp
    "POA" - Poach        | "%DM" - fractional dmg  | "SIG" - Sight Unseeing
    "REN" - Renew        | "SYP" - Syphon          | "NUM" - Numerology
    "CHA" - Charm        | "ACH" - Achilles        | "WIT" - Wither
    "ADD" - Addle        | "SHR" - Shear           | "EXP" - Expose
    "yes" means that foe is susceptible
    "imm" means that foe is immune and cannot be affected
    - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
#11 "Begins Battle with Status" deals with foe's possible status changes when
    your chrs run into it.
    "100%" means that foe will always be under listed status changes
    "50%"  means that foe may or may not be under listed status changes
    - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
#12 "Passive Abilities" deal with foe's pass-ables.
    "Start" means that foe begins the battle with pass-able/s
    "Gain"  means that foe gains pass-able/s in some way during battle
    "Lose"  means that foe loses pass-able/s in some way during battle
    - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
#13 "Target Preference" deals with foe's preferred method of choosing the
     victim and then starting to assault it.
    - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
#14 "Notes" will tell you interesting info about the foe in question or go into
    further details if something isn't very clear from the info provided.
    - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
#15 "Items" deals with all the items you can acquire from the foe.
    - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
#16 "DROP" has five categories*1
    "a -"  means "always", drops with 100% chance when foe is KOed
    "c -"  means "common", drops with 40% chance when foe is KOed
    "u -"  means "uncommon", drops with 25% chance when foe is KOed
    "r -"  means "rare", drops with 3% chance when foe is KOed
    "vr -" means "very rare", drops with 1% chance when foe is KOed

    Not all foes have all five categories of items, and they may not even have
    any items for dropping. In such cases categories are omitted, or word
    "none" will be there to let you know that you shouldn't bother with it.
    - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
#17 "STEAL" has three categories*2
    "c -" means "common", can be stolen with 55% chance
    "u -" means "uncommon", can be stolen with 10% chance
    "r -" means "rare", can be stolen with 3% chance

    Not all foes have all three categories of items, and they may not even have
    any items for stealing. In such cases categories are omitted, or word
    "none" will be there to let you know that you shouldn't bother with it.
    - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
#18 "POACH" has two categories*3
    "c -" means "common", can be poached with 95% chance
    "r -" means "rare", can be poached with 5% chance

    Not all foes can be poached, and some foes have same item in both "common"
    and "rare" category. If foe cannot be poached, word "none" will be there to
    let you know that you shouldn't bother with it.
    - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
#19 "SP.IT" means "Special Item" and has three categories*4
    "mn -" means "Monograph", drops with specific % when foe is KOed, provided
           you have the corresponding Monograph in your inventory
    "cj -" means "Canopic Jar", drops with specific % when foe is KOed,
           provided you have the Canopic Jar in your inventory
    "ki -" means "Key Item", always drops when foe is KOed

    Not all foes have items from "Special Item" categories. In such cases
    categories are omitted, or word "none" will be there to let you know that
    you shouldn't bother with it.
    - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
#20 "Attack List" will tell you all skills that the foe can use in some way.
    "a"  - means that skill is used with 100% chance when/if specific
           conditions are met (like foe losing 50% of HP)
    "c"  - means that skill is used with 50% chance
    "u"  - means that skill is used with 25% chance
    "r"  - means that skill is used with 5% chance
    "1x" - means that skill is used only once per listed variable/s
    - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
#21 "Place of Encounter" will tell you all places where you can find this foe.
    - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
#22 "Spawn Conditions" will tell you what requirements must be met to encounter
    this foe. This entry will not be listed under all foes, only those that
    require some extra touch to lure out. Subject to change.
    - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
#23 *1 Battle Chain will improve the chances of loot being dropped when foe is
       killed, based on below chart ("always" category is *not* affected by
       battle chain).
       |------------------------------------------|
       | Cat / lv  |  Lv0  |  Lv1  |  Lv2  |  Lv3 |
       |------------------------------------------|
       | Common    |  40%  |  45%  |  50%  |  55% |
       |------------------------------------------|
       | Uncommon  |  25%  |  30%  |  35%  |  40% |
       |------------------------------------------|
       | Rare      |   3%  |   6%  |   8%  |  12% |
       |------------------------------------------|
       | Very rare |   1%  |   2%  |   3%  |   5% |
       |------------------------------------------|

    *2 Chr can improve stealing chances by wearing Thief's Cuffs (see below).
       Additionally, chr can now succeed in stealing up to three (3) items at
       once (normally you can only steal one and then foe doesn't have anything
       else).
       - Stealing common item's chances rise from 55% to 80%
       - Stealing uncommon item's chances rise from 10% to 30%
       - Stealing rare item's chances rise from 3% to 6%
       Once you successfully steal from the foe, you must zone at least two
       screens away for the foe's item "store" to be refreshed. Exceptions are
       non-aggro foes and marks - once you steal from them, you can go to
       neighboring zone and come back immediately for refreshed item "store".
       And you can steal multiple times from the same foe under special
       conditions (for example Gilgamesh), but there is only a handful of such
       foes.

    *3 First of all, poached items are not connected to battle chain in any
       way. If foe is poachable, you get either common or rare item and that's
       it. To successfully poach a foe, it must be in critical condition (HP is
       lower than 20% MAX HP, and foe is flashing red). Beware - poached foe
       doesn't drop any EXP, LP, loot, CPT or gil.

    *4 This category of items is also not connected to battle chain in any way.
       Not including "Key Items" category, you must possess eight Key Items if
       you want to get drops from "mn -" and "cj -" categories. They are:
       - Mage's Monograph for Fiend type foes
       - Scholar's Monograph for Construct type foes
       - Knight's Monograph for Giant and Insect type foes
       - Sage's Monograph for Elemental type foes
       - Warmage's Monograph for Amorph and Undead type foes
       - Dragoon's Monograph for Dragon and Plant type foes
       - Hunter's Monograph for Beast Avion type foes
       - Canopic Jar causes all of the above types to drop Arcana / High Arcana
       All items obtained from "mn -" and "cj -" categories have fixed % at
       which they are dropped and there is no way to improve it except by being
       persistent about it.
       Note: "Ichthian" Genus is considered a Fiend type.
    - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
#24 Some of the enemies have different battle mechanics between the two
    versions (Japanese and US). I have found some of them, but I bet there is
    probably more of them - if you happen to come across them, let me know
    about it.

Gazer spawns near her position; be aware that spawned Gazer can be under
Invisible status if Ashe is hunting for it in [Shunia Twinspan] or [Site 3].
Once you kill a Gazer, you must leave Lhusu Mines and then come back to hunt
another one.

------------------------------ SPAWN CONDITIONS -------------------------------
Lv99 Red Chocobo can be encountered under following conditions:
- Ashe has obtained Treaty Blade
- after entering Ozmone Plain, Ashe has killed 6+ chocobos
- when Ashe comes back to [Haulo Green] from zoning two areas away, she has
  0,4% chance of finding Lv99 Red Chocobo among other chocobos
- do the following trick: when you enter [Haulo Green], kill six chocobos, go
  away two screens and come back into [Haulo Green]. Chocobos have respawned,
  but now you do the following...Petrify all chocobos you find and let the
  counter run out so they turn to Stone - keep walking between the two places
  chocos appear at in [Haulo Green] and they will keep respawning *without you
  needing to zone two areas away for a respawn*; eventually you'll be lucky
  enough to get Lv99 bird to pop

43.)                      VERSION DIFFERENCES - G4300
===============================================================================
===============================================================================

Here you will find a list of small and big differences between Japanese and US
version of FFXII. It will be incomplete at best, but you can help me out by
sending in your contributions.

001 - NTSC-J   - Symbol for Shell status is a shell.
      NTSC-U/C - Symbol for Shell status is a green blob.

002 - NTSC-J   - Some scenes that have only the subtitles...
      NTSC-U/C - ...are instead shown as scenes with spoken dialogue along with
                 subtitles. Example is scene where Vaan exits Rabanastre in
                 search of Rogue Tomato.

003 - NTSC-J   - When there are scripted events happening in major battles,
                 some are shown in full screen with spoken dialogue. You can
                 also see your chrs' gauges in lower right of screen.
      NTSC-U/C - When there are scripted events happening in major battles,
                 they are shown as scenes with spoken dialogue along with
                 subtitles. Example is battle against Doctor C. once you defeat
                 one of his Rooks.

004 - NTSC-J   - Some regular and boss foes use skills...
      NTSC-U/C - ...which are nowhere to be found in this version. This
                 essentially means that you are looking at same foe, but with
                 different skills.

005 - NTSC-J   - If you are in main menu and are trying to examine what magics
                 and techs your chrs have learned, you will find them on two
                 pages. First has a list of all magics, and second has a list
                 of techs, Quickies and espers.
      NTSC-U/C - If you are in main menu and are trying to examine what magics
                 and techs your chrs have learned, you will find them on three
                 pages. First has a list of white and black magics, second has
                 a list of time, green and arcane magics, and third has a list
                 of techs, Quickies and espers.

006 - NTSC-J   - Difficulty of Clan hunt marks you need to track down and kill
                 is expressed as E, D, C, B, A, S, H and X, with E being
                 easiest marks and X being the hardest marks.
      NTSC-U/C - Difficulty of Clan hunt marks you need to track down and kill
                 is expressed as: I, II, III, IV, V, VI, VII and VIII, with (I)
                 being easiest marks and (VIII) being the hardest marks. To
                 simplify the matters for me, I have marked them in numbers
                 from 1 to 8, where 1 are the easiest marks and 8 are the
                 hardest mark.

007 - NTSC-J   - When you're in Gambits submenu, the bars cover about 2/3 of
                 the screen and you can see chr's silhouette very clearly.
      NTSC-U/C - When you're in Gambits submenu, the bars cover about entire
                 screen, also covering the chr's silhouette. You can see it
                 (kinda) clearly only if you press Select on all gambit bars to
                 completely reset them.

008 - NTSC-J   - When you hold down R2 to escape, word ESCAPING appears.
      NTSC-U/C - When you hold down R2 to escape, word FLEEING appears.

009 - NTSC-J   - Battle chain takes longer to start. For example, for battle
                 chain to read '2-Chain' you need to kill three enemies of same
                 class.
      NTSC-U/C - Battle chain is quicker to start. For example, for battle
                 chain to read '2-Chain' you need to kill two enemies of same
                 class.

010 - NTSC-J   - Symbol for Lure status is a kanji.
      NTSC-U/C - Symbol for Lure status is a duck.

011 - NTSC-J   - Depending on amount of hits you do in Quickening chain,
                 following words are displayed:
                 3+ hits - COOL!
                 5+ hits - VERY COOL!
                 10+ hits - EXCELLENT!
      NTSC-U/C - Nothing like that appears in US version.

012 - NTSC-J   - Symbols for elements are expressed as colored circles (for
                 example, white circle represents holy element).
      NTSC-U/C - Symbols for elements are expressed as symbols (for example,
                 drop of water represents water element).
